Человечество определяется своим поиском истины. Некоторые ищут эту истину через личную власть, стремясь подчинить себе ближнего. Кто‑то ищет истину в удовольствиях, считая самоудовлетворение величайшим достижением в жизни. Другие стремятся к просветлению через собственные мысли и рассуждения, всю жизнь учатся и никогда не могут прийти к познанию истины — 2 Тимофею 3:7. Ещё некоторые верят, что жизнь служения сама по себе является наградой, поэтому они стараются прославиться через огласку своих актов служения и благотворительности.

Раз за разом в истории коллективная мысль человека поворачивалась к чему‑то, большему, чем он сам. Восходят и гибнут религии, основываются и рушатся империи, развиваются и разваливаются философии.

На этом фоне интеллектуальных колебаний зародилось движение, которое большинство моих читателей узнает, в небольшом гористом регионе земного шара. Цюрих, Швейцария, год 1525 нашей эры — его принято считать датой и местом рождения, но его корни были пущены ровно за 1500 лет до того, в Галилее, где Один преподавал и жил последние ответы на все вопросы человека.

Начала этого более позднего движения хорошо задокументированы. Коротко говоря, его основала небольшая группа разношёрстных учеников, духовенства и простых людей, которые искали истину в её чистейшем виде. Истории о Конраде Гребеле, Феликсе Манце и Георге Блауроке хорошо известны многим из нас. Они стремились отделиться от духовной порочности, которая их окружала, и заложили основы того, что впоследствии стало известно как анабаптистское движение.

Эти трое вскоре попали под присмотр гражданских и духовных властей своего времени, перенеся лишения и страдания за свою веру. Двое из них в конце концов отдали свои жизни за истину, которую так высоко ценили. Феликс Манц был первым анабаптистским мучеником. 5 января 1527 года, не прошло и двух лет после его смелого повторного крещения, его утопили в реке Лиммат, протекавшей через Цюрих. Его последние слова были: «В руки Твои, Боже, предаю дух мой».

Движение анабаптистов пережило этих троих.

Оно распространилось и выросло по Моравии, Нидерландам, Швейцарии и Пфальцу в Германии. Почти через сто лет в цюрихских холмах появился ещё один заметный лидер; это был пожилой фермер. Он был закален в руководстве своим пастырским стадом через взлёты и падения испытаний, с которыми сталкивались верующие того времени. Его имя — Ханс Ландис.

Год был 1613‑й, точнее 26 января. В маленький замок Ваденсвиль на берегу Цюрихского озера съехались пожилой Ханс Ландис вместе с четырнадцатью членами своей общины. Среди них особенно выделялись Галли Фукс, школьный учитель и недавний новообращённый, а также Бахман, кузнец и известный смутьянин, который также недавно обратился. Навстречу им пришли девять церковных и государственных чиновников, включая мэра Цюриха Рудольфа Рхана; его шефа полиции, Конрада Гребеля (возможно, однофамильца первого повторно крестившего почти столетие назад); и многочисленных местных пасторов из цюрихской протестантской церкви. Причина этой встречи заключалась в том, что духовное служение Ханса пользовалось благословением, и его небольшая община быстро росла, вызывая отток прихожан из сельских приходов протестантской церкви. Снижение посещаемости создавало несколько трудностей для совместного церковно‑государственного управления.

Во‑первых, протестантская церковь получала значительные средства от своих прихожан. Поэтому другая церковь, переманивающая и обращающая её членов, рассматривалась не только как духовная угроза, но и как финансовая. Кантоны региона часто враждовали по религиозным мотивам, от ожесточённых споров до полномасштабных военных кампаний. Во‑вторых, отклоняющиеся духовные учения, не совпадавшие с официальной религией правительства, нередко появлялись в периоды гражданских волнений; крестьянские восстания соседних кантонов ещё ясно стояли в памяти местной знати и духовенства. События вроде меннонитов в Мюнстере и их насильственных толкований Писания оставались наглядным предупреждением о религиозном рвении, вышедшем из‑под контроля. Эти восстания произошли в те времена, когда католическая церковь рушилась в этом районе, что давало возможности для укоренения новых, иногда крайних верований. Теперь деяния Ханса и его общины казались чиновникам делом, граничившим с мятежом и предательством.

Эта встреча не была первой стычкой Ханса Ландиса и его общины с местными властями. Почти четыре года назад уже проводилось расследование. В том докладе говорилось, что их места встреч — леса, сараи и даже дом Ханса Ландиса. Однако списка членов не было, так как даже протестантские соседи отказались назвать кого‑либо из анабаптистов. Местное население не только отказывалось сотрудничать в указании членов общины Ханса, но и ходили слухи, что тауферы вели общий фонд под управлением диакона Якоба Исслера, из которого они обеспечивали нужды в своей среде. Для чиновников это выглядело лишь как очередной приём, чтобы склонить бедных общины оставить свою церковь и присоединиться к Хансу и его людям.

Мэр Рхан открыл заседание, обращаясь к собравшимся как к «преподобным, высоким и ученым, благочестивым, благородным, разумным, мудрым, (и) дорогим господам». Затем он обратился к Хансу и братьям, дав им приветствие «почетные, дорогие и добрые друзья», прежде чем напомнить им об их положении, назвав их «подданными». После этих не слишком тонких манёвров он задал им вопрос, попросив объяснить «причины, по которым вы отделились от нашей церкви и … начали отдельную секту». После этого он заверил их, что совет желает быть терпимым, но сепаратисты «не должны злоупотреблять терпением и милостью господ».

В ответ на это вступление Ханс попросил разрешения встать ему и его братьям и обратиться к их «Благородным Господам». Получив разрешение, он встал, поблагодарил мэра за добрые приветственные слова и затем задавал вопросы об их интересе к вероучениям анабаптистов, утверждая, что они не раз слышали о них прежде. Он добавил, что всё их учение — «ни что иное, как то, чему учил Христос и что писали апостолы». Как и прежде, анабаптисты просили лишь позволить им хранить это, поддерживая своё правительство в делах, не касающихся совести. Они также продолжали молиться за правительство и своих руководителей.

Мэр Рхан не принял этот ответ доброжелательно, восприняв его как намёк на то, что он и протестантская церковь не соблюдают заповеди Христа. Услышав это, Ханс попросил разрешения на короткое время вывести свою группу из комнаты. По возвращении был представлен Галли Фукс, который дал перед господами свидетельство о своём духовном пути через протестантскую и католическую церкви, отметив, что хотя обе хорошо проповедуют с кафедры, обе отрицают это учение своим безбожным поведением. Изучив веру и применение анабаптистов, Галли уверовал.

Чиновники отнеслись скептически, заявив, что высказывания Галли «всё ещё не дают причины для вашего отделения». После этой реплики был выведен ещё один новообращённый — кузнец Бахман. Его незамедлительно узнал Конрад Гребель (не тот самый анабаптистский основатель), шеф полиции Цюриха, — как одного из местных хулиганов: «Это правда, ты был безбожен [и] нет никого в округе, с кем у меня было бы больше проблем, чем с тобой».

Свидетельство Бахмана перекликалось со многими мыслями Галли, особенно по вопросам чистоты и отделённости истинной церкви, и закончилось цитатой из Сираха: «Кто суетится в глине, тот испачкается».

Дискуссии продолжались, вспыхивали споры вокруг причастия, примеров поведения церковных лидеров и познания спасения. Когда заседание подошло к концу, Галли Фукс не удержался от последнего замечания: «Если бы вы отдали нам церковь в Хирцеле, … вы бы увидели … у кого была бы большая толпа!» Это вызвало смех в комнате, и Ханс ухватился за последнюю возможность обратиться, моля: «О, дорогие господа, оставьте нас при том, во что мы верим».

После этой мольбы мэр совещался и в конце концов решил отпустить братьев без ареста; при выходе их слышали, как они говорили в согласии: «Мы бы также отдали жизнь, тело, имущество и кровь». Скоро им предстояло исполнить эту решимость.

Прошло пятнадцать месяцев. Ханс был заточён в башне Велленберг в Цюрихе вместе с Галли Фуксом, диаконом Якобом Исслером, Хансом Мейли, Стефаном Цендером и Павлом Дегией (родом из Милана, Италия). Там их держали четырнадцать недель и неоднократно упрашивали, допрашивали и угрожали. Наконец был вынесен приказ, чтобы они покинули кантон Цюрих, но Ханс отказался; на это совет ответил угрозой, которую часто считали хуже смерти. Совет постановил, что из‑за гражданского неповиновения этих людей, а не их верований, их следует приговорить к рабству на галерах и отправить грести на судах Франции в Средиземном море.

Якоб Исслер умолял господ, спрашивая, как они могут так поступить, зная, что тауферы (анабаптисты) не выносят разлуки со своими семьями. Стефан Цендер добавил: «Мы не боялись бы пойти через море и воду, ибо они тоже творение Божие». Несмотря на эти мольбы, совет привёл угрозы в исполнение, приговорив всех шестерых к галерам.

Приговор потряс общину. Ожидаемая продолжительность жизни молодого здорового раба‑гребца составляла не более трёх лет, и эти три года были бы наполнены голодом, непогодой, побоями и изнеможением. Даже в более суровых католических кантонах этот приговор считался тяжким. В более снисходительном протестантском сообществе он вызвал общественный гнев.

Заключённым дали последний шанс покинуть кантон, и трое из них сдались. Но Галли Фукс, Стефан Цендер и Ханс Ландис твёрдо отказались менять своё решение. Их под конвоем повели на запад к французскому посланнику в Солотурне, городке в кантоне Берн. Берн отреагировал так же, как Цюрих, предложив выкуп за освобождение заключённых. Когда это не дало результата, в их камеру в Солотурне тайно подложили напильник. Цепи узников были быстро перерезаны, и они бежали из города, возвращаясь в свои дома. Там жители, всё ещё возмущённые их обращением, отказались выдать их властям.

Весть об их побеге разнеслась и усилилась, и вскоре Ханс принялся крестить новых обращённых и даже совершать несколько браков. Анабаптисты процветали, помогая бедным общины через еду и беспроцентные займы из своего фонда милосердия. Эта обновлённая деятельность разгневала и напугала власти, которые в конце концов решили, что усилия их пожилого лидера нужно нейтрализовать.

Ханса немедленно арестовали по этому решению и снова заключили в Велленберг. Здесь угрозы и увещевания со стороны властей усилились. Если он не отречётся или хотя бы не покинет кантон, ему придётся умереть.

Такие угрозы не поколебали Ханса. Он, напротив, увещевал правителей не грешить в обращении с ним, подтверждая своё намерение, что он «отдал себя Богу» и «готов ожидать того, что Бог допустит прийти на него».

Это смелое стояние Ханса привело к такому же осознанию у властей: им придётся претворить угрозы в действие. Считая Ханса мятежником, они утверждали, что он «хотел быть своим собственным владыкой и господином вопреки почётным властям», и что он проявлял «упорное, мятежное сопротивление злых людей». Несмотря на эти обвинения и угрозы, магистраты понимали, что казнь будет непопулярной. Ханс пользовался уважением местного населения и даже имел связи в Амстердаме, где жила его дочь, замужняя за голландским меннонитом.

Офицер Гребель, протестантское духовенство и прочие много времени проводили в беседах с Хансом в его тюремной камере, но безуспешно. К четвергу, 29 сентября 1614 года, они осознали, что он полностью непоколебим в своей вере, не желая ни отрекаться, ни покидать кантон. Этот доклад, представленный господам, погрузил их в глубокие раздумья. Некоторые предлагали публично отрубить Хансу ухо и изгнать его, другие считали более уместным пожизненное заключение. Вопрос был вынесен на голосование в полдень, и большинство быстро приняло решение. Ханс Ландис должен быть тут же публично обезглавлен.

Услышав приговор, Ханс подумал, что это ещё один улов, чтобы склонить его к отречению. Однако при подходе к известному месту публичного казнения в Цюрихе его лицо побледнело, и руки взметнулись к голове. Тем не менее он быстро успокоился, улыбнулся и просил толпу не плакать, ибо уповал на добрую надежду. Заметив там жену и детей, он попросил их отойти, чтобы его решимость не поколебалась.

Приговор был оглашён; Ханс стоял молча. Ни одного упрёка в отношении его личной морали не прозвучало. Проблемой было его нежелание распустить свою церковь. Он оставался твёрдым, и потому палач Пауль Фолльмар повёл Ханса на место казни. Некоторые наблюдатели утверждали, что Фолльмар отпустил Ханса, будто давая ему шанс на побег. Когда Ханс им не воспользовался, Фолльмар вознёс руки к Богу, прося прощения за то, что закон требовал от него исполнить. Ханс, улыбаясь, простил человека, тогда как разные церковные пасторы увещевали его отречься, но Ханс отвечал, что в них он не видел покаяния.

Дойдя до места казни, Фолльмар дал Хансу возможность свободно выступить, и Ханс кратко сказал: «Не знаю, что ещё мне сказать, кроме того, что желал бы, чтобы все пришли к познанию своих грехов и раскаянию, чтобы они могли быть спасены; этого я желал бы всем».

Затем, в поле видимости того места, где почти столетие назад Феликс Манц отдал свою жизнь, он преклонил колени и склонил голову. Меч сверкнул вниз, и после этого Пауль Фолльмар задал ритуальный вопрос: «Правильно ли я казнил этого человека?»

«Да,» последовал ответ, «ты казнил этого бедного человека».

Немедленный эффект жертвы пожилого Ханса вызвал волну сочувствия и возмущения в неанабаптистском сообществе. Рудольф Рхан и Конрад Гребель продолжали оказывать давление на оставшихся анабаптистов, поместив Маргарету Ландис, вдову Ханса, в одиночное заключение в городской больнице после её отказа подчиниться их требованиям. Дети Ханса также оставались твёрдыми в вере, отказываясь отречься, но несколько его внуков вскоре после казни деда начали посещать городскую церковь.

Местная анабаптистская община также оставалась сильной. Её духовные потомки унесли слово Христа с собой, когда через столетие великая эмиграция высадилась на диких берегах Нового Света. Здесь, в религиозной свободе Пенсильвании, они основали новые общины, где вера, ради которой Ханс Ландис отдал свою жизнь, процветала в последующих поколениях. Сегодня по всей Америке есть верующие, стремящиеся жить по совести, во многом благодаря жизни, которой жил Ханс около 400 лет назад. Кто‑то из них — его потомки, кто‑то — друзья его потомков. Пусть же мы будем вдохновлены идти так, как ходил Иисус, подобно Хансу.

And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full. And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish? And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm. And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith? And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him? Mark 4:37-41

Many times, I have read this passage and wondered what we are to derive from it. It seems to be a story that generates more questions than it solves. We often like to think of Jesus as the relational form of the Godhead; a sort of go-between, between us and the Almighty God. But here, in our scriptural passage, His behavior is almost unthinkable in human terms. How could Christ sleep in such a storm, much less in a boat filling with water? We can believe that He is Master of the wind and seas, and they must bow at His command, but does He expect us to do the same? Would our compassionate Christ expect us to be calm and fearless in such dire straits? Is all exhibition of fear the fruit of our lack of faith? These probing questions are disturbing, for we all would hope that our faith in Him is strong enough to secure our salvation, yet experience has taught us that our own walk through the troublesome pastures of life has produced nothing more noble than the harrowing bleating of the disciples.

Why are ye so fearful? How is it that ye have no faith? The questions seem almost out of place coming from our Saviour, almost as though He is not as patient and longsuffering as we had hoped. But Christ has placed a definitive expectation upon His disciples that is not beyond their attainment. Was He calling on them to rebuke the storm themselves? Should they have awakened Him sooner? Did he expect them to quietly row on in confident assurance? The Scripture here supplies us with few answers, but we do know that there is an abiding lesson here concerning fear and faith.

Storms are a common part of life, and no major dilemma is pleasant. While Paul sailed toward Rome, they experienced a time …when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away –Acts 27:20. In the midst of a cloudy and hopeless situation there is one bell that continues to toll clear and bright: There is a peace that can be apprehended even in the most dreadful circumstances. Paul had spent a precarious …night and a day I have been in the deep –2 Corinthians 11:25, yet he did not demand the wind and sea to submit to his authority. Rather, he states that in the midst of the storm …there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve, Saying, Fear not, Paul… –Acts 27:23-24. This is a scene similar to the peril being endured by the disciples (in our text for today) yet we see a different outcome. Paul was comforted and commended while the disciples received rebuke.

While bobbing about in the clutches of a potential watery grave, the disciples cried out: …Master, carest thou not that we perish? –Mark 4:38. How natural it is for us all to thrust our frustration and blame upon another. To think that some apathetic person is shirking their responsibility is very disheartening. In like fashion …the shipmaster came to him [Jonah], and said unto him, What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not –Jonah 1:6.

There seems to be an edge to the shipmaster’s rebuke very similar to the disciple’s response to the sleeping Jesus. Christ finds no pleasure in allowing trouble to visit us, but there seems to be no other veritable vehicle of grace wherewith His peace can flood our souls. If there first be no valley, how shall we value the mountaintop? If there be no thorns, how shall we enjoy the rose? If there first be no storm, how shall we appreciate the calm? Paul suffered the same despair being …pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life –2 Corinthians 1:8. Yet he carried within his breast a visionary anchor for his soul.

For he commandeth, and raiseth the stormy wind, which lifteth up the waves thereof. They mount up to the heaven, they go down again to the depths: their soul is melted because of trouble. They reel to and fro, and stagger like a drunken man, and are at their wits’ end. Then they cry unto the LORD in their trouble, and he bringeth them out of their distresses. He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still. Then are they glad because they be quiet; so he bringeth them unto their desired haven –Psalm 107:25-30.

The Desired Haven…

Somehow, we have embraced the thought that the desired haven of rest is an earthly euphoric utopia void of any storms. The shipmaster in charge of guiding the vessel en route to Rome thought that …the haven was not commodious to winter in … supposing that they had obtained their purpose… –Acts 27:12-13, so he set sail at the first hint of approval from the soft south wind. But the haven Christ promotes is a harbor that is free from fretful fear and fledgling faith. This is a peace … not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid –John 14:27. This rest is ours to be had just by sailing with Christ and trusting Him to guide us through each storm.

The tenacious storms of adversity can arise without warning as quickly as …a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon –Acts 27:14. These tempestuous winds carry an amazing audacity to jolt any relationship. To feel tense and alert in the midst of stressful situations is but human nature. Our central medulla gland unleashes a powerful hormone called adrenaline into our system, our muscles become tense, our mind focuses, so that we are aroused and prepared for fight or flight. This is not necessarily anxiety but a natural response. As humans, we have a divine capacity to reason in the midst of extreme passion and pressure. The disciples did not know what Jesus would do. They only knew that this situation was out of control. Here is where they made their major mistake. Christ knew Who was in control. Paul knew Who was in control. Even Jonah knew why the tempest had arisen. Our faith is bound to fail when anxiety escalates, and we think we must control the raging trials about us. We may have a noble agenda and a sincere heart and still find our faltering faith frazzled. We mistakenly marvel that God sits in heaven and does nothing. We faithfully launch our prayers upward, but the heavens seem brazenly silent. We would expect that from worshippers of Baal, Buddha, and from backsliders. But it is not supposed to happen to people with strong convictions—people who are born again, attend church regularly, read their Bible, and pray on a daily basis. We must reconsider that God is not so concerned about our environmental peace, but rather that our inner soul arrives safe and sound at His haven of rest.

When we are happy, we jubilantly claim that rest, even though we have no sense of truly needing Him. His insertions into our lives often seem like interruptions. But when times get desperate and we have exhausted all our resources, we lean hard upon Him. In that excruciating hour, He often tests our sincerity and offers us nothing … nothing but silence. Christ, sleeping in our boat. Sleeping… right when we need him the most. And then the question, Why are ye so fearful? How is it that ye have no faith? Frankly, this seems hard to me—even harsh—and entirely out of character with what I would normally expect from Jesus. But the question must be answered, for it is necessary if we wish to enter His haven of rest. The winds obey Him, but they don’t obey us … or do they? We obviously cannot control the weather, our environment, our situations, or the people around us. Yet these externals are not the root cause of our anxiety. It is our own faulty premonitions that pound our soul and prevent us from entering the portal of peace. The winds that whip our vessel into a fearful frenzy are not driven from without but unleashed from within. This anxiety rides on the waves of unbelief, while Christ continues in His divine slumber, waiting until we recognize the source of our anxiety and call out in faith. These four strong winds are roused at the slightest provocation when we are…

…Preserving our Person

If we are healthy, and if things are going well in our family and finances, we may be prone to misinterpret our circumstances. It is a mistake to believe that easy sailing is a mark of God’s favor, and that trouble is a sign of His displeasure. All good and perfect gifts come from God, but a debilitating storm can fall under that category as well. Our personal surroundings are temporal while our soul is eternal. God will frequently expend our personal comforts in order to expand our faith. But great fear arises when our person is demoted. Many of our phobias arise in the absence of actual danger.

  1. The acrophobic person has a fear of heights and is afraid he will fall from the heights of any platform though it is secure and guarded well. Even if countless others have successfully stood there, he is miserably trapped in this fear, not because he is in danger, but because he has grossly overestimated his likelihood of falling and refuses to believe the truth.
  2. The zoophobic lives in fear of animals, creating images in his mind of being clawed to death or disemboweled.
  3. The claustrophobic is afraid of small, tight places, while the agoraphobic fears open places.
  4. Arachibutyrophobia is the fear of getting peanut butter stuck to the roof of your mouth.

In the face of his fear, the phobic may experience a racing heart, heavy breathing, dry mouth, perspiration, dizziness, or light-headedness. Thus, their phobias become real to them. While most will excuse their personal glitch, the truth remains that this anxiety is unfounded. When we excuse and cater to the preservation of our person, fear is inevitable. The disciples feared that they were perishing, and Christ asked them why. Is it not better …to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better –Philippians 1:23. If we can trust Christ with our life, can we not trust him with our death?

For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel’s, the same shall save it –Mark 8:35.

…Protecting our Property

Outwardly, the life of Christ was one of the most troubled lives that was ever lived. Foxes had their dens and the birds had their nests while He lay His pillow in the back of a rocking boat groaning under tempest and tumult of the incessant waves breaking over it. But His inner haven was a sea of glass. This was partially due to the fact that He had no property to protect. Even the boat was borrowed. “Much coin, much care” states the ancient proverb, and anxiety rises when wealth falls. And one of the company said unto him, Master, speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance with me –Luke 12:13. Jesus refused to side with him. Instead, He spoke to the covetous heart that was causing the anxiety. If Christ gives us wealth, we do not need to feel guilty. If He takes it, we do not need to feel anxiety. In the midst of the storm, we are exhorted …to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship –Acts 27:22. This was ministered as healing balm to the bedraggled sailors, but to those who feel inclined to protect their property it is a sordid saga. When the rich young ruler was offered salvation in exchange for his earthly collection of trinkets, …he went away sorrowful: for he had great possessions –Matthew 19:22. Those of us who become anxious at the loss of our wealth are no less foolish.

…Perfecting our Plan

We set out on a course. Maybe we change jobs, enter into a relationship, or embark upon some new avenue of ministry. We have launched out in faith and before we know it, we are struggling. The winds and waves of ordinary life seem to be working against us. We have expectations that are not being met and it seems that Christ is not doing His part. It is not Christ, but rather it is our expectation that is the cause of our anxiety. We expect much from our investments and it is discouraging to see our efforts go for naught. Martha’s pulse quickened at the lack of help she was receiving in the kitchen. Her frustration rose while her well-planned meal remained unfinished. Her complaint is no less accusing than the disciples’ while rowing in the sea. …Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me –Luke 10:40. Her anxiety was not caused by Mary’s neglect nor Christ’s indifference. Her sister was docked at the haven of rest while Martha battled the tumultuous emotions within her heart. So does the perfectionist create his own storm when his unfulfilled vision falls short of his expectations. But Christ is more concerned about faith-filled bosoms than water-filled boats.

…Pleasing all People

The Scriptures have taught us well to love our neighbor as ourselves, but that does not insinuate that we must strive and aim for their approval. It feels wonderful to be liked. It is painful to be rejected. Thus, many souls spend their waking hours seeking the approval of others. They must dress like, act like, talk like, and live like their peers. These live a life laden with stressful waves of anxiety. A flurry of “what ifs” arrive with each new acquaintance. There is no ship more fragile than a relationship. No matter how great a sacrifice we make to be loved, we will eventually encounter a disappointing squall sucking us down to the depths of despair. When our best efforts fail us and our best friends derail us, we must bring our battered vessel to the haven of rest. Inconvenient, unfortunate, unpleasant, and annoying relationships will always exist. We shall do much better to make excuses for others’ poor behavior than for our own. When we can rebuke the winds that arise within our own minds, we will immediately find ourselves at the desired haven.

There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest… –Hebrews 4:9-11.

Lalu timbullah angin ribut yang dahsyat, dan gelombang-gelombang memukul perahu sehingga kini perahu itu penuh air. Ia berada di bagian belakang perahu, tertidur di atas bantal; lalu mereka membangunkannya dan berkata kepadanya, Tuan, tidakkah Engkau berhati-hati bahwa kita binasa? Ia bangkit lalu menegur angin itu dan berkata kepada laut, Diam, tenanglah! Maka angin itu berhenti, dan timbullah ketenangan yang besar. Lalu Ia berkata kepada mereka, Mengapa kamu begitu takut? Mengapa kamu tidak mempunyai iman? Mereka sangat takut dan saling berkata satu kepada yang lain, Siapakah gerangan orang ini, sehingga bahkan angin dan laut pun taat kepada-Nya? Markus 4:37-41

Berkali-kali saya telah membaca bagian ini dan bertanya-tanya apa yang harus kita ambil darinya. Tampaknya ini adalah kisah yang menimbulkan lebih banyak pertanyaan daripada yang dipecahkannya. Kita sering suka memandang Yesus sebagai bentuk pribadi dari Keilahian; semacam perantara antara kita dan Allah Yang Mahakuasa. Tetapi di sini, dalam bagian Kitab Suci kita, perilaku-Nya nyaris tak terbayangkan dalam istilah manusia. Bagaimana mungkin Kristus dapat tidur dalam badai seperti itu, apalagi di perahu yang penuh dengan air? Kita bisa percaya bahwa Ia adalah Tuan atas angin dan laut, dan mereka harus tunduk pada perintah-Nya, tetapi apakah Ia mengharapkan kita untuk berbuat sama? Apakah Kristus yang penuh belas kasihan mengharapkan kita untuk tenang dan tak takut dalam keadaan yang begitu genting? Apakah segala bentuk ketakutan merupakan buah dari kurangnya iman kita? Pertanyaan-pertanyaan menggugah ini mengganggu, karena kita semua berharap iman kita kepada-Nya cukup kuat untuk menjamin keselamatan kita, namun pengalaman mengajarkan kita bahwa perjalanan kita melalui padang rumput yang bermasalah dalam hidup ini tidak menghasilkan sesuatu yang lebih mulia daripada tangisan ketakutan para murid.

Mengapa kamu begitu takut? Mengapa kamu tidak mempunyai iman? Pertanyaan-pertanyaan itu tampak hampir tidak pada tempatnya datang dari Juruselamat kita, hampir seolah-olah Ia tidak sepenyayang dan sabar seperti yang kita harapkan. Tetapi Kristus telah menempatkan suatu harapan yang tegas atas murid-murid-Nya yang bukan di luar jangkauan mereka. Apakah Ia menuntut mereka untuk menegur badai itu sendiri? Haruskah mereka membangunkan-Nya lebih cepat? Apakah Ia mengira mereka harus tetap mendayung dengan tenang dalam keyakinan yang mantap? Kitab Suci di sini memberi kita sedikit jawaban, tetapi kita tahu bahwa ada pelajaran yang tetap mengenai takut dan iman.

Badai adalah bagian umum dari hidup, dan tidak ada kesulitan besar yang menyenangkan. Ketika Paulus berlayar menuju Roma, mereka mengalami suatu masa …ketika tidak tampak matahari maupun bintang beberapa hari lamanya, dan angin ribut yang dahsyat menimpa kami, sehingga hilanglah segala harapan bahwa kami selamat –Kisah Para Rasul 27:20. Di tengah situasi yang mendung dan putus asa ada satu lonceng yang terus berdentang jernih dan terang: Ada damai sejahtera yang dapat diraih bahkan dalam keadaan yang paling mengerikan. Paulus telah mengalami suatu malam yang genting …malam dan siang aku telah berada di dalam kedalaman –2 Korintus 11:25, namun ia tidak menuntut agar angin dan laut tunduk pada kekuasaannya. Sebaliknya, ia menyatakan bahwa di tengah badai …malam itu berdiri dekat aku malaikat Allah, yang aku punak, dan yang aku layani, berkata, Jangan takut, Paulus… –Kisah Para Rasul 27:23-24. Ini adalah adegan yang mirip dengan bahaya yang ditanggung para murid (dalam teks kita untuk hari ini) namun kita melihat hasil yang berbeda. Paulus diberi penghiburan dan pujian sementara para murid mendapat teguran.

Saat terombang-ambing di cengkraman kuburan berair yang mungkin menanti, para murid berseru: …Tuan, tidakkah Engkau berhati-hati bahwa kita binasa? –Markus 4:38. Betapa alamiahnya bagi kita semua untuk melemparkan frustrasi dan tuduhan kepada orang lain. Mengira bahwa seseorang yang acuh tak acuh mengabaikan tanggung jawabnya sangat mengecewakan. Dengan cara yang serupa …nahkoda datang kepada Yunus lalu berkata kepadanya, Apakah maksudmu, hai orang yang tidur? Bangunlah, berserulah kepada Allahmu, barangkali Allah akan memikirkan kita sehingga kita tidak binasa –Yunus 1:6.

Tampak ada nada tajam dalam teguran nahkoda yang sangat mirip dengan tanggapan murid-murid kepada Yesus yang sedang tidur. Kristus tidak senang membiarkan kesusahan menimpa kita, tetapi tampaknya tidak ada kendaraan kasih karunia sejati lain di mana damai-Nya dapat membanjiri jiwa kita. Jika tidak ada lembah terlebih dahulu, bagaimana kita akan menghargai puncak gunung? Jika tidak ada duri, bagaimana kita bisa menikmati mawar? Jika tidak ada badai terlebih dahulu, bagaimana kita akan menghargai ketenangan? Paulus menderita keputusasaan yang sama ketika ia …tertekan melampaui ukuran, di luar kekuatan, sehingga kami putus asa bahkan akan hidup –2 Korintus 1:8. Namun ia membawa dalam dadanya sebuah jangkar penglihatan bagi jiwanya.

Sebab Ia berfirman lalu menimbulkan angin ribut yang mengangkat gelombang-gelombangnya. Mereka naik sampai ke langit, lalu turun lagi ke dasar laut: jiwanya menjadi cair karena kesusahan. Mereka bergoyang ke sana ke mari dan sempoyongan seperti orang mabuk, dan sampai pada kesusahan besar. Lalu mereka berseru kepada TUHAN dalam kesesakan mereka, maka Ia mengeluarkan mereka dari kesesakan itu. Ia menjadikan badai menjadi tenang, sehingga gelombang-gelombangnya menjadi reda. Mereka bersukacita karena Ia membawa mereka ke pelabuhan yang diinginkan –Mazmur 107:25-30.

Pelabuhan yang Diinginkan…

Dengan entah bagaimana, kita telah menerima gagasan bahwa pelabuhan istirahat yang diinginkan adalah utopia duniawi yang euforia tanpa badai. Nahkoda yang bertanggung jawab menuntun kapal menuju Roma berpikir bahwa …pelabuhan itu tidak layak untuk menginap waktu musim dingin …menyangka bahwa mereka telah mencapai maksudnya… –Kisah Para Rasul 27:12-13, sehingga ia berlayar pada petunjuk pertama angin selatan yang lembut. Tetapi pelabuhan yang dipromosikan Kristus adalah sebuah pelabuhan yang bebas dari ketakutan yang gelisah dan iman yang rapuh. Ini adalah suatu damai … bukan seperti yang diberikan dunia, Kuberikan kepada kamu. Janganlah gelisah hatimu dan janganlah takut –Yohanes 14:27. Istirahat ini menjadi milik kita hanya dengan berlayar bersama Kristus dan mempercayai-Nya untuk menuntun kita melalui setiap badai.

Badai-badai keras karena kesengsaraan bisa muncul tanpa peringatan secepat …angin yang sangat keras yang disebut Euroklidon –Kisah Para Rasul 27:14. Angin ribut ini membawa keberanian luar biasa untuk mengguncang setiap hubungan. Merasa tegang dan waspada di tengah situasi yang menegangkan adalah sifat manusiawi. Kelenjar medula tengah kita melepaskan hormon kuat yang disebut adrenalin ke dalam sistem kita, otot-otot kita menjadi tegang, pikiran kita fokus, sehingga kita terbangun dan siap untuk berkelahi atau melarikan diri. Ini tidak selalu cemas tetapi respons alami. Sebagai manusia, kita mempunyai kapasitas ilahi untuk menggunakan nalar di tengah gairah dan tekanan ekstrem. Para murid tidak tahu apa yang akan dilakukan Yesus. Mereka hanya tahu bahwa situasi ini di luar kendali. Di sinilah mereka membuat kesalahan utama. Kristus tahu Siapa yang mengendalikan. Paulus tahu Siapa yang mengendalikan. Bahkan Yunus tahu mengapa badai itu muncul. Iman kita cenderung gagal ketika kecemasan meningkat, dan kita berpikir kita harus mengendalikan cobaan yang mengamuk di sekitar kita. Kita mungkin memiliki agenda mulia dan hati yang tulus dan tetap menemukan iman kita goyah. Kita secara keliru heran bahwa Allah duduk di surga dan tidak berbuat apa-apa. Kita dengan tekun meluncurkan doa kita ke atas, tetapi langit tampak berani-beraninya tetap sunyi. Kita mungkin mengharapkan itu dari penyembah Baal, Buddha, dan dari orang yang telah meninggalkan jalan—tetapi seharusnya tidak terjadi pada orang-orang yang berkeyakinan kuat—orang yang dilahirkan kembali, sering menghadiri gereja, membaca Alkitab mereka, dan berdoa setiap hari. Kita harus mempertimbangkan kembali bahwa Allah tidak begitu memperhatikan kedamaian lingkungan kita, melainkan agar jiwa batiniah kita tiba dengan selamat di pelabuhan istirahat-Nya.

Saat kita senang, kita gembira mengklaim istirahat itu, meskipun kita tidak merasakan kebutuhan yang sungguh akan Dia. Campur tangan-Nya dalam hidup kita sering tampak seperti gangguan. Tetapi ketika masa menjadi putus asa dan kita telah menguras semua sumber daya kita, kita bersandar kuat pada-Nya. Pada saat yang menyiksa itu, Ia sering menguji ketulusan kita dan menawarkan kita tidak ada apa-apa … tidak lain kecuali keheningan. Kristus, tertidur di perahu kita. Tertidur… tepat ketika kita paling membutuhkan-Nya. Dan kemudian pertanyaan, Mengapa kamu begitu takut? Mengapa kamu tidak mempunyai iman? Jujur, ini terasa keras bagi saya—bahkan kasar—dan sepenuhnya di luar karakter yang biasa saya harapkan dari Yesus. Tetapi pertanyaan itu harus dijawab, karena itu perlu jika kita ingin memasuki pelabuhan istirahat-Nya. Angin-angin itu taat kepada-Nya, tetapi mereka tidak taat kepada kita … atau apakah mereka? Jelas kita tidak dapat mengendalikan cuaca, lingkungan kita, situasi kita, atau orang-orang di sekitar kita. Namun eksternal-eksternal ini bukanlah penyebab akar dari kecemasan kita. Jemakan prasangka kita sendiri-lah yang memukul jiwa kita dan menghalangi kita memasuki gerbang damai. Angin yang memukul perahu kita menjadi kegirangan karena ketakutan tidak didorong dari luar tetapi dilepaskan dari dalam. Kecemasan ini menunggangi gelombang ketidakpercayaan, sementara Kristus tetap dalam tidur ilahi-Nya, menunggu sampai kita mengenali sumber kecemasan kita dan berseru dengan iman. Keempat angin kencang ini terbangkitkan pada provokasi sekecil apa pun ketika kita…

…Memelihara Pribadi Kita

Jika kita sehat, dan jika segala sesuatu berjalan baik dalam keluarga dan keuangan kita, kita mungkin cenderung salah menafsirkan keadaan kita. Merupakan kesalahan percaya bahwa berlayar lancar adalah tanda kasih karunia Allah, dan bahwa kesusahan adalah tanda ketidakpuasan-Nya. Semua pemberian baik dan sempurna berasal dari Allah, tetapi badai yang melemahkan juga bisa termasuk dalam kategori itu. Lingkungan pribadi kita bersifat temporal sedangkan jiwa kita abadi. Allah seringkali akan menghabiskan kenyamanan pribadi kita demi memperluas iman kita. Tetapi ketakutan besar muncul ketika pribadi kita diturunkan. Banyak fobia kita muncul tanpa adanya bahaya nyata.

  1. Orang yang akrofobik takut pada ketinggian dan takut ia akan jatuh dari ketinggian manapun meskipun tiang atau platform itu aman dan terjaga. Bahkan jika banyak orang lain telah berhasil berdiri di sana, ia terperangkap sengsara dalam ketakutan ini, bukan karena ia dalam bahaya, tetapi karena ia sangat melebih-lebihkan kemungkinan jatuhnya dan menolak mempercayai kebenaran.
  2. Zoofobik hidup dalam ketakutan terhadap binatang, mencipta citra dalam pikirannya bahwa ia dicakar sampai mati atau dikeluarkan isinya.
  3. Klaustrofobik takut pada ruang yang kecil dan sempit, sementara agorafobik takut pada tempat-tempat terbuka.
  4. Arachibutyrophobia adalah ketakutan mendapatkan selai kacang yang menempel di langit-langit mulutmu.

Dalam menghadapi ketakutannya, orang yang fobia mungkin mengalami detak jantung yang cepat, napas berat, mulut kering, berkeringat, pusing, atau terasa ringan di kepala. Dengan demikian, fobia mereka menjadi nyata bagi mereka. Sementara kebanyakan orang akan memberi alasan untuk gangguan pribadi mereka, kebenaran tetap bahwa kecemasan ini tidak beralasan. Ketika kita memaafkan dan melayani pemeliharaan pribadi kita, ketakutan tak terelakkan. Para murid takut bahwa mereka akan binasa, dan Kristus bertanya kepada mereka mengapa. Tidakkah lebih baik …meninggal dan berada bersama Kristus; jauh lebih baik itu –Filipi 1:23. Jika kita dapat mempercayai Kristus dengan hidup kita, bukankah kita dapat mempercayai-Nya dengan kematian kita?

Sebab barangsiapa hendak menyelamatkan nyawanya, ia akan kehilangannya; tetapi barangsiapa yang kehilangan nyawanya karena Aku dan karena Injil, ia akan menyelamatkannya –Markus 8:35.

…Melindungi Harta Kita

Dilihat dari luar, hidup Kristus adalah salah satu hidup yang paling diliputi masalah yang pernah ada. Rubah mempunyai liang dan burung mempunyai sarang sementara Ia meletakkan kepala-Nya di bantal di belakang sebuah perahu yang berayun merintih di bawah badai dan kekacauan gelombang yang tak hentinya memecah di atasnya. Tetapi pelabuhan batin-Nya adalah lautan kaca. Ini sebagian disebabkan oleh fakta bahwa Ia tidak memiliki harta untuk dilindungi. Bahkan perahu itu pun dipinjam. “Banyak uang, banyak kepedulian” bunyi peribahasa kuno, dan kecemasan muncul ketika kekayaan menurun. Dan seorang berkata kepada-Nya, Tuan, suruhlah saudara-Ku supaya membagi warisan dengan aku –Lukas 12:13. Yesus menolak berpihak kepadanya. Sebaliknya, Ia berbicara kepada hati yang tamak yang menyebabkan kecemasan itu. Jika Kristus memberi kita kekayaan, kita tidak perlu merasa bersalah. Jika Ia mengambilnya, kita tidak perlu merasa cemas. Di tengah badai, kita dihibur …supaya beroleh penghiburan: sebab tidak akan hilang nyawa seorang pun di antara kamu, hanya perahu itu saja –Kisah Para Rasul 27:22. Ini diucapkan sebagai balsam penyembuhan bagi para pelaut yang compang-camping, tetapi bagi mereka yang cenderung melindungi harta benda mereka itu adalah saga yang suram. Ketika orang kaya muda ditawari keselamatan dengan imbalan koleksi barang duniawinya, …ia pergi dengan sedih: sebab ia mempunyai banyak harta –Matius 19:22. Kita yang menjadi cemas karena kehilangan kekayaan kita tidaklah kurang bodoh.

…Menyempurnakan Rencana Kita

Kita memulai suatu lintasan. Mungkin kita mengganti pekerjaan, memasuki suatu hubungan, atau memulai jalur pelayanan baru. Kita telah berlayar karena iman dan sebelum kita menyadarinya, kita berjuang. Angin dan gelombang kehidupan biasa tampak bekerja melawan kita. Kita memiliki harapan yang tidak terpenuhi dan tampaknya Kristus tidak melakukan bagiannya. Bukan Kristus, melainkan harapan kita yang menjadi penyebab kecemasan kita. Kita mengharapkan banyak dari investasi kita dan mengecewakan melihat usaha kita sia-sia. Nadi Marta berdebar karena kurangnya bantuan yang diterimanya di dapur. Frustrasinya meningkat sementara makan yang ia rencanakan rapi tetap belum selesai. Keluhannya tidak kurang menuduh daripada para murid yang sedang mendayung di laut. …Tuhan, tidakkah Engkau peduli bahwa saudariku meninggalkan aku melayani seorang diri? Suruhlah ia supaya menolong aku –Lukas 10:40. Kecemasannya tidak disebabkan oleh pengabaian Maria ataupun oleh ketidakpedulian Kristus. Saudarinya sedang berlabuh di pelabuhan istirahat sementara Marta berjuang melawan emosi yang bergemuruh di dalam hatinya. Demikianlah si perfeksionis menciptakan badainya sendiri ketika visi yang tidak terpenuhi tidak sesuai dengan harapannya. Tetapi Kristus lebih peduli kepada dada yang dipenuhi iman daripada perahu yang dipenuhi air.

…Menyenangkan Semua Orang

Kitab Suci telah mengajarkan kita dengan baik untuk mengasihi sesama seperti diri sendiri, tetapi itu tidak menyiratkan bahwa kita harus berusaha dan mengincar persetujuan mereka. Rasanya menyenangkan disukai. Menyakitkan ditolak. Karena itu, banyak jiwa menghabiskan jam-jam mereka terjaga mencari persetujuan orang lain. Mereka harus berpakaian seperti, bertindak seperti, berbicara seperti, dan hidup seperti rekan-rekan mereka. Mereka menjalani hidup yang dipenuhi gelombang kecemasan yang menekan. Gelombang “bagaimana jika” datang dengan setiap kenalan baru. Tidak ada kapal yang lebih rapuh daripada suatu hubungan. Betapapun besar pengorbanan yang kita lakukan untuk dicintai, akhirnya kita akan mengalami badai yang mengecewakan yang menarik kita ke dasar keputusasaan. Ketika usaha terbaik kita mengecewakan dan sahabat terbaik kita menjatuhkan kita, kita harus membawa kapal kita yang compang-camping ke pelabuhan istirahat. Hubungan yang merepotkan, tidak menguntungkan, tidak menyenangkan, dan menjengkelkan akan selalu ada. Kita akan jauh lebih baik membuat alasan bagi tingkah laku buruk orang lain daripada bagi diri kita sendiri. Ketika kita dapat menegur angin yang timbul dalam pikiran kita sendiri, kita akan segera mendapati diri kita di pelabuhan yang diinginkan.

Jadi masih ada suatu istirahat bagi umat Allah. Karena barangsiapa telah masuk ke dalam istirahat-Nya, ia juga telah berhenti dari pekerjaan sendiri, sama seperti Allah berhenti dari pekerjaan-Nya. Karena itu marilah kita berusaha agar kita masuk ke dalam istirahat itu… –Ibrani 4:9-11.

And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full. And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish? And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm. And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith? And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him? Mark 4:37-41

Many times, I have read this passage and wondered what we are to derive from it. It seems to be a story that generates more questions than it solves. We often like to think of Jesus as the relational form of the Godhead; a sort of go-between, between us and the Almighty God. But here, in our scriptural passage, His behavior is almost unthinkable in human terms. How could Christ sleep in such a storm, much less in a boat filling with water? We can believe that He is Master of the wind and seas, and they must bow at His command, but does He expect us to do the same? Would our compassionate Christ expect us to be calm and fearless in such dire straits? Is all exhibition of fear the fruit of our lack of faith? These probing questions are disturbing, for we all would hope that our faith in Him is strong enough to secure our salvation, yet experience has taught us that our own walk through the troublesome pastures of life has produced nothing more noble than the harrowing bleating of the disciples.

Why are ye so fearful? How is it that ye have no faith? The questions seem almost out of place coming from our Saviour, almost as though He is not as patient and longsuffering as we had hoped. But Christ has placed a definitive expectation upon His disciples that is not beyond their attainment. Was He calling on them to rebuke the storm themselves? Should they have awakened Him sooner? Did he expect them to quietly row on in confident assurance? The Scripture here supplies us with few answers, but we do know that there is an abiding lesson here concerning fear and faith.

Storms are a common part of life, and no major dilemma is pleasant. While Paul sailed toward Rome, they experienced a time …when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away –Acts 27:20. In the midst of a cloudy and hopeless situation there is one bell that continues to toll clear and bright: There is a peace that can be apprehended even in the most dreadful circumstances. Paul had spent a precarious …night and a day I have been in the deep –2 Corinthians 11:25, yet he did not demand the wind and sea to submit to his authority. Rather, he states that in the midst of the storm …there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve, Saying, Fear not, Paul… –Acts 27:23-24. This is a scene similar to the peril being endured by the disciples (in our text for today) yet we see a different outcome. Paul was comforted and commended while the disciples received rebuke.

While bobbing about in the clutches of a potential watery grave, the disciples cried out: …Master, carest thou not that we perish? –Mark 4:38. How natural it is for us all to thrust our frustration and blame upon another. To think that some apathetic person is shirking their responsibility is very disheartening. In like fashion …the shipmaster came to him [Jonah], and said unto him, What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not –Jonah 1:6.

There seems to be an edge to the shipmaster’s rebuke very similar to the disciple’s response to the sleeping Jesus. Christ finds no pleasure in allowing trouble to visit us, but there seems to be no other veritable vehicle of grace wherewith His peace can flood our souls. If there first be no valley, how shall we value the mountaintop? If there be no thorns, how shall we enjoy the rose? If there first be no storm, how shall we appreciate the calm? Paul suffered the same despair being …pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life –2 Corinthians 1:8. Yet he carried within his breast a visionary anchor for his soul.

For he commandeth, and raiseth the stormy wind, which lifteth up the waves thereof. They mount up to the heaven, they go down again to the depths: their soul is melted because of trouble. They reel to and fro, and stagger like a drunken man, and are at their wits’ end. Then they cry unto the LORD in their trouble, and he bringeth them out of their distresses. He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still. Then are they glad because they be quiet; so he bringeth them unto their desired haven –Psalm 107:25-30.

The Desired Haven…

Somehow, we have embraced the thought that the desired haven of rest is an earthly euphoric utopia void of any storms. The shipmaster in charge of guiding the vessel en route to Rome thought that …the haven was not commodious to winter in … supposing that they had obtained their purpose… –Acts 27:12-13, so he set sail at the first hint of approval from the soft south wind. But the haven Christ promotes is a harbor that is free from fretful fear and fledgling faith. This is a peace … not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid –John 14:27. This rest is ours to be had just by sailing with Christ and trusting Him to guide us through each storm.

The tenacious storms of adversity can arise without warning as quickly as …a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon –Acts 27:14. These tempestuous winds carry an amazing audacity to jolt any relationship. To feel tense and alert in the midst of stressful situations is but human nature. Our central medulla gland unleashes a powerful hormone called adrenaline into our system, our muscles become tense, our mind focuses, so that we are aroused and prepared for fight or flight. This is not necessarily anxiety but a natural response. As humans, we have a divine capacity to reason in the midst of extreme passion and pressure. The disciples did not know what Jesus would do. They only knew that this situation was out of control. Here is where they made their major mistake. Christ knew Who was in control. Paul knew Who was in control. Even Jonah knew why the tempest had arisen. Our faith is bound to fail when anxiety escalates, and we think we must control the raging trials about us. We may have a noble agenda and a sincere heart and still find our faltering faith frazzled. We mistakenly marvel that God sits in heaven and does nothing. We faithfully launch our prayers upward, but the heavens seem brazenly silent. We would expect that from worshippers of Baal, Buddha, and from backsliders. But it is not supposed to happen to people with strong convictions—people who are born again, attend church regularly, read their Bible, and pray on a daily basis. We must reconsider that God is not so concerned about our environmental peace, but rather that our inner soul arrives safe and sound at His haven of rest.

When we are happy, we jubilantly claim that rest, even though we have no sense of truly needing Him. His insertions into our lives often seem like interruptions. But when times get desperate and we have exhausted all our resources, we lean hard upon Him. In that excruciating hour, He often tests our sincerity and offers us nothing … nothing but silence. Christ, sleeping in our boat. Sleeping… right when we need him the most. And then the question, Why are ye so fearful? How is it that ye have no faith? Frankly, this seems hard to me—even harsh—and entirely out of character with what I would normally expect from Jesus. But the question must be answered, for it is necessary if we wish to enter His haven of rest. The winds obey Him, but they don’t obey us … or do they? We obviously cannot control the weather, our environment, our situations, or the people around us. Yet these externals are not the root cause of our anxiety. It is our own faulty premonitions that pound our soul and prevent us from entering the portal of peace. The winds that whip our vessel into a fearful frenzy are not driven from without but unleashed from within. This anxiety rides on the waves of unbelief, while Christ continues in His divine slumber, waiting until we recognize the source of our anxiety and call out in faith. These four strong winds are roused at the slightest provocation when we are…

…Preserving our Person

If we are healthy, and if things are going well in our family and finances, we may be prone to misinterpret our circumstances. It is a mistake to believe that easy sailing is a mark of God’s favor, and that trouble is a sign of His displeasure. All good and perfect gifts come from God, but a debilitating storm can fall under that category as well. Our personal surroundings are temporal while our soul is eternal. God will frequently expend our personal comforts in order to expand our faith. But great fear arises when our person is demoted. Many of our phobias arise in the absence of actual danger.

  1. The acrophobic person has a fear of heights and is afraid he will fall from the heights of any platform though it is secure and guarded well. Even if countless others have successfully stood there, he is miserably trapped in this fear, not because he is in danger, but because he has grossly overestimated his likelihood of falling and refuses to believe the truth.
  2. The zoophobic lives in fear of animals, creating images in his mind of being clawed to death or disemboweled.
  3. The claustrophobic is afraid of small, tight places, while the agoraphobic fears open places.
  4. Arachibutyrophobia is the fear of getting peanut butter stuck to the roof of your mouth.

In the face of his fear, the phobic may experience a racing heart, heavy breathing, dry mouth, perspiration, dizziness, or light-headedness. Thus, their phobias become real to them. While most will excuse their personal glitch, the truth remains that this anxiety is unfounded. When we excuse and cater to the preservation of our person, fear is inevitable. The disciples feared that they were perishing, and Christ asked them why. Is it not better …to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better –Philippians 1:23. If we can trust Christ with our life, can we not trust him with our death?

For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel’s, the same shall save it –Mark 8:35.

…Protecting our Property

Outwardly, the life of Christ was one of the most troubled lives that was ever lived. Foxes had their dens and the birds had their nests while He lay His pillow in the back of a rocking boat groaning under tempest and tumult of the incessant waves breaking over it. But His inner haven was a sea of glass. This was partially due to the fact that He had no property to protect. Even the boat was borrowed. “Much coin, much care” states the ancient proverb, and anxiety rises when wealth falls. And one of the company said unto him, Master, speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance with me –Luke 12:13. Jesus refused to side with him. Instead, He spoke to the covetous heart that was causing the anxiety. If Christ gives us wealth, we do not need to feel guilty. If He takes it, we do not need to feel anxiety. In the midst of the storm, we are exhorted …to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship –Acts 27:22. This was ministered as healing balm to the bedraggled sailors, but to those who feel inclined to protect their property it is a sordid saga. When the rich young ruler was offered salvation in exchange for his earthly collection of trinkets, …he went away sorrowful: for he had great possessions –Matthew 19:22. Those of us who become anxious at the loss of our wealth are no less foolish.

…Perfecting our Plan

We set out on a course. Maybe we change jobs, enter into a relationship, or embark upon some new avenue of ministry. We have launched out in faith and before we know it, we are struggling. The winds and waves of ordinary life seem to be working against us. We have expectations that are not being met and it seems that Christ is not doing His part. It is not Christ, but rather it is our expectation that is the cause of our anxiety. We expect much from our investments and it is discouraging to see our efforts go for naught. Martha’s pulse quickened at the lack of help she was receiving in the kitchen. Her frustration rose while her well-planned meal remained unfinished. Her complaint is no less accusing than the disciples’ while rowing in the sea. …Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me –Luke 10:40. Her anxiety was not caused by Mary’s neglect nor Christ’s indifference. Her sister was docked at the haven of rest while Martha battled the tumultuous emotions within her heart. So does the perfectionist create his own storm when his unfulfilled vision falls short of his expectations. But Christ is more concerned about faith-filled bosoms than water-filled boats.

…Pleasing all People

The Scriptures have taught us well to love our neighbor as ourselves, but that does not insinuate that we must strive and aim for their approval. It feels wonderful to be liked. It is painful to be rejected. Thus, many souls spend their waking hours seeking the approval of others. They must dress like, act like, talk like, and live like their peers. These live a life laden with stressful waves of anxiety. A flurry of “what ifs” arrive with each new acquaintance. There is no ship more fragile than a relationship. No matter how great a sacrifice we make to be loved, we will eventually encounter a disappointing squall sucking us down to the depths of despair. When our best efforts fail us and our best friends derail us, we must bring our battered vessel to the haven of rest. Inconvenient, unfortunate, unpleasant, and annoying relationships will always exist. We shall do much better to make excuses for others’ poor behavior than for our own. When we can rebuke the winds that arise within our own minds, we will immediately find ourselves at the desired haven.

There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest… –Hebrews 4:9-11.

Og det oppstod en stor storm av vind, og bølgene slo inn i båten, så den nå var i ferd med å fylles. Og han var i akterenden av båten, sov på en pute; og de vekket ham og sa til ham: Mester, bryr du deg ikke om at vi går til grunne? Og han stod opp og irettesatte vinden og sa til sjøen: Ti! Vær stille! Og vinden sluttet, og det ble stor stillhet. Og han sa til dem: Hvorfor er dere så redde? Hvordan kan det være at dere ikke har tro? Og de ble forferdelig redde og sa til hverandre: Hvem er denne mannen, at også vinden og sjøen adlyder ham? Mark 4:37-41

Gjentatte ganger har jeg lest dette avsnittet og lurt på hva vi skal utlede av det. Det synes å være en fortelling som reiser flere spørsmål enn den løser. Vi liker ofte å tenke på Jesus som den relasjonelle formen for Guddommen; et slags mellomledd mellom oss og den allmektige Gud. Men her, i vårt skriftsted, er Hans væremåte nesten utenkelig i menneskelige termer. Hvordan kunne Kristus sove i en slik storm, enn si i en båt som fylles med vann? Vi kan tro at han er Herre over vind og hav, og at de må bøye seg for hans befaling, men forventer han at vi skal gjøre det samme? Ville vår medfølende Kristus forvente at vi skulle være rolige og fryktløse i slike desperate stridigheter? Er all fremvisning av frykt frukten av vår mangel på tro? Disse spørrende spørsmålene er forstyrrende, for vi ville alle håpe at vår tro på ham er sterk nok til å sikre vår frelse, likevel har erfaring lært oss at vår egen vandring gjennom livets besværlige beiter har produsert ikke mer edelt enn disiplene sitt skremte bjeff.

Hvorfor er dere så redde? Hvordan kan det være at dere ikke har tro? Spørsmålene virker nesten malplasserte når de kommer fra vår Frelser, nesten som om han ikke er så tålmodig og langmodig som vi hadde håpet. Men Kristus har lagt en definitiv forventning på sine disipler som ikke er utenfor deres rekkevidde. Kalte han dem til å irettesette stormen selv? Burde de ha vekket ham tidligere? Forventet han at de i stille tillit skulle ro videre? Skriften gir oss få svar her, men vi vet at det finnes en vedvarende lærepenge angående frykt og tro.

Stormer er en vanlig del av livet, og ingen stor nød er behagelig. Mens Paulus seilte mot Roma, opplevde de en tid …da verken sol eller stjerner var synlige i mange dager, og det var et ikke lite uvær over oss, og alt håp om at vi skulle bli berget ble fjernet – Apostlenes gjerninger 27:20. Midt i en skyet og håpløs situasjon ringer det likevel en klar og lys klokke: Det finnes en fred som kan gripes selv i de mest fryktelige omstendigheter. Paulus hadde gjennomlevd et farefylt …natt og dag var jeg i dypet – 2 Korinterbrev 11:25, men han krevde ikke at vind og sjø skulle underlegge seg hans myndighet. Snarere sier han at midt i stormen …stod denne natten hos meg en Guds engel, hvis jeg er, og hvem jeg tjener, og som sa: Frykt ikke, Paulus… – Apostlenes gjerninger 27:23-24. Dette er en scene lik faren disiplene gjennomlevde (i dagens tekst), likevel ser vi et annet utfall. Paulus ble trøstet og rost, mens disiplene fikk irettesettelse.

Mens de drev omkring i fare for å gå til grunne i vannet, ropte disiplene: …Mester, bryr du deg ikke om at vi går til grunne? – Markus 4:38. Hvor naturlig det er for oss alle å skyve vår frustrasjon og skyld over på en annen. Å tenke at en apatiske person svikter sitt ansvar er svært nedslående. På samme måte …kom skipsføreren til ham [Jona] og sa til ham: Hva er det du driver med, du sovende? Stå opp, kall på din Gud! Kanskje Gud vil kjenne på oss, så vi ikke går til grunne – Jona 1:6.

Det synes å ligge et skjerpende preg i skipsførerens irettesettelse, svært lik disiplene sin reaksjon på den sovende Jesus. Kristus finner ingen glede i å la trengsel besøke oss, men det synes ikke å finnes noe annet virkelig middel for nåde hvor hans fred kan oversvømme våre sjeler. Hvis det først ikke finnes en dal, hvordan skal vi verdsette fjelltoppen? Hvis det ikke finnes torner, hvordan skal vi nyte rosen? Hvis det først ikke finnes storm, hvordan skal vi sette pris på stillheten? Paulus led den samme fortvilelsen ved å være …presset uten mål, over styrke, så vi fortvilet selv om livet – 2 Korinterbrev 1:8. Likevel bar han i sitt bryst et synlig anker for sin sjel.

For han befaler og reiser stormfull vind, som løfter opp bølgene sine. De stiger opp til himmelen, de går ned igjen til dypet; sjelen deres smelter av nød. De vakler fram og tilbake og svinser som en beruset mann og er ved sitt endelige. Da roper de til HERREN i trengselen, og han fører dem ut av deres nød. Han gjør stormen stille, så bølgene legger seg. Da blir de glade fordi det er stille, og han fører dem til deres ønskede havn – Salme 107:25-30.

Det ønskede havnestedet…

På en eller annen måte har vi omfavnet tanken om at det ønskede havnestedet for hvile er en jordisk euforisk utopi uten noen stormer. Skipsføreren som skulle føre fartøyet på vei til Roma mente at …havnen ikke var egnet for å overvintre i … idet han antok at de hadde nådd sitt mål… – Apostlenes gjerninger 27:12-13, så han satte seil ved første tegn på godkjenning fra den milde sørvinden. Men havnen Kristus fremmer er en havn som er fri fra ærslig frykt og svak tro. Dette er en fred … ikke som verden gir, gir jeg dere. La ikke hjertet ditt være grepet av uro, og vær ikke redd – Johannes 14:27. Denne hvilen er vår å ha bare ved å seile med Kristus og stole på at han leder oss gjennom hver storm.

De seige stormene av motgang kan oppstå uten varsel like raskt som …en stormfull vind kalt euroklidon – Apostlenes gjerninger 27:14. Disse stormfulle vinder bærer en forbløffende frimodighet til å ryste ethvert forhold. Å føle seg anspent og årvåken midt i stressende situasjoner er bare menneskelig natur. Vår sentrale medullakjertel frigjør et kraftfullt hormon kalt adrenalin i systemet, musklene blir anspente, sinnet skjerpes, slik at vi blir opphisset og klare for kamp eller flukt. Dette er ikke nødvendigvis angst, men en naturlig reaksjon. Som mennesker har vi en gudgitt evne til å resonnere midt i sterk lidenskap og press. Disiplene visste ikke hva Jesus ville gjøre. De visste bare at situasjonen var ute av kontroll. Her gjorde de sin store feil. Kristus visste hvem som hadde kontroll. Paulus visste hvem som hadde kontroll. Selv Jona visste hvorfor uværet hadde reist seg. Vår tro er dømt til å svikte når angsten eskalerer, og vi tror vi må kontrollere de rasende prøvelsene rundt oss. Vi kan ha en edel agenda og et inderlig hjerte og likevel finne vår vaklende tro sprengt. Vi undrer oss feilaktig over at Gud sitter i himmelen og ikke gjør noe. Vi sender trofast våre bønner oppover, men himmelen synes skamløst taus. Det ville vi forvente fra Baal-tilbedere, Buddha-tilhengere og fra tilbakefallne. Men det skal ikke skje med mennesker med sterke overbevisninger—mennesker som er født på ny, går regelmessig i kirken, leser sin Bibel og ber daglig. Vi må revurdere at Gud ikke er så opptatt av vår ytre fred, men snarere at vår indre sjel kommer trygt og sikkert frem til hans hvilehavn.

Når vi er lykkelige, påberoper vi oss gledelig den hvilen, selv om vi ikke har noen følelse av virkelig å trenge ham. Hans inngripen i våre liv virker ofte som avbrudd. Men når tidene blir desperate og vi har uttømt alle ressurser, lener vi oss tungt på ham. I den eksepsjonelt smertefulle timen tester han ofte vår oppriktighet og gir oss ingenting … ingenting annet enn stillhet. Kristus, sovende i vår båt. Sovende… akkurat når vi trenger ham mest. Og så spørsmålet: Hvorfor er dere så redde? Hvordan kan det være at dere ikke har tro? Ærlig talt virker dette hardt på meg—enda strengt—og helt ute av karakter for hva jeg normalt ville forvente av Jesus. Men spørsmålet må besvares, for det er nødvendig om vi ønsker å entre hans hvilehavn. Vindene adlyder ham, men de adlyder oss ikke … eller gjør de? Vi kan åpenbart ikke kontrollere været, vårt miljø, våre omstendigheter eller menneskene omkring oss. Likevel er ikke disse ytre ting årsaken til vår angst. Det er våre egne feilaktige formodninger som banker på vår sjel og hindrer oss i å tre inn i fredens port. Vindene som pisker vårt fartøy inn i en fryktelig raseri er ikke drevet utenfra, men sluppet løs innenfra. Denne angsten rir på vantroets bølger, mens Kristus fortsetter sin guddommelige slummer, og venter til vi kjenner igjen kilden til vår angst og roper ut i tro. Disse fire sterke vindene blir opprørt ved den minste provokasjon når vi er…

…Bevarende vår person

Hvis vi er friske, og hvis ting går godt i familien og økonomien, kan vi være tilbøyelige til å misforstå våre omstendigheter. Det er en feil å tro at lett seilas er et tegn på Guds velbehag, og at trengsel er et tegn på hans misnøye. Alle gode og fullkomne gaver kommer fra Gud, men en svekkende storm kan også falle inn under den kategorien. Vårt personlige omgivelser er tidsmessige mens vår sjel er evig. Gud vil ofte bruke våre personlige bekvemmeligheter for å utvide vår tro. Men stor frykt oppstår når vår person nedgraderes. Mange av våre fobier oppstår i fraværet av virkelig fare.

  1. Akrofobiske personen har frykt for høyder og er redd for å falle fra enhver plattform, selv om den er sikker og godt beskyttet. Selv om utallige andre har stått der trygt, er han elendig fanget i denne frykten, ikke fordi han er i fare, men fordi han grovt har overvurdert sannsynligheten for å falle og nekter å tro sannheten.
  2. Zoofobiske lever i frykt for dyr, og skaper bilder i sitt sinn av å bli kloret ihjel eller opprevet.
  3. Klaustrofobiske er redd for små, trange steder, mens agorafobiske frykter åpne plasser.
  4. Arachibutyrofobi er frykten for at peanøttsmør skal sitte fast i ganen din.

I møte med sin frykt kan den fobiske oppleve hjertebank, tung pust, tørr munn, svette, svimmelhet eller ørhet. Dermed blir deres fobier virkelige for dem. Mens de fleste vil unnskylde sin personlige feil, gjenstår sannheten at denne angsten er grunnløs. Når vi godtar og imøtekommer bevaringen av vår person, er frykt uunngåelig. Disiplene fryktet at de holdt på å gå til grunne, og Kristus spurte dem hvorfor. Er det ikke bedre …å gå bort og være hos Kristus, for det er langt bedre – Filipperne 1:23. Hvis vi kan stole på Kristus med vårt liv, kan vi da ikke stole på ham med vår død?

For den som vil frelse sitt liv, skal miste det; men den som mister sitt liv for min skyld og for evangeliets skyld, han skal finne det igjen – Markus 8:35.

…Beskyttende vår eiendom

Utvendig var Kristi liv ett av de mest trengselsfulle som noen gang har blitt levd. Reven hadde sitt hi og fuglene sine reir, mens han la sin pute i akterenden av en gyngete båt som stønnende under uvær og tumultet fra de ustanselige bølgene som slo over den. Men hans indre havn var som et glasshav. Dette skyldtes delvis at han ingen eiendom hadde å beskytte. Selv båten var lånt. «Mye mynt, mye bekymring» sier det gamle ordtaket, og angst stiger når rikdom faller. Og en av mengden sa til ham: Mester, si til min bror at han skal dele arven med meg – Lukas 12:13. Jesus nektet å ta parti med ham. I stedet talte han til det begjærlige hjertet som forårsaket angsten. Hvis Kristus gir oss rikdom, trenger vi ikke å føle skyld. Hvis han tar den, trenger vi ikke å føle angst. Midt i stormen blir vi formanet …til å være ved godt mot; det skal ikke falle noe menneskes liv bort blant dere, men skuten skal bli borte – Apostlenes gjerninger 27:22. Dette ble gitt som helbredende balsam til de sjargne sjømenn, men for dem som er tilbøyelige til å beskytte sin eiendom er det en sørgelig saga. Da den rike unge mannen ble tilbudt frelse i bytte mot sin jordiske samling av skatter, …gikk han bort bedrøvet; for han hadde store eiendeler – Matteus 19:22. Vi som blir angstelige for tap av vår rikdom er ikke mindre tåpelige.

…Perfeksjonerende vår plan

Vi legger ut på et kurs. Kanskje vi skifter jobb, går inn i et forhold, eller begir oss ut på en ny tjenestevei. Vi har kastet oss ut i tro, og før vi vet ordet av det, strever vi. Livets vinder og bølger synes å arbeide mot oss. Vi har forventninger som ikke blir innfridd, og det virker som om Kristus ikke gjør sin del. Det er ikke Kristus, men våre forventninger som er årsaken til vår angst. Vi forventer mye av våre investeringer, og det er nedslående å se våre anstrengelser gå tapt. Martas puls økte ved mangelen på hjelp hun fikk på kjøkkenet. Hennes frustrasjon steg mens hennes velplanlagte måltid forble uferdig. Hennes klage er ikke mindre anklagende enn disiplene mens de rodde på sjøen. …Herre, bryr du deg ikke om at min søster har latt meg tjene alene? Si derfor til henne at hun skal hjelpe meg – Lukas 10:40. Hennes angst ble ikke forårsaket av Marias forsømmelse eller Kristi likegyldighet. Hennes søster var ført inn i hvilehavnen mens Marta kjempet med de tumultaktige følelsene i sitt hjerte. Slik skaper perfeksjonisten sin egen storm når hans uoppfylte visjon faller kort for hans forventninger. Men Kristus er mer opptatt av troende bryst enn av vannfylte båter.

…Behagelig for alle mennesker

Skriftene har lært oss godt å elske vår neste som oss selv, men det innebærer ikke at vi må strebe etter deres godkjennelse. Det føles fantastisk å bli likt. Det gjør vondt å bli avvist. Så mange sjeler bruker sine våkne timer på å søke andres godkjennelse. De må kle seg som, oppføre seg som, snakke som og leve som sine jevnaldrende. Disse lever et liv tungt lastet med stressende bølger av angst. Et virvar av «tenk om» kommer med hver ny bekjentskap. Det finnes ingen mer skjør skute enn et forhold. Uansett hvor stort offer vi gjør for å bli elsket, vil vi etter hvert møte en skuffende vindstøt som suger oss ned i fortvilelsens dyp. Når våre beste anstrengelser svikter oss og våre beste venner lar oss avspore, må vi føre vårt tilrakkede fartøy til hvilehavnen. Ubeleilige, uheldige, ubehagelige og irriterende relasjoner vil alltid eksistere. Vi gjør klokere i å unnskylde andres dårlige oppførsel mer enn vår egen. Når vi kan irettesette vindene som oppstår i våre egne sinn, vil vi straks finne oss selv ved det ønskede havnestedet.

Derfor gjenstår det en hvile for Guds folk. For den som er kommet inn i hans hvile, har også hvilt fra sine gjerninger, slik Gud hvilte fra sine. La oss derfor våke på, for at ingen av dere må mangle mål om å komme inn i den hvile – Hebreerne 4:9-11.
