This hymn is generally considered to be one of the greatest hymns ever written and is found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. It was written by a man who was frail in body, but strong in spirit. It was he who coined the phrase, “It is better to wear out than to rust out.” Let us now take a glimpse into the life of this servant of God.

Henry Francis Lyte, the author of this great and noteworthy hymn, was born June 1, 1793, in Ednam, near Kelso, Scotland. At a young age, he was left an orphan and was in comparative poverty. He was educated at Trinity College in Dublin, Ireland. It was there that his gift of poetry began to appear, winning him three prizes. His primary goal with his studies was to become a physician, instead, by the providence of God, he became a minister of the gospel of Jesus Christ.

One day in Cornwall, a fellow clergyman who was on his deathbed, requested that Lyte would come and give him some spiritual comfort. “To their mutual grief, they found themselves [both] groping for the light, veritable blind guides”. As they searched for truth and assurance of salvation, they fixed their faith on Christ, and Lyte came away from that sickroom a changed man, never to be the same again. It is said that it was his encounter with God at the bedside of that dying man that prompted Lyte’s noble hymn, “Jesus, I My Cross Have Taken.” In the year 1823, Henry F. Lyte took charge of a seashore parish, Lower Brixham, in Devonshire, England. It was at that place where he spent the last 23 years of his life toiling as a pastor for the spiritual good of the poor fishing people and the rough seafaring men of that region until his death in the fall of 1847. For all of Henry’s dedication and labor, he received a reward: having a Sunday school of several hundred scholars, as well as “a splendid company of seventy or eighty teachers, personally trained by him.”

Throughout his lifetime, his health was continually threatened by asthma and tuberculosis. Notwithstanding his physical frailties, he worked tirelessly with an established reputation as a poet, musician, and minister. Wherever he went, he was greatly loved and admired by his people. Toward the end of these later years, his health became gradually worse. So it was that during the winter months, he felt compelled to seek a warmer climate in Italy, which is a part of southern Europe.

Though he was greatly weakened by his sickness, on September 4, 1847, as Lyte was about to leave to head southward, he was arrested by an “irresistible desire” to preach once more to his congregation. He dearly loved these people and he had labored among them for so many years. “Against the protest of his amazed friends, he accomplished this purpose, and it is recorded that Lyte nearly had to crawl to the pulpit and his message came as from a dying man.” “O brethren,” he said, as he entered the familiar pulpit for the last time, “I stand here among you today, as alive from the dead, if I may hope to impress it upon you, and induce you to prepare for that solemn hour which must come to all, by a timely appreciation and dependance on the death of Christ.” These final words made a deep impact upon his congregation, after which he closed the service by administering the Lord’s Supper to his weeping people. Later that evening, after the service, he was inspired to “poetical composition” and wrote the eight stanzas of his last and greatest hymn:

Abide with me: fast falls the eventide;
The darkness deepens; Lord, with me abide:
when other helpers fail, and comforts flee,
Help of the helpless, O abide with me.

Swift to its close ebbs out life’s little day;
Earth’s joys grow dim, its glories pass away;
Change and decay in all around I see;
O Thou who changest not, abide with me.

Not a brief glance I beg, a passing word;
But, as Thou dwell’st with Thy disciples, Lord,
Familiar, condescending, patient, free,
Come, not to sojourn, but abide, with me.

Come not in terrors, as the King of kings;
But kind and good, with healing in Thy wings;
Tears for all woes, a heart for every plea;
Come, Friend of sinners, and thus ‘bide with me.

Thou on my head in early youth didst smile;
And, though rebellious and perverse meanwhile,
thou hast not left me, oft as I left thee:
On to the close, O Lord, abide with me.

I need Thy presence every passing hour;
What but Thy grace can foil the tempter’s power?
Who like Thyself my guide and stay can be?
Through cloud and sunshine, O abide with me.

I fear no foe, with Thee at hand to bless:
Ills have no weight, and tears no bitterness.
Where is death’s sting? Where, grave, thy victory?
I triumph still, if Thou abide with me.

Hold Thou Thy cross before my closing eyes;
Shine through the gloom, and point me to the skies;
Heaven’s morning breaks, and earth’s vain shadows flee:
In life, in death, O Lord, abide with me.

This hymn he gave to one of the family members that very night. Leaving the following day, he began his trek to Rome, Italy, hoping to gain some relief from his sickness. Lyte make it as far as Nice, France where his sickness prevented his further travel. He passed away soon after the age of 55, on November 20, 1847. His last words were “Joy! Peace!”

The scene behind this hymn is that of the resurrected Christ Jesus walking on the road to Emmaus with two of His somewhat sad and discouraged disciples. As they neared the end of their seven-mile walk and approached the village where they were going, Jesus …made as though he would have gone further. But they constrained him, saying, Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them –Luke 24:28-29.

We can draw a parallel between that scene and Henry F. Lyte’s own experience of drawing toward the close of his earthly journey. Thus, as the disciples besought the risen Lord to abide with them in the close of that ancient day, so was the meaning of this song written in the “shadows of death” to the hymn writer.

Lyte himself composed a tune for this hymn on the same evening that he wrote it, but it never became widely used. However, the tune universally used was written fourteen years later by William Henry Monk, a noted London musician, and editor of the well-known Anglican hymnal, Hymns Ancient and Modern. He included this song in his first edition, which was published in 1861.

In all, William H. Monk composed 50 tunes for the hymnal. It is said that Monk, being “inspired by the beauty of a glorious sunset while yet experiencing a deep personal sorrow,” composed (in only 10 minutes) the tune, Eventide, for the song, “Abide With Me, Fast Falls The Eventide”. William Monk also wrote the music for other familiar hymns such as “Look, Ye Saints! The Sight Is Glorious”, and “The Strife Is O’er”.

To summarize, Henry Lyte experienced many sorrows during his lifetime. Both of his parents died at an early age leaving him an orphan. And his own sickness and frailty caused him to be in ongoing danger of asthma and tuberculosis. Yet, in spite of all his trials, we find in him a resilient spirit to reach out to others; to touch and minister the Gospel to those poor people among whom he lived. “In no other writer,” says Dr. Breed (in the Treasury of Hymn Stories), “are poetry and religion more exquisitely united.”

Questo inno è generalmente considerato uno dei più grandi mai scritti e si trova in quasi ogni inno­la­rio o raccolta di inni pubblicata oggi. Fu scritto da un uomo fragile di corpo, ma forte nello spirito. Fu lui a coniare la frase: “È meglio consumarsi che arrugginirsi.” Volgiamo ora uno sguardo alla vita di questo servo di Dio.

Henry Francis Lyte, l'autore di questo grande e notevole inno, nacque il 1° giugno 1793 a Ednam, vicino a Kelso, in Scozia. In giovane età rimase orfano e visse in relativa povertà. Fu educato al Trinity College di Dublino, in Irlanda. Fu lì che il suo dono per la poesia cominciò ad apparire, guadagnandogli tre premi. Il suo obiettivo primario negli studi era diventare medico; invece, per provvidenza di Dio, divenne ministro del vangelo di Gesù Cristo.

Un giorno in Cornovaglia, un collega ecclesiastico gravemente malato sul letto di morte chiese che Lyte venisse a confortarlo spiritualmente. “Alla loro comune tristezza, si ritrovarono [entrambi] a tentare di trovare la luce, veri guide cieche”. Mentre cercavano la verità e l'assicurazione della salvezza, fissarono la loro fede in Cristo, e Lyte uscì da quella camera di malato un uomo trasformato, mai più lo stesso. Si dice che fu il suo incontro con Dio al capezzale di quell'uomo morente a spingere Lyte al nobile inno, “Jesus, I My Cross Have Taken.” Nell'anno 1823, Henry F. Lyte assunse la cura di una parrocchia sulla costa, Lower Brixham, nel Devonshire, in Inghilterra. Fu in quel luogo che trascorse gli ultimi 23 anni della sua vita faticando come pastore per il bene spirituale dei poveri pescatori e degli uomini di mare rudi di quella regione fino alla sua morte nell'autunno del 1847. Per tutta la dedizione e il lavoro di Henry, ricevette una ricompensa: avere una scuola domenicale di diverse centinaia di scolari, oltre a “una splendida compagnia di settanta o ottanta insegnanti, formati personalmente da lui.”

Per tutta la vita la sua salute fu continuamente minacciata dall'asma e dalla tubercolosi. Nonostante le sue fragilità fisiche, lavorò instancabilmente con una consolidata reputazione di poeta, musicista e ministro. Ovunque andasse, era molto amato e ammirato dalla sua gente. Verso la fine di quegli ultimi anni, la sua salute peggiorò gradualmente. Così, durante i mesi invernali, si sentì costretto a cercare un clima più caldo in Italia, che si trova nell'Europa meridionale.

Pur essendo fortemente indebolito dalla malattia, il 4 settembre 1847, mentre Lyte stava per partire verso sud, fu preso da un “irresistibile desiderio” di predicare ancora una volta alla sua congregazione. Amava profondamente quelle persone e aveva lavorato tra loro per tanti anni. “Contro il protesto dei suoi amici sbalorditi, egli portò a compimento questo scopo, e si narra che Lyte dovette quasi strisciare fino al pulpito e il suo messaggio venne come da un uomo morente.” “O fratelli,” disse, entrando nel pulpito a lui familiare per l'ultima volta, “io sto qui oggi in mezzo a voi, come vivo dai morti, se posso sperare di imprimervelo e indurvi a prepararvi per quell'ora solenne che deve venire per tutti, mediante una tempestiva apprezzamento e dipendenza dalla morte di Cristo.” Queste ultime parole produssero un profondo impatto sulla sua congregazione, dopo le quali chiuse il servizio amministrando la Cena del Signore al suo popolo in lacrime. Più tardi quella sera, dopo il servizio, fu ispirato a una “composizione poetica” e scrisse le otto strofe del suo ultimo e più grande inno:

Resta con me: rapido cala il vespro;
L'oscurità si fa più profonda; Signore, resta con me:
quando altri soccorritori mancano, e i conforti fuggono,
Aiuto degli impotenti, o resta con me.

Presto giunge alla fine il piccolo giorno della vita;
Le gioie della terra si affievoliscono, le sue glorie svaniscono;
Vedo mutazione e decadenza tutt'intorno;
O Tu che non cambi, resta con me.

Non chiedo un fugace sguardo, una parola di passaggio;
Ma, come Tu dimoravi con i tuoi discepoli, Signore,
Familiare, condiscendente, paziente, libero,
Vieni, non per soggiornare, ma resta con me.

Non venire con terrori, come Re dei re;
Ma gentile e buono, con guarigione nelle Tue ali;
Lacrime per ogni afflizione, un cuore per ogni supplica;
Vieni, Amico dei peccatori, e così resta con me.

A me hai sorriso sulla fronte nella prima giovinezza;
E, benché ribelle e perverso nel frattempo,
non mi hai abbandonato, tante volte come io Ti avevo abbandonato:
Fino alla fine, o Signore, resta con me.

Ho bisogno della Tua presenza in ogni ora che passa;
Che cosa se non la Tua grazia può fermare il potere del tentatore?
Chi, come Te, può essere la mia guida e il mio sostegno?
Tra nuvole e sole, o resta con me.

Non temo nemico, con Te a mano per benedire:
I mali non hanno peso, e le lacrime non hanno amarezza.
Dov'è il pungiglione della morte? Dov'è, tomba, la tua vittoria?
Io trionfo ancora, se Tu resti con me.

Tieniti Tu la Tua croce davanti ai miei occhi che si chiudono;
Fa' splendere attraverso l'oscurità, e indicami i cieli;
Si apre il mattino del cielo, e le vane ombre della terra fuggono:
Nella vita, nella morte, o Signore, resta con me.

Quell'inno lo donò a un membro della famiglia quella stessa notte. Il giorno seguente, partì per Roma, in Italia, sperando di trarre qualche sollievo dalla sua malattia. Lyte riuscì ad arrivare fino a Nizza, in Francia, dove la sua malattia gli impedì di proseguire il viaggio. Morì poco dopo all'età di circa 55 anni, il 20 novembre 1847. Le sue ultime parole furono “Gioia! Pace!”

Lo scenario dietro questo inno è quello di Cristo risorto che cammina sulla via di Emmaus con due dei Suoi discepoli alquanto tristi e scoraggiati. Mentre si avvicinavano alla fine della loro camminata di sette miglia e si accostavano al villaggio dove stavano andando, Gesù …fece come se volesse proseguire oltre. Ma lo costrinsero a restare, dicendo: “Resta con noi, perché si fa sera e il giorno è ormai al declino.” Ed egli entrò per fermarsi con loro – Luca 24:28-29.

Possiamo tracciare un parallelo tra quella scena e l'esperienza di Henry F. Lyte che si avvicinava alla fine del suo viaggio terreno. Così, come i discepoli implorarono il Signore risorto di restare con loro al termine di quel giorno antico, così fu il significato di questa canzone scritta “nell'ombra della morte” per il cantore dell'inno.

Lyte stesso compose una melodia per questo inno la stessa sera in cui lo scrisse, ma non divenne mai ampiamente usata. Tuttavia, la melodia universalmente usata fu composta quattordici anni dopo da William Henry Monk, un noto musicista londinese ed editore del ben noto inno­lario anglicano, Hymns Ancient and Modern. Egli incluse questo canto nella sua prima edizione, pubblicata nel 1861.

In totale, William H. Monk compose 50 melodie per l'inno­lario. Si dice che Monk, essendo “ispirato dalla bellezza di un glorioso tramonto mentre al contempo sperimentava un profondo dolore personale,” compose (in soli 10 minuti) la melodia, Eventide, per il canto “Abide With Me, Fast Falls The Eventide”. William Monk scrisse anche la musica per altri inni familiari come “Look, Ye Saints! The Sight Is Glorious” e “The Strife Is O'er”.

Per riassumere, Henry Lyte sperimentò molte sventure durante la sua vita. Entrambi i suoi genitori morirono in giovane età lasciandolo orfano. E la sua stessa malattia e fragilità lo posero in continuo pericolo di asma e tubercolosi. Eppure, nonostante tutte le sue prove, troviamo in lui uno spirito resiliente che si protese verso gli altri; per toccare e ministere il Vangelo a quelle povera persone tra cui viveva. “In nessun altro scrittore,” dice il dott. Breed (in Treasury of Hymn Stories), “poesia e religione sono più squisitamente unite.”

Compositore - William Henry Monk, 1823-1889

As a child, you might think you can’t make a difference in the lives of people around you, but that is not true! Your little acts of kindness will not soon be forgotten. Being a true friend to someone who is hurting can change that person’s life forever.

This is the true story of “Hadassah” (not her real name) a young girl who was very much looking forward to starting school. Once she started first grade, what a disappointment it was to find that the second-grade girls were ready for someone to be mean to, or so it seemed. Maybe it would have been better if Hadassah had stood up to them, but she didn’t. Instead, she chose to act as if it didn’t hurt and tried to ignore them. Some days were better than others, but sadly this went on for three or four years.

Sure, there were good times too, but many evenings she walked home from school, crying most of the way and wishing that she wouldn’t need to go back to school the next day!

One day, one of the girls lost her pen. She was sure that Hadassah had stolen it. This was very disturbing to a very conscientious Hadassah. At the next recess she was blamed for cheating on her flash cards. Many other made-up stories were also passed around among the girls.

However, there was one little girl in that second-grade group of girls whose name we’ll say was “Esther”. She was Hadassah’s best friend and supported her all through those difficult years.

Esther was a very gentle, sweet girl, which is mostly what Hadassah remembered her for. Esther had cystic fibrosis and in the 1970s they didn’t have as many treatment options available for that disease as they do now, so those patients usually died very young. As Esther’s sickness became worse, the days that she felt well enough to be in school were rare. Since Esther was well-liked, the days when she was in school were special to everyone. Perhaps Esther realized she would be in heaven before the other girls—we don’t know for sure. But she taught the girls a song, “How Far Is Heaven”, which Hadassah still likes to sing today!

Hadassah still remembers seeing the emergency squad go past her house when they took Esther to the hospital for the last time. It was a very sad group of schoolgirls when Esther died at the age of 13. Esther had touched the hearts of many people in her short life, including the nurses who had cared for her during her stay in the hospital. Hadassah still remembers seeing some of the nurses crying at Esther’s funeral. Do you think Hadassah will ever forget Esther? Never!

Besides being her best friend, another bright spot for Hadassah was that when Esther was in school the other girls weren’t as mean to her (Hadassah). It so happened that in about the fourth grade, Esther was in school more often. One day she went home and told her parents what she was witnessing in school—how the other girls were against Hadassah and were being so mean to her. Esther’s father brought this problem up in the next parent/teacher meeting. What a night and day change started the very next day! One of the girls even came to Hadassah and apologized. Finally, they could all be friends and today those girls are Hadassah’s “old school friends”.

It’s worth it to stand beside someone who is being treated unkindly. Your support may be what God uses to help your friend to go through their hard times in a good way! And share it with your parents, they can help find a way to change the problem.

As kind mag jy dink jy kan nie ’n verskil maak in die lewens van mense om jou nie, maar dit is nie waar nie! Jou klein dade van vriendelikheid sal nie gou vergeet word nie. Om ’n ware vriend te wees vir iemand wat seergemaak is, kan daardie persoon se lewe vir altyd verander.

Dit is die ware verhaal van “Hadassah” (nie haar regte naam nie), ’n jong meisie wat baie uitsien om skool toe te begin. Sodra sy graad een begin het, wat ’n teleurstelling was om uit te vind dat die meisies in graad twee klaar was vir iemand om gemeen mee te wees, of dit het so gelyk. Miskien sou dit beter gewees het as Hadassah vir hulle opgestaan het, maar sy het dit nie gedoen nie. In plaas daarvan het sy besluit om op te tree asof dit haar nie seermaak nie en het probeer om hulle te ignoreer. Sommige dae was beter as ander, maar tragies genoeg het dit drie of vier jaar aangehou.

Natuurlik was daar ook goeie tye, maar baie aand het sy van die skool af huis toe gestap en die meeste van die pad gehuil en gewens sy hoef nie die volgende dag weer skool toe te gaan nie!

Eendag het een van die meisies haar pen verloor. Sy was seker Hadassah het dit gesteel. Dit was baie ontstellend vir ’n baie pligsgetroue Hadassah. By die volgende pouse is sy beskuldig van afknou by haar flitskaartjies. Nog baie ander aangemaakte stories is ook onder die meisies versprei.

Daar was egter een klein meisie in daardie groep meisies in graad twee wie se naam ons sal sê was “Esther”. Sy was Hadassah se beste vriendin en het haar deur daardie moeilike jare ondersteun.

Esther was ’n baie sagmoedige, lieflike meisie, wat meestal is wat Hadassah haar oor onthou het. Esther het fibrose gehad en in die 1970’s het hulle nie soveel behandelingsopsies vir daardie siekte gehad as wat daar nou is nie, so daardie pasiënte is gewoonlik baie jonk oorlede. Toe Esther se siekte erger geword het, was die dae waarop sy goed genoeg gevoel het om by die skool te wees skaars. Aangesien Esther gewild was, was die dae waarop sy by die skool was spesiaal vir almal. Miskien het Esther besef sy sal vroeër in die hemel wees as die ander meisies—ons weet dit nie seker nie. Maar sy het die meisies ’n lied geleer, "Hoe ver is die hemel", wat Hadassah vandag nog graag sing!

Hadassah onthou nog dat sy die noodspan sien verbygaan het by haar huis toe hulle Esther die laaste keer hospitaal toe geneem het. Dit was ’n baie droewige groep skoolmeisies toe Esther op 13-jarige ouderdom oorlede is. Esther het in haar korte lewe die harte van baie mense geraak, insluitende die verpleegsters wat na haar omgesien het tydens haar hospitaalverblyf. Hadassah onthou nog dat sy sommige van die verpleegsters by Esther se begrafnis huil sien. Dink jy Hadassah sal ooit Esther vergeet? Nooit!

Behalwe dat sy haar beste vriendin was, was nog ’n helder plekkie vir Hadassah dat wanneer Esther by die skool was die ander meisies nie so gemeen teenoor haar (Hadassah) was nie. Dit het gebeur dat ongeveer in graad vier Esther meer gereeld by die skool was. Eendag het sy huis toe gegaan en vir haar ouers vertel wat sy by die skool sien—hoe die ander meisies teen Hadassah was en so gemeen met haar optree. Esther se pa het hierdie probleem by die volgende ouer/onderwyser-vergadering ter sprake gebring. Wat ’n dag-en-nag verandering het die volgende dag begin! Een van die meisies het selfs na Hadassah toe gekom en verskoning aangebied. Uiteindelik kon hulle almal vriende wees en vandag is daardie meisies Hadassah se “ou skoolvriende”.

Dit is die moeite werd om langs iemand te staan wat sleg behandel word. Jou ondersteuning mag wees wat God gebruik om jou vriend te help om deur hulle moeilike tye op ’n goeie manier te kom! En deel dit met jou ouers, hulle kan help om ’n manier te vind om die probleem te verander.

    In the last couple of years, something that God has been working on in my heart is the area of submission. I don’t want to look back in a wrong way, but I see where I have failed my husband in the role that God has given for me to function as his helper, one that is meet for him. As I have been thinking about my own life, I have come to realize how important our role is as Christian women, in our homes and in the lives of our children.

    I realize that our children are going to need to make their own decision when it comes to being a disciple of Christ, but my desire is that I am not the reason that our children rebel against the Word of God. When we honor our husbands the way that God has taught in His Word, the example of our lives will draw the unbelieving to Christ. In the flesh, we will not be able to honor our husbands in a way that will bring glory to God, but with Christ we can do all things according to His will.

    I have a burden about this because in the last couple of months I have noticed how much our homes are under constant attack from the enemy of our souls, as he tries to use our flesh and the world. As I write on this, I don’t feel that I will do justice to it, so I will just write some of my thoughts and pray that all who read this article will be encouraged in their marriages to honor, respect, and love their husbands.

    • Nevertheless let … the wife see that she reverence her husband –Ephesians 5:33.
    • Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands… –1 Peter 3:1.
    • Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are… –1 Peter 3:6.
    • Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord –Ephesians 5:22.
    • But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God –1 Corinthians 11:3.
    • Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection. But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence. For Adam was first formed, then Eve. And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression –1 Timothy 2:11-14.
    • Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be [subject] to their own husbands in every thing –Ephesians 5:24.
    • Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law –1 Corinthians 14:34.

    These Scriptures are not my own, but God’s. He gives us His Word to read and to live by because that is the only way we will be able to have peace and harmony in our homes. Even more importantly, the ONLY way that we can have a clear conscience before God is when we are in the center of His will.

    When we think of submission, what comes to mind? Do we think that if we submit, we will be taken advantage of? Do we think that we are wiser than our husbands? I know to the flesh this sounds kind of hard, but if we could only realize that if we don’t allow our husbands to lead out and make decisions, we are only crippling them. The reality is that if our husbands make mistakes, it is okay because we ourselves make mistakes as well. Also, if we are born again, and we are walking with God, but our husbands are not, God will still take care of us. The Scriptures teach that if our husband is not in his place, then through the wife walking according to the clear teaching that God has given her in His Word, the husband can be won through her conversation (or by the way she conducts her life).

    We need to trust God with our whole lives, even in the area of our marriage. God is a God of order. Think of how God desires the children to honor the parents and the parents to not provoke their children to anger; it’s no different in the husband-and-wife relationship. The husband is to love his wife as Christ loves the church, and the wife is to reverence her husband.

    In the beginning, God created male and female. He created Adam and said that it was not good for man to be alone; then He created woman from the rib of Adam’s side. God’s heart in the beginning was that man and woman would be one, and together they would walk with God and glorify Him. Then through Adam and Eve yielding to temptation, sin was brought into the world. Whenever we are struggling in our marriage, I am reminded how it was Eve that first yielded to the serpent’s temptation. Let us as wives be quick to examine our own hearts to be sure that we are in our place. When situations arise, how often are we as women tempted to think that we know better and could handle the situation better than our husbands.

    God has designed our husbands to be our protector if we stay under them. I realize that we are imperfect, and that makes it more challenging to submit to our husbands. However, I believe that when we are born again by the Spirit of God, His love in us enables us to submit to our husbands. I also realize that there are a lot of broken homes. My encouragement to anyone who is in a less than ideal situation is to sincerely pray…first for yourself that you can walk in a blameless way and also for your husband that he would be what God has designed him to be—not what you think he should be. Many times, we get confused about this and it causes us to have bad thoughts about our husbands.

    Titus gives us sisters clear direction from God. The aged women likewise, that they be … teachers of good things; That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed –Titus 2:3-5.

    Another temptation that we women face is to compare our husbands with other men. Perhaps we tell our husbands that this other man wouldn’t do such and such the way you do, or the way he does something is better than the way you do. Maybe we don’t even say these words, but our actions can tell our husbands a lot. God’s Word teaches us to be obedient to our own husbands, and not another. Each husband is gifted in a different way, and that is why each wife is especially suited for their husband. And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help [helper, aid, supporter] meet [suitable, appropriate, complementary] for him –Genesis 2:18.

    That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children –Titus 2:4. The word “love,” in to love their husbands means “to be affectionately fond of their man” as compared to the word “love” in to love their children which means “to have a maternal fondness for one’s children”. What kind of love are we showing our husbands? Can our husbands trust us that we only have their good in mind, or do we pretend to love in order to get something in return? True love will forgive in spite of failures, even when we think the pain is too great to bear. True love will cause us to pray for ourselves and our husbands when we feel differently about something than they do. True love will not cause us to despair, rather it will cause us to seek God even more.

    When we are tempted to speak about our husbands’ faults to others, let us not yield to that temptation but let’s pray for them. Would we appreciate our husbands talking about our faults to other people? Also, pray for discernment to know if, and when, to speak to someone about a sin that your husband may be involved in. Let us not rail on or nag our husbands when difficulties arise. Instead, let us ask God to work in our lives and give the problem to Him and let it there. Our husbands are only too human, just as we are. If we fail at times, then we must not be surprised that they too might fail at times as well. I think what makes our marriages perfect is that we learn to forgive one another and press on to be one together.

    Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation [conduct] of the wives; While they behold your chaste [modest, innocent, perfect, pure] conversation coupled with fear. Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement [terror]. Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered –1 Peter 3:1-2 & 3:6-7.

    One of the first times that this verse became real to us was when our first child was around five months old. We were quite a ways from home and he started crying with a lot of pain. We prayed for him, but he still cried. We could not figure out what was wrong, so we took him into the ER. They told us that he had an ear infection and gave us medication. However, he still cried. We had a ten-hour journey home, and he cried the whole way. After we had gotten home, my husband and I discovered that there were some unresolved things between us. After we confessed our wrongs to each other and to God, we prayed again for our son. Immediately after we prayed, our son quit crying. I know not every situation turns out like this one did, but God taught us that we need to be open with each other with no hidden sin, that our prayers be not hindered.

    Some questions that could be asked are: What are our children seeing in our homes? Do they see Mom reverencing their dad with joy or with fear? Do they see Mom being appropriately affectionate with her husband, such as through kind words, seeking to love the things that he loves, holding hands, etc. (I have come to realize that it is difficult to hold hands with my husband if there is something between us.) Does Mom question, challenge, or criticize what Dad does?

    As our own children are growing older and into their youth years, I see how important it is that these principles are lived out in our homes. If we openly question our husband’s authority, I believe we are sowing a seed in our children that they too will question their dad’s authority. Ultimately, in the time that we live, we are seeing a generation that is questioning everything about God’s created order—there is gender confusion, evolution, and rebellion against authority in general. I have often wondered if perhaps the reason that we see so much rebellion in our plain churches is because of God’s order not being lived out in our homes.

    There was a friend of ours who told us that if there would be one Christian principle that he thought would have the most impact on the home, it would be the principle of the headship order. We have a dear friend who had become a Christian before her husband. She went through a lot of difficult times, but she continued to love and reverence her husband. She fasted and prayed for many years for her husband. Today her husband will testify that it was because of his wife’s godly conduct that drew him to repentance and faith in Christ.

    Another example with a different outcome… I know of a couple that didn’t have a solid marriage. The husband was not in his place and the wife became bitter, so bitter in fact, that she said that when she is buried in the grave, she doesn’t want to be buried beside her husband. This much bitterness has had a terrible effect on their children. I wondered if she had not become bitter, if she could have at least spared her children from the many heartaches that they have suffered.

    I also know of another couple where both of them were badly mistreated by close family, but they chose not to become bitter. They drew closer to God and to each other through those valleys and they are reaping the benefits of the fruit of their choices to this day.

    Even closer to home… I grew up in a home that was not a Christian home. Neither of my parents were born again. When they began to allow God to work in their hearts, I could see it. I would come home from gatherings and see my dad weeping as he was reading his Bible. Also, on one particular evening I came home and saw my parents sitting at the table and they were singing together. I will testify that this had a tremendous effect on my life. I could also see my own mother desiring to be in her place as God had designed her to be. When we pass from this life, what will our family say about us? Will they testify that the love of God reigned in our mortal bodies?

    On a practical note, I thought I would write a few ways that we can show that we love our husbands in deed and not just in word.

    • Asking them for advice (not just going on what we think)
    • Fixing their favorite foods
    • Keeping the house orderly and neat
    • Being ready and willing to drop our plans to help our husbands with whatever they need
    • Meeting them at the door with a smile (no matter how bad of day we may have had)
    • Keeping the house quiet, even with little children, when he’s trying to rest or study
    • Teaching our children proper manners in relating to each other in the home
    • Teaching our children to love and respect their father, even if he isn’t always perfect

    Another challenge I wish to give to each married sister is to think of something that you can tell your husband that you are blessed about with him, Try doing this every day for two weeks. It’s amazing what effect kindness can have on a marriage. Maybe to some this would seem like drudgery, but it’s not. I am amazed that as we get older, how much we think alike, even sometimes finishing each other’s sentences. I realize there is so much more that could have been written. I trust that God will continue to open His Word to us as we seek Him.

    Editor’s Note:

    I was one who struggled majorly and for years with not knowing how to submit and yet wanting to. Following is my attempt to share what God has been teaching me.

    One of the main reasons that many people struggle with “submission” is that they don’t really understand what God means with the subject—they don’t understand the reality of biblical submission. Usually, a person knows what they believe on a certain subject, so in their mind when they are being asked to “submit” on that point, they think they are being asked to compromise their personal belief—or sin against their conscience.

    The answer is two-fold.

    First, if two people agree on an issue, then there is no need for anyone to submit. Thus, to submit does not mean that the person submitting is necessarily changing their mind, rather they are choosing to support the other person’s decision based on the fact that God says that that person is the one He is holding responsible for the decisions of that party—whether it be a couple, the home, a school, a church, etc.

    Second, God knew that whenever there would be more than one person discussing a decision that needs to be made, that it would always mean that the one would end up submitting to the other. Therefore, to provide clarity in responsibility, He gives clear direction regarding whom He considers the responsible person (the spiritual authority) in each type of situation—the husband in a marriage, the father in the family, the man (the head) in the home, the ordained leaders in the church, the schoolteachers/principal in the school setting, etc. That way everyone can know who God sees as responsible for any mistakes that are made.

    Consider that even though Eve took the fruit and ate it first, and then gave it to her husband to eat, God provides us with clarity regarding who He holds responsible for that failure (sin). Wherefore, as by one man [not one woman] sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned … Nevertheless death reigned from Adam [not from Eve] to Moses, even over them [Adam’s descendants—all of the human race] that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam’s transgression… –Romans 5:12-14.

    So, we see that God provides protection and security to all those who are under authority if they stay under that authority. The one who God clearly states as being the authority figure in each relationship will always be the one that God holds responsible for decisions made by that group of people. Just like in the fall in the Garden of Eden, sins of omission and of commission within each family will be primarily held to dad’s account. Whether dad was giving wrong direction to the family or if he was not giving direction at all, it doesn’t matter, he will still be held to account since God sees the man as being the head of his home. (see 1 Corinthians 11:3 and Romans 13:12)

    I løpet av de siste par årene har noe Gud har arbeidet med i mitt hjerte vært området underordning. Jeg vil ikke se tilbake på en feil måte, men jeg ser hvor jeg har sviktet min ektemann i den rollen Gud har gitt meg for å være hans hjelper, en som er passende for ham. Når jeg har tenkt over mitt eget liv, har jeg kommet til å innse hvor viktig vår rolle er som kristne kvinner, i våre hjem og i våre barns liv.

    Jeg innser at barna våre må ta sitt eget valg når det gjelder å være en disippel av Kristus, men mitt ønske er at jeg ikke skal være grunnen til at våre barn gjør opprør mot Guds Ord. Når vi ærer våre ektemenn slik Gud har lært i Sitt Ord, vil vårt livs eksempel trekke de uomvendte til Kristus. I kjødet vil vi ikke være i stand til å ære våre ektemenn på en måte som bringer ære til Gud, men med Kristus kan vi gjøre alle ting i samsvar med Hans vilje.

    Jeg har en byrde over dette fordi jeg i løpet av de siste par månedene har lagt merke til hvor mye hjemmene våre er under konstant angrep fra sjelens fiende, ettersom han forsøker å bruke vårt kjød og verden. Når jeg skriver om dette, føler jeg ikke at jeg vil gjøre det rettferdig, så jeg vil bare skrive noen av mine tanker og be om at alle som leser denne artikkelen blir oppmuntret i ekteskapene sine til å ære, respektere og elske sine ektemenn.

    • Nevertheless let … the wife see that she reverence her husband –Efeserne 5:33.

    Disse skriftstedene er ikke mine, men Guds. Han gir oss Sitt Ord for å lese og leve etter fordi det er den eneste måten vi kan ha fred og harmoni i våre hjem på. Enda viktigere, den ENESTE måten vi kan ha en klar samvittighet foran Gud på er når vi er i sentrum av Hans vilje.

    Når vi tenker på underordning, hva kommer til tankene? Tenker vi at hvis vi underordner oss, vil vi bli utnyttet? Tenker vi at vi er klokere enn våre ektemenn? Jeg vet at dette i kjødet høres ganske hardt ut, men om vi bare kunne innse at hvis vi ikke lar våre ektemenn lede og ta avgjørelser, så lammer vi dem bare. Realiteten er at om våre ektemenn gjør feil, er det greit fordi vi selv også gjør feil. Også, om vi er gjenfødte og vandrer med Gud, men våre ektemenn ikke er det, vil Gud fortsatt ta seg av oss. Skriftene lærer at om vår ektemann ikke er i sin plass, så gjennom at hustruen går etter den klare læren Gud har gitt henne i Sitt Ord, kan ektemannen vinnes gjennom hennes oppførsel (eller ved måten hun fører sitt liv på).

    Vi må stole på Gud med hele livet vårt, også på ekteskapets område. Gud er en Gud av orden. Tenk på hvordan Gud ønsker at barna skal ære foreldrene og foreldrene ikke skal opphisse barna sine til vrede; det er ikke annerledes i ektemann- og koneforholdet. Ektemannen skal elske sin kone som Kristus elsker kirken, og konen skal ære sin ektemann.

    I begynnelsen skapte Gud mann og kvinne. Han skapte Adam og sa at det ikke var godt for mennesket å være alene; så skapte Han kvinnen av Adams ribben. Guds hjerte i begynnelsen var at mann og kvinne skulle være ett, og sammen skulle de vandre med Gud og ære Ham. Så ved at Adam og Eva ga etter for fristelsen, kom synden inn i verden. Når vi sliter i vårt ekteskap, blir jeg minnet om at det var Eva som først gav etter for slangens fristelse. La oss som koner være raske til å undersøke våre egne hjerter for å være sikre på at vi er i vår plass. Når situasjoner oppstår, hvor ofte blir vi som kvinner fristet til å tro at vi vet bedre og kunne håndtert situasjonen bedre enn våre ektemenn.

    Gud har utformet våre ektemenn til å være våre beskyttere dersom vi blir under dem. Jeg innser at vi er ufullkomne, og det gjør det mer utfordrende å underordne oss våre ektemenn. Likevel tror jeg at når vi blir gjenfødt ved Guds Ånd, gjør Hans kjærlighet i oss oss i stand til å underordne oss våre ektemenn. Jeg innser også at det finnes mange knuste hjem. Min oppmuntring til enhver som er i en mindre enn ideell situasjon er å be oppriktig… først for deg selv at du kan vandre på en ubesmittet måte og også for din ektemann at han må bli det Gud har skapt ham til å være — ikke det du mener han burde være. Mange ganger blir vi forvirret om dette og det fører oss til å få dårlige tanker om våre ektemenn.

    Titus gir oss søstre klar retning fra Gud. The aged women likewise, that they be … teachers of good things; That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed –Titus 2:3-5.

    En annen fristelse vi kvinner møter er å sammenligne våre ektemenn med andre menn. Kanskje sier vi til våre ektemenn at denne andre mannen ikke ville gjort slik eller slik slik du gjør, eller at måten han gjør noe på er bedre enn måten du gjør det på. Kanskje sier vi ikke disse ordene, men våre handlinger kan fortelle våre ektemenn mye. Guds Ord lærer oss å være lydige mot våre egne ektemenn, ikke en annen. Hver ektemann er gitt forskjellige gaver, og derfor er hver kone spesielt egnet for sin ektemann. And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help [helper, aid, supporter] meet [suitable, appropriate, complementary] for him –1. Mosebok 2:18.

    That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children –Titus 2:4. Ordet «love» i to love their husbands betyr «å være hengivent glad i sin mann» sammenlignet med ordet «love» i to love their children som betyr «å ha en moderlig hengivenhet for sine barn». Hvilken slags kjærlighet viser vi våre ektemenn? Kan våre ektemenn stole på at vi bare ønsker deres beste, eller later vi til å elske for å få noe igjen? Sann kjærlighet vil tilgi til tross for feil, selv når vi tror smerten er for stor å bære. Sann kjærlighet vil få oss til å be for oss selv og våre ektemenn når vi føler annerledes om noe enn de gjør. Sann kjærlighet vil ikke få oss til å fortvile, men vil føre oss til å søke Gud enda mer.

    Når vi blir fristet til å snakke om våre ektemenns feil til andre, la oss ikke gi etter for den fristelsen, men la oss be for dem. Ville vi sette pris på at våre ektemenn snakket om våre feil til andre? Be også om skjelneevne for å vite om, og når, du bør snakke med noen om en synd din ektemann kan være involvert i. La oss ikke skjelle ut eller pese på våre ektemenn når vanskeligheter oppstår. I stedet, la oss be Gud om å virke i våre liv og gi problemet til Ham og la det være der. Våre ektemenn er like menneskelige som vi er. Om vi feiler noen ganger, må vi ikke bli overrasket om de også feiler noen ganger. Jeg tror det som gjør ekteskapene våre fullkomne er at vi lærer å tilgi hverandre og fortsette framover for å være ett sammen.

    Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation [conduct] of the wives; While they behold your chaste [modest, innocent, perfect, pure] conversation coupled with fear. Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement [terror]. Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered –1. Peter 3:1-2 & 3:6-7.

    En av de første gangene dette verset ble virkelig for oss var da vårt første barn var rundt fem måneder gammel. Vi var temmelig langt hjemmefra og han begynte å gråte med mye smerte. Vi ba for ham, men han gråt fortsatt. Vi kunne ikke finne ut hva som var galt, så vi tok ham med på legevakten. De sa at han hadde en ørebetennelse og ga oss medisin. Likevel gråt han fortsatt. Vi hadde en ti timers reise hjem, og han gråt hele veien. Etter at vi kom hjem, oppdaget min mann og jeg at det var noen uløste ting mellom oss. Etter at vi tilsto våre feil for hverandre og for Gud, ba vi igjen for vår sønn. Umiddelbart etter at vi ba, sluttet vår sønn å gråte. Jeg vet ikke at alle situasjoner ender slik som denne gjorde, men Gud lærte oss at vi trenger å være åpne med hverandre uten skjult synd, slik at våre bønner ikke blir hindret.

    Noen spørsmål som kan stilles er: Hva ser barna våre i hjemmene våre? Ser de at mor ærer far med glede eller med frykt? Ser de at mor er passende hengiven med sin ektemann, for eksempel gjennom milde ord, ved å søke å elske de tingene han elsker, holde hender osv. (Jeg har kommet til å innse at det er vanskelig å holde hender med min ektemann hvis det er noe mellom oss.) Spør mor, utfordrer eller kritiserer hun det far gjør?

    Ettersom våre egne barn blir eldre og inn i ungdomsårene, ser jeg hvor viktig det er at disse prinsippene leves ut i våre hjem. Hvis vi åpent utfordrer vår ektemanns autoritet, tror jeg vi sår et frø i barna våre om at de også vil utfordre sin fars autoritet. Til syvende og sist, i den tiden vi lever i, ser vi en generasjon som stiller spørsmål ved alt som gjelder Guds skapte orden — det finnes kjønnsforvirring, evolusjon og opprør mot autoritet generelt. Jeg har ofte lurt på om kanskje grunnen til at vi ser så mye opprør i våre plain-kirker er på grunn av at Guds orden ikke leves ut i våre hjem.

    En venn av oss sa at om det skulle være ett kristent prinsipp som han mente ville ha størst innvirkning på hjemmet, ville det være prinsippet om overhodeordenen. Vi har en kjær venn som ble kristen før sin ektemann. Hun gikk gjennom mange vanskelige tider, men hun fortsatte å elske og ære sin ektemann. Hun fastet og ba i mange år for sin ektemann. I dag vil hennes ektemann vitne om at det var på grunn av hans kones gudfryktige oppførsel at han ble dratt til omvendelse og tro på Kristus.

    Et annet eksempel med et annet utfall… Jeg kjenner et par som ikke hadde et solid ekteskap. Ektemannen var ikke i sin plass og konen ble bitter, så bitter faktisk at hun sa at når hun blir begravet vil hun ikke bli lagt ved siden av sin ektemann. Så mye bitterhet har hatt en forferdelig effekt på deres barn. Jeg undret på om hun ikke hadde blitt bitter, om hun i det minste kunne ha spart barna sine for de mange hjertesorgene de har lidd.

    Jeg kjenner også til et annet par hvor begge ble dårlig behandlet av nær familie, men de valgte å ikke bli bitre. De kom nærmere Gud og hverandre gjennom disse dalene og høster fruktene av valgene sine den dag i dag.

    Enda nærmere hjemmet… Jeg vokste opp i et hjem som ikke var et kristent hjem. Ingen av foreldrene mine var gjenfødte. Når de begynte å la Gud virke i deres hjerter, kunne jeg se det. Jeg kom hjem fra samlinger og så min far gråte mens han leste i Bibelen. Også en spesiell kveld kom jeg hjem og så foreldrene mine sitte ved bordet og de sang sammen. Jeg vil vitne at dette hadde en enorm effekt på mitt liv. Jeg kunne også se at min egen mor ønsket å være i sin plass slik Gud hadde designet henne å være. Når vi går bort fra dette livet, hva vil vår familie si om oss? Vil de vitne at Guds kjærlighet rådet i våre dødelige legemer?

    På en praktisk merknad tenkte jeg å skrive noen måter vi kan vise at vi elsker våre ektemenn i gjerning og ikke bare i ord.

    • Spørre dem om råd (ikke bare gjøre det vi selv mener)
    • Lage deres favorittmat
    • Holde huset ryddig og pent
    • Være beredt og villig til å droppe våre planer for å hjelpe våre ektemenn med hva de enn trenger
    • Møte dem i døren med et smil (uansett hvor dårlig dag vi måtte ha hatt)
    • Holde huset stille, selv med små barn, når han prøver å hvile eller studere
    • Lære våre barn korrekt oppførsel i forhold til hverandre hjemme
    • Lære våre barn å elske og respektere sin far, selv om han ikke alltid er perfekt

    En annen utfordring jeg ønsker å gi hver gift søster er å tenke på noe du kan si til din ektemann som du føler deg velsignet ved med ham. Prøv å gjøre dette hver dag i to uker. Det er forbløffende hvilken effekt vennlighet kan ha på et ekteskap. Kanskje virker dette for noen som pliktarbeid, men det er det ikke. Jeg er forundret over at når vi blir eldre, hvor mye vi tenker likt, noen ganger fullfører hverandres setninger. Jeg innser at det er så mye mer som kunne vært skrevet. Jeg stoler på at Gud vil fortsette å åpne Sitt Ord for oss når vi søker Ham.

    Redaktørens merknad:

    Jeg var en som slet stort og i mange år med å ikke vite hvordan jeg skulle underordne meg, men som likevel ønsket det. Følgende er mitt forsøk på å dele hva Gud har lært meg.

    En av hovedgrunnene til at mange sliter med «underordning» er at de virkelig ikke forstår hva Gud mener med emnet—de forstår ikke realiteten av bibelsk underordning. Vanligvis vet en person hva de tror om et bestemt tema, så i deres sinn når de blir bedt om å «underordne seg» i det punktet, tror de at de blir bedt om å kompromittere sin personlige tro—eller synde mot sin samvittighet.

    Svaret er todelt.

    For det første, om to mennesker er enige om en sak, er det ingen grunn for noen å underordne seg. Dermed betyr det å underordne seg ikke nødvendigvis at den som underordner seg endrer mening, snarere velger de å støtte den andre personens beslutning basert på det faktum at Gud sier at den personen er den Han holder ansvarlig for avgjørelser for den parten—enten det er et par, hjemmet, en skole, en kirke osv.

    For det andre, Gud visste at når det ville være mer enn én person som diskuterte en beslutning som må tas, ville det alltid bety at den ene ender opp med å underordne seg den andre. Derfor, for å gi klarhet i ansvar, gir Han klar retning angående hvem Han anser som den ansvarlige personen (den åndelige autoriteten) i hver type situasjon—ektemannen i et ekteskap, faren i familien, mannen (hodet) i hjemmet, de ordinerte lederne i kirken, skolelærerne/rektoren i skolemiljøet osv. På den måten kan alle vite hvem Gud ser som ansvarlig for eventuelle feil som blir gjort.

    Tenk at selv om Eva tok frukten og spiste den først, og så ga den til sin ektemann å spise, gir Gud oss klarhet angående hvem Han holder ansvarlig for den feilen (synden). Wherefore, as by one man [not one woman] sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned … Nevertheless death reigned from Adam [not from Eve] to Moses, even over them [Adam’s descendants—all of the human race] that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam’s transgression… –Romerne 5:12-14.

    Så, vi ser at Gud gir beskyttelse og sikkerhet til alle som er under autoritet hvis de forblir under den autoriteten. Den som Gud klart uttaler som autoritetsfigur i hvert forhold vil alltid være den som Gud holder ansvarlig for beslutninger gjort av den gruppen mennesker. Akkurat som i fallet med fallet i Edens hage, vil synder ved unnlatelser og handlinger innenfor hver familie primært bli holdt far ansvarlig for. Enten far gav feil retning til familien eller om han ikke gav retning i det hele tatt, spiller det ingen rolle, han vil likevel bli stilt til ansvar siden Gud ser mannen som hodet i hans hjem. (se 1. Korinter 11:3 og Romerne 13:12)

As a child, you might think you can’t make a difference in the lives of people around you, but that is not true! Your little acts of kindness will not soon be forgotten. Being a true friend to someone who is hurting can change that person’s life forever.

This is the true story of “Hadassah” (not her real name) a young girl who was very much looking forward to starting school. Once she started first grade, what a disappointment it was to find that the second-grade girls were ready for someone to be mean to, or so it seemed. Maybe it would have been better if Hadassah had stood up to them, but she didn’t. Instead, she chose to act as if it didn’t hurt and tried to ignore them. Some days were better than others, but sadly this went on for three or four years.

Sure, there were good times too, but many evenings she walked home from school, crying most of the way and wishing that she wouldn’t need to go back to school the next day!

One day, one of the girls lost her pen. She was sure that Hadassah had stolen it. This was very disturbing to a very conscientious Hadassah. At the next recess she was blamed for cheating on her flash cards. Many other made-up stories were also passed around among the girls.

However, there was one little girl in that second-grade group of girls whose name we’ll say was “Esther”. She was Hadassah’s best friend and supported her all through those difficult years.

Esther was a very gentle, sweet girl, which is mostly what Hadassah remembered her for. Esther had cystic fibrosis and in the 1970s they didn’t have as many treatment options available for that disease as they do now, so those patients usually died very young. As Esther’s sickness became worse, the days that she felt well enough to be in school were rare. Since Esther was well-liked, the days when she was in school were special to everyone. Perhaps Esther realized she would be in heaven before the other girls—we don’t know for sure. But she taught the girls a song, “How Far Is Heaven”, which Hadassah still likes to sing today!

Hadassah still remembers seeing the emergency squad go past her house when they took Esther to the hospital for the last time. It was a very sad group of schoolgirls when Esther died at the age of 13. Esther had touched the hearts of many people in her short life, including the nurses who had cared for her during her stay in the hospital. Hadassah still remembers seeing some of the nurses crying at Esther’s funeral. Do you think Hadassah will ever forget Esther? Never!

Besides being her best friend, another bright spot for Hadassah was that when Esther was in school the other girls weren’t as mean to her (Hadassah). It so happened that in about the fourth grade, Esther was in school more often. One day she went home and told her parents what she was witnessing in school—how the other girls were against Hadassah and were being so mean to her. Esther’s father brought this problem up in the next parent/teacher meeting. What a night and day change started the very next day! One of the girls even came to Hadassah and apologized. Finally, they could all be friends and today those girls are Hadassah’s “old school friends”.

It’s worth it to stand beside someone who is being treated unkindly. Your support may be what God uses to help your friend to go through their hard times in a good way! And share it with your parents, they can help find a way to change the problem.

כילדה, ייתכן שתחשבי שאינך יכולה לשנות את חייהם של האנשים סביבך, אבל זה לא נכון! המעשים הקטנים של טוב לב לא יישכחו במהירות. להיות חברה אמתית של מישהי שסובלת יכול לשנות את חייה של אותה אישה לעד.

זו הסיפור האמיתי של "הדסה" (לא שמה האמיתי), ילדה צעירה שציפתה בקוצר רוח להתחיל את בית הספר. ברגע שהתחילה בכיתה א', כמה אכזבה הייתה לגלות שהבנות בכיתה ב' היו מוכנות למישהו להיות mean אליהן, או כך זה נראה. אולי היה עדיף אילו הדסה הייתה עומדת מולם, אבל היא לא עשתה זאת. במקום זאת, היא בחרה לפעול כאילו זה לא פגע בה וניסתה להתעלם. כמה ימים היו טובים יותר מאחרים, אך למרבה הצער זה נמשך שלוש או ארבע שנים.

בוודאי, היו גם זמנים טובים, אבל הרבה ערבים היא הלכה הביתה מבית הספר ובכתה ברוב הדרך ואחלה שלא תצטרך לחזור לבית הספר למחרת!

יום אחד, אחת הבנות איבדה את העט שלה. היא הייתה בטוחה שהדסה גנבה אותו. זה היה מטריד מאוד את הדסה, שהייתה מצפונית מאוד. בהפסקה הבאה האשימו אותה ברמאות בכרטיסי הזיכרון שלה. גם סיפורים מאולתרים רבים אחרים נפוצו בקרב הבנות.

עם זאת, הייתה שם ילדה קטנה אחת בקבוצת בנות כיתה ב' שאותה נגיד קוראים לה "אסתר". היא הייתה חברת הלב של הדסה ותמכה בה בכל אותן שנים קשות.

אסתר הייתה ילדה עדינה ומתוקה מאוד, וזה בעיקר מה שהדסה זוכרת אותה עבורו. לאסתר הייתה סיסטיק פיברוזיס ובשנות ה-70 לא היו אפשרויות טיפול רבות למחלה הזו כפי שיש היום, ולכן אותם חולים בדרך כלל מתו צעירים מאוד. ככל שמחלתה של אסתר התדרדרה, הימים שבהם הרגישה מספיק טוב כדי להיות בבית הספר היו נדירים. מכיוון שאסתר הייתה אהובה, הימים שבהם היא הייתה בבית הספר היו מיוחדים לכולם. אולי אסתר הבינה שהיא תהיה בשמיים לפני הבנות האחרות—אנחנו לא יודעים בוודאות. אבל היא לימדה את הבנות שיר, "כמה רחוקים השמיים", שהדסה עדיין אוהבת לשיר היום!

הדסה עדיין זוכרת שראתה את צוות החירום חולף ליד הבית כשהם לקחו את אסתר לבית החולים בפעם האחרונה. זו הייתה קבוצת ילדות מבית הספר מאד עצובה כשאסתר מתה בגיל 13. אסתר נגעה בלבם של אנשים רבים בחייה הקצרים, כולל האחיות שטיפלו בה בתקופת אשפוזה. הדסה עדיין זוכרת שראתה כמה מהאחיות בוכות בהלוויה של אסתר. האם את חושבת שהדסה אי פעם תשכח את אסתר? לעולם לא!

מלבד היותה החברה הטובה שלה, נקודה מוארת נוספת עבור הדסה הייתה שכשהאסתר הייתה בבית הספר הבנות האחרות לא היו כל כך mean אליה (להדסה). יצא שבערך בכיתה ד' אסתר הייתה בבית הספר יותר לעתים. יום אחד היא חזרה הביתה וסיפרה להוריה מה היא עיסקה בו בבית הספר—כמה הבנות האחרות היו נגד הדסה והיו כל כך מרושעות כלפיה. אביה של אסתר העלה את הבעיה הזו בפגישת הורים/מורים הבאה. איזו מהפך התחיל כבר מהיום שאחריו! אחת הבנות אפילו באה אל הדסה והתנצלה. בסופו של דבר, הן יכלו כולן להיות חברות והיום אותן בנות הן "חברות בית הספר הישנות" של הדסה.

שווה לעמוד לצד מישהי שמטופלת בחוסר אדיבות. התמיכה שלך עשויה להיות מה שאלוהים ישתמש בו כדי לעזור לחברתך לעבור את זמנה הקשה בדרך טובה! ושתפי את זה עם ההורים שלך, הם יכולים לעזור למצוא דרך לשנות את הבעיה.

This hymn is generally considered to be one of the greatest hymns ever written and is found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. It was written by a man who was frail in body, but strong in spirit. It was he who coined the phrase, “It is better to wear out than to rust out.” Let us now take a glimpse into the life of this servant of God.

Henry Francis Lyte, the author of this great and noteworthy hymn, was born June 1, 1793, in Ednam, near Kelso, Scotland. At a young age, he was left an orphan and was in comparative poverty. He was educated at Trinity College in Dublin, Ireland. It was there that his gift of poetry began to appear, winning him three prizes. His primary goal with his studies was to become a physician, instead, by the providence of God, he became a minister of the gospel of Jesus Christ.

One day in Cornwall, a fellow clergyman who was on his deathbed, requested that Lyte would come and give him some spiritual comfort. “To their mutual grief, they found themselves [both] groping for the light, veritable blind guides”. As they searched for truth and assurance of salvation, they fixed their faith on Christ, and Lyte came away from that sickroom a changed man, never to be the same again. It is said that it was his encounter with God at the bedside of that dying man that prompted Lyte’s noble hymn, “Jesus, I My Cross Have Taken.” In the year 1823, Henry F. Lyte took charge of a seashore parish, Lower Brixham, in Devonshire, England. It was at that place where he spent the last 23 years of his life toiling as a pastor for the spiritual good of the poor fishing people and the rough seafaring men of that region until his death in the fall of 1847. For all of Henry’s dedication and labor, he received a reward: having a Sunday school of several hundred scholars, as well as “a splendid company of seventy or eighty teachers, personally trained by him.”

Throughout his lifetime, his health was continually threatened by asthma and tuberculosis. Notwithstanding his physical frailties, he worked tirelessly with an established reputation as a poet, musician, and minister. Wherever he went, he was greatly loved and admired by his people. Toward the end of these later years, his health became gradually worse. So it was that during the winter months, he felt compelled to seek a warmer climate in Italy, which is a part of southern Europe.

Though he was greatly weakened by his sickness, on September 4, 1847, as Lyte was about to leave to head southward, he was arrested by an “irresistible desire” to preach once more to his congregation. He dearly loved these people and he had labored among them for so many years. “Against the protest of his amazed friends, he accomplished this purpose, and it is recorded that Lyte nearly had to crawl to the pulpit and his message came as from a dying man.” “O brethren,” he said, as he entered the familiar pulpit for the last time, “I stand here among you today, as alive from the dead, if I may hope to impress it upon you, and induce you to prepare for that solemn hour which must come to all, by a timely appreciation and dependance on the death of Christ.” These final words made a deep impact upon his congregation, after which he closed the service by administering the Lord’s Supper to his weeping people. Later that evening, after the service, he was inspired to “poetical composition” and wrote the eight stanzas of his last and greatest hymn:

Abide with me: fast falls the eventide;
The darkness deepens; Lord, with me abide:
when other helpers fail, and comforts flee,
Help of the helpless, O abide with me.

Swift to its close ebbs out life’s little day;
Earth’s joys grow dim, its glories pass away;
Change and decay in all around I see;
O Thou who changest not, abide with me.

Not a brief glance I beg, a passing word;
But, as Thou dwell’st with Thy disciples, Lord,
Familiar, condescending, patient, free,
Come, not to sojourn, but abide, with me.

Come not in terrors, as the King of kings;
But kind and good, with healing in Thy wings;
Tears for all woes, a heart for every plea;
Come, Friend of sinners, and thus ‘bide with me.

Thou on my head in early youth didst smile;
And, though rebellious and perverse meanwhile,
thou hast not left me, oft as I left thee:
On to the close, O Lord, abide with me.

I need Thy presence every passing hour;
What but Thy grace can foil the tempter’s power?
Who like Thyself my guide and stay can be?
Through cloud and sunshine, O abide with me.

I fear no foe, with Thee at hand to bless:
Ills have no weight, and tears no bitterness.
Where is death’s sting? Where, grave, thy victory?
I triumph still, if Thou abide with me.

Hold Thou Thy cross before my closing eyes;
Shine through the gloom, and point me to the skies;
Heaven’s morning breaks, and earth’s vain shadows flee:
In life, in death, O Lord, abide with me.

This hymn he gave to one of the family members that very night. Leaving the following day, he began his trek to Rome, Italy, hoping to gain some relief from his sickness. Lyte make it as far as Nice, France where his sickness prevented his further travel. He passed away soon after the age of 55, on November 20, 1847. His last words were “Joy! Peace!”

The scene behind this hymn is that of the resurrected Christ Jesus walking on the road to Emmaus with two of His somewhat sad and discouraged disciples. As they neared the end of their seven-mile walk and approached the village where they were going, Jesus …made as though he would have gone further. But they constrained him, saying, Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them –Luke 24:28-29.

We can draw a parallel between that scene and Henry F. Lyte’s own experience of drawing toward the close of his earthly journey. Thus, as the disciples besought the risen Lord to abide with them in the close of that ancient day, so was the meaning of this song written in the “shadows of death” to the hymn writer.

Lyte himself composed a tune for this hymn on the same evening that he wrote it, but it never became widely used. However, the tune universally used was written fourteen years later by William Henry Monk, a noted London musician, and editor of the well-known Anglican hymnal, Hymns Ancient and Modern. He included this song in his first edition, which was published in 1861.

In all, William H. Monk composed 50 tunes for the hymnal. It is said that Monk, being “inspired by the beauty of a glorious sunset while yet experiencing a deep personal sorrow,” composed (in only 10 minutes) the tune, Eventide, for the song, “Abide With Me, Fast Falls The Eventide”. William Monk also wrote the music for other familiar hymns such as “Look, Ye Saints! The Sight Is Glorious”, and “The Strife Is O’er”.

To summarize, Henry Lyte experienced many sorrows during his lifetime. Both of his parents died at an early age leaving him an orphan. And his own sickness and frailty caused him to be in ongoing danger of asthma and tuberculosis. Yet, in spite of all his trials, we find in him a resilient spirit to reach out to others; to touch and minister the Gospel to those poor people among whom he lived. “In no other writer,” says Dr. Breed (in the Treasury of Hymn Stories), “are poetry and religion more exquisitely united.”

यह भजन सामान्यतः लिखे गए सबसे महान भजनों में से एक माना जाता है और आज प्रकाशित लगभग हर भजन-संग्रह या भजन पुस्तक में पाया जाता है। इसे एक ऐसे व्यक्ति ने लिखा था जो शारीरिक रूप से दुर्बल था, पर आत्मा में दृढ़ था। उन्होंने ही यह वाक्यांश गढ़ा था, “घिसने से बेहतर है सेने से खराब होना।” आइए अब हम ईश्वर के इस सेवक के जीवन पर एक नज़र डालें।

हेनरी फ्रांसिस लाईट, इस महान और उल्लेखनीय भजन के लेखक, का जन्म 1 जून, 1793 को एडनम में हुआ था, जो केल्सो, स्कॉटलैंड के निकट है। कम उम्र में ही वे अनाथ रह गए और तुलनात्मक रूप से गरीबी में रहे। उन्हें आयरलैंड के डबलिन के ट्रिनिटी कॉलेज में पढ़ाया गया। यहीं उनका कविता-प्रतिभा प्रकट होने लगी और उन्हें तीन पुरस्कार मिले। अपनी पढ़ाई का प्राथमिक उद्देश्य चिकित्सक बनना था, पर ईश्वर की व्यवस्था से वे यीशु मसीह के सुसमाचार के एक मंत्री बन गए।

एक दिन कॉर्नवॉल में, एक सह-पादरी जो अपनी मृत्युशैय्या पर था, ने लाईट से अनुरोध किया कि वे आकर उन्हें आध्यात्मिक सान्त्वना दें। “उन दोनों के दुःख के लिए, वे पाते हैं कि वे दोनों ही प्रकाश की ओर गुमराह करते हुए थरथरा रहे थे, सच्चे अन्धे मार्गदर्शक।” जब वे सत्य और उद्धार की सुनिश्चितता की खोज कर रहे थे, तब उन्होंने अपना विश्वास मसीह पर केंद्रित किया, और लाईट उस रोगी के शयनकक्ष से एक परिवर्तित व्यक्ति बनकर निकले, कभी पहले जैसे न रहने के लिए। कहा जाता है कि उस मरते हुए व्यक्ति के शयनकक्ष में ईश्वर के साथ उनकी वह मुठभेड़ ही लाईट के महान भजन, “Jesus, I My Cross Have Taken” लिखने के प्रेरक कारणों में से थी। वर्ष 1823 में, हेनरी एफ. लाईट ने डेवोनशायर, इंग्लैंड के लोअर ब्रिक्सहम नामक तटवर्ती पारिश की जिम्‍मेवारी ली। उसी स्थान पर उन्होंने अपने जीवन के अंतिम 23 वर्ष अपने प्रांत के गरीब मछुआरे लोगों और कठोर समुद्री यात्रियों की आध्यात्मिक भलाई के लिए एक पादरी के रूप में परिश्रम करते हुए बिताए, और पतझड़ 1847 में उनकी मृत्यु हुई। हेनरी की समर्पित सेवा और परिश्रम का फल उन्हें मिला: उनके पास सैकड़ों विद्यार्थियों का एक संडे स्कूल था, साथ ही “सत्तर या अस्सी शिक्षकों की एक भव्य सभा, जिन्हें व्यक्तिगत रूप से उन्होंने प्रशिक्षित किया था।”

जीवन भर उनकी सेहत दम और तपेदिक से लगातार खतरे में रही। शारीरिक दुर्बलताओं के बावजूद, वे एक स्थापित कवि, संगीतकार और पादरी के रूप में अथक रूप से कार्य करते रहे। जहां-जहां वे गए, अपने लोगों द्वारा उन्हें अत्यंत प्रेम और प्रशंसा मिली। इन अंतिम वर्षों के निकट, उनकी सेहत धीरे-धीरे और खराब हो गई। इसलिए सर्दियों के महीनों में उन्हें इटली के एक गर्म जलवायु की ओर जाने की आवश्यकता महसूस हुई, जो दक्षिणी यूरोप का हिस्सा है।

यद्यपि बीमारी से वे बहुत कमजोर थे, 4 सितंबर, 1847 को जब लाईट दक्षिण की ओर प्रस्थान करने वाले थे, तो उन्हें एक "अपरिहार्य इच्छा" ने रोका कि वे एक बार फिर अपने समुदाय को उपदेश दें। वे इन लोगों से बहुत स्नेह करते थे और इतने वर्षों से उनके बीच काम कर रहे थे। “उनके चकित मित्रों की आपत्ति के विरुद्ध, उन्होंने यह कार्य पूरा किया, और ऐसा रिकॉर्ड है कि लाईट को प्रायः उपदेश देने के लिए रेंगते हुए पादरीपृष्ठ तक जाना पड़ा और उनका संदेश किसी मरते हुए व्यक्ति से आता हुआ प्रतीत हुआ।” “हे भाइयों,” उन्होंने कहा, जब वे Familiar pulpit में अंतिम बार प्रवेश कर रहे थे, “मैं आज तुम लोगों के बीच यहां खड़ा हूँ, मरे हुए में से जीवित होकर, यदि मैं आशा कर सकता हूँ कि इसे तुम पर प्रभावित करूँ और तुम सबको उस गंभीर घड़ी के लिए तैयार करने के लिए प्रेरित कर सकूँ जो सभी को आनी है, मसीह की मृत्यु पर समयपूर्व प्रशंसा और निर्भरता द्वारा।” इन अंतिम शब्दों ने उनकी उपासना सभा पर गहरा प्रभाव डाला, जिसके बाद उन्होंने अपने रोते हुए लोगों को प्रभु का भोज देकर सेवा समाप्त की। उसी शाम सेवा के बाद, वे "काव्यात्मक रचना" के लिए प्रेरित हुए और उन्होंने अपने अंतिम और महानतम भजन की आठ छंदें लिखीं:

मेरे संग रहो: घटते हैं शीघ्र शाम के क्षण;
अँधेरा गहरा होता जाता है; हे प्रभु, मेरे संग रहो:
जब अन्य सहायक असफल हों, और सांत्वनाएँ दूर भागें,
असहायों के सहायक, हे मेरे संग रहो।

जीवन का छोटा दिन शीघ्र ही लुप्त हो जाता है;
पृथ्वी की खुशियाँ मंद पड़ जाती हैं, उसकी महिमा विलीन हो जाती है;
चारों ओर परिवर्तन और क्षय मैं देखता हूँ;
हे तू जो न बदलता है, मेरे संग रहो।

मैं एक क्षणिक झलक नहीं माँगता, न ही किसी गुजरते हुए शब्द की चाह;
परन्तु, जैसे तू अपने शिष्यों के साथ वास करता था, हे प्रभु,
परिचित, दीनतापूर्ण, धैर्यवान, मुक्त,
आओ, ठहरने नहीं, पर मेरे संग रहो।

राजाओं के राजा के रूप में भय में आओ मत;
पर दयालु और श्रेष्ठ होकर, अपने पंखों में उपचार लिए;
सभी दुखों के लिये आँसू, हर प्रार्थना के लिये एक हृदय;
आओ, पापियों के मित्र, और ऐसे ही मेरे संग रहो।

तू ने मेरी शिरोपरिणामिका पर यौवन में स्मित किया था;
और, जबकि मैं उस समय विद्रोही और विपरीत था,
तू ने मुझे नहीं छोड़ा, जितनी बार मैंने तुझे छोड़ा:
अंत तक चले चलो, हे प्रभु, मेरे संग रहो।

मुझे प्रत्येक गुजरते घंटे में तेरा सान्निध्य चाहिए;
तेरी ही अनुग्रह के सिवा कौन प्रलोभक की शक्ति को परास्त कर सकता है?
कौन तेरे समान मेरा मार्गदर्शक और सहारा हो सकता है?
मेघ और धूप में, हे मेरे संग रहो।

मैं किसी शत्रु से नहीं डरता, तेरे हाथ में आशीर्वाद के साथ:
विडंबनाओं का कोई भार नहीं, और आँसुओं में कोई कड़वाहट नहीं।
मृत्यु की विषैला काँटा कहाँ? क़ब्र, तेरी जीत कहाँ?
मैं फिर भी विजय प्राप्त करता हूँ, यदि तू मेरे संग रहे।

मेरी बंद होती आँखों के सामने तू अपना क्रूस थामे रख;
अन्धकार में चमक चमक कर उजागर कर, और मुझे आकाश की ओर इंगित कर;
स्वर्ग की सुबह फूट रही है, और पृथ्वी के व्यर्थ साये भाग रहे हैं:
जीवन में, मृत्यु में, हे प्रभु, मेरे संग रहो।

इस भजन को उन्होंने उसी रात परिवार के एक सदस्य को दे दिया। अगले दिन प्रस्थान करते हुए, उन्होंने रोम, इटली की ओर अपनी यात्रा शुरू की, यह आशा करते हुए कि उन्हें अपनी बीमारी से कुछ राहत मिले। लाईट फ्रांस के नाइस तक ही पहुँच पाए जहाँ उनकी बीमारी ने आगे की यात्रा से रोक दिया। वे 55 वर्ष की आयु के थोड़े बाद ही, 20 नवंबर, 1847 को स्वर्गवासी हो गए। उनके अंतिम शब्द थे “आनन्द! शांति!”

इस भजन के पीछे दृश्य वह है जब पुनरुत्थित मसीह यीशु दो कुछ उदास और हतोत्साहित शिष्यों के साथ एम्माउस की सड़क पर चल रहे थे। जब वे अपने सात-मील के मार्ग के अंत के निकट पहुँचे और उस गाँव के पास पहुँचे जहाँ वे जा रहे थे, यीशु …ऐसा कर रहे थे जैसे आगे चला ही जाएगा। पर वे उसे रोककर कहने लगे, हमारे साथ ठहरो; क्योंकि सांझ हो रही है, और दिन बहुत घट चुका है। और उसने उनके साथ जाकर ठहर कर उनसे भोज किया – लूका 24:28-29।

हम उस दृश्य और हेनरी एफ. लाईट के अपने सांसारिक मार्ग के निकट आने के अनुभव के बीच समानता निकाल सकते हैं। इस प्रकार, जैसे शिष्यों ने उस प्राचीन दिन के समाप्ति पर उठे प्रभु से उनके साथ ठहरने का आग्रह किया, वैसे ही मृत्यु के “छायाओं” में भजन रचयिता के लिए यह गीत लिखा गया था।

लाईट ने उसी शाम इस भजन के लिए एक सुर भी रचा था, पर वह व्यापक रूप से प्रयुक्त नहीं हुआ। तथापि, जो सुर सार्वभौमिक रूप से प्रयुक्त हुआ, वह चौदह वर्ष बाद विलियम हेनरी मोंक ने लिखा, जो एक प्रसिद्ध लंदन संगीतज्ञ और प्रख्यात एंग्लिकन भजन-संग्रह Hymns Ancient and Modern के संपादक थे। उन्होंने इस गीत को अपनी पहली प्रति में शामिल किया, जो 1861 में प्रकाशित हुई थी।

कुल मिलाकर, विलियम एच. मोंक ने उस भजन-संग्रह के लिए 50 सुर रचे। कहा जाता है कि मोंक, “एक भव्य सूर्यास्त की सुंदरता से प्रेरित होकर जबकि वे व्यक्तिगत गहरे शोक का अनुभव कर रहे थे,” ने (केवल 10 मिनट में) इस गीत “Abide With Me, Fast Falls The Eventide” के लिए "Eventide" नामक सुर रचा। विलियम मोंक ने अन्य परिचित भजनों के लिये भी संगीत लिखा जैसे “Look, Ye Saints! The Sight Is Glorious” और “The Strife Is O’er.”

सारांशतः, हेनरी लाईट ने अपने जीवन में अनेक दुख अनुभव किए। उनके दोनों माता-पिता कम आयु में ही मर गए, जिससे वे अनाथ रह गए। और उनकी अपनी बीमारी और दुर्बलता के कारण उन्हें लगातार दमा और तपेदिक का खतरा बना रहा। फिर भी, सभी परीक्षाओं के बावजूद, हम उनमें दूसरों तक पहुँचने का एक लचीला आत्मा पाते हैं; उन गरीब लोगों को स्पर्श करने और सुसमाचार की सेवा करने का साहस जिनके बीच वे रहते थे। “किसी अन्य लेखक में,” डॉ. ब्रिट (Treasury of Hymn Stories में) कहते हैं, “कविता और धर्म इतनी सुंदरता से एकीकृत नहीं हैं।”
