And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water. And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus –Matthew 14:28-29.

Men who follow Jesus are men of faith. Discipleship is not for cowards or the faint of heart, nor is it for those who demand a rationale for acts of obedience. The disciples had spent the day with Jesus. After the feeding of the five thousand Matthew writes that …straightway Jesus constrained his disciples to get into a ship, and to go before him unto the other side, while he sent the multitudes away –Matthew 14:22.

If there was anything that the disciples were familiar with and skilled in, it was sailing the waters of Galilee. This was their territory. Peter and John had fished these waters with their father from their earliest remembrance. But tonight, they were making little headway… the wind was contrary.

And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea. And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear. But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid –Matthew 14:25-27.

Peter then made this bold appeal …Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water –Matthew 14:28. What was Peter thinking? He had never walked on water. Jesus was not asking him to walk on water. It was not logical. It defied the laws of nature… yet when Jesus said “come”. Peter stepped out of the boat and walked on the water to go to Jesus. That’s right! He was treading on water.

Peter was responding to a clear call from Jesus. Jesus said “come”. It is important that we understand that faith is our response to the clear call of God on our lives. Too often in our ambition to be useful we choose our path and call our ambition “faith” when God may not be in it at all.

If you want to be a man of faith, open your Bible and pray. Ask God to reveal His plan for your life. The Bible contains many commandments that can provide practical direction for our lives. Take God at His Word. Step out in faith and obedience then you will experience the miracle of God’s power in your life.

Peter’s boat was his security. He and his boat had a long relationship. It had served him well for many years. Peter felt right at home in his old bark, although tonight she did not seem to respond well to his masterful seamanship. He had drawn many a draught of fish over her gunwales. Now as he stands on her deck watching Jesus approach, “walking on the water”, he was overcome with a desire to go to Jesus. In reckless abandonment he stepped off her deck …and a miracle happened.

A walk of faith often calls us away from that which is familiar and secure. If we make safety and security our priority—if we limit our actions to carefully calculated risks (limited to that which we can manage and control)—we limit the power of God working in and through us.

Our forefathers in Europe knew that if they embraced the journey of unreserved discipleship, it could be costly. They risked the seizure of their property; many of them lost all that they owned. Since they willingly faced imprisonment and death, we refer to them as heroes of the faith. These were men who were willing to abandon all for the sake of the gospel. Because of their faith we receive the benefits of a godly heritage.

I commend our younger generation of Anabaptist youth for their willingness to make following Jesus a priority. In the past our priority has been to build our security base, be it our farm or business, and then consider mission work as a possibility. That was never Jesus’ model for service. When Jesus sent out his disciples he said. And he said unto them, Take nothing for your journey, neither staves, nor scrip, neither bread, neither money; neither have two coats apiece –Luke 9:3.

Later, after they had returned, Jesus asked them, And he said unto them, When I sent you without purse, and scrip, and shoes, lacked ye any thing? And they said, Nothing –Luke 22:35.

You do not need to go into foreign missions to experience the power of God released in your life. Every act of radical obedience is an act of faith. There are men in our Anabaptist communities who are experiencing moral defeat. If we are going to succumb to a victim mentality (“I can’t help it”), and define moral failure as an addiction, we set ourselves up for ongoing defeat. Men of faith are men of action who take measurable steps of obedience which will lead them to ultimate victory. Moral failure begins with small compromises that end in crushing defeat.

Peter’s actions were not logical. If Peter would have processed his decision using the scientific method, he would not have taken such a risk. Many of the simple commands of Christ have no apparent scientific reasoning. From baptism, to communion, to foot washing, to anointing with oil, these are all acts of faith. The significance and the power of each lies in the doing of it with a heart of obedient faith, not in the thing itself.

So it is with many aspects of the Christian experience. We can analyze a thing endlessly, ultimately resulting in its demise. This happens in many churches. We reason away the woman’s head covering. We reason away the nonconformed lifestyle. We reason away the permanence of marriage. We reason away brotherhood accountability. What we have left has no resemblance to the simple teachings of Jesus. Discipleship calls us to faithful obedience. Jesus and the apostles taught it, so we do it. The blessing and the power lie in the doing of it.

That is what Peter discovered. He walked on water! He did not dip a toe to test the water first. I like to think he leaped from the boat and hit the water with both feet. That would be faith and Peter had faith.

But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? And when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased –Matthew 14:30-32.

Peter had faith to walk on water until he began to look around and began to process his situation using the scientific method. This is not to invalidate the scientific method. The scientific method proves the order of creation and the evidence of a creator.

In Hebrews 11 we read that …faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen –Hebrews 11:1.

It is our faith that is the substance and our faith that is the evidence of spiritual realities. Just as the scientific method proves the realities of the created world, so our faith proves spiritual realities.

Boisterous wind and crashing waves produced a fearful, sinking Peter. We sometimes criticize Peter for taking his eyes off of Jesus and sinking into the waves; however, Peter walked on water, I know of no one else who walked on water. When we transition from obedient faith to carnal rationalization, we lose power with God.

Are we suggesting that faith is irrational? No, not at all. As a matter of fact, the first act of faith is to believe that Jesus is the logos. John wrote, In the beginning was the Word [Logos], and the Word [Logos], was with God, and the Word [Logos], was God –John 1:1. It is from the Greek word Logos that we get our English word logic.

Just as there are laws in nature that make the scientific method durable and replicable, so there are spiritual laws that give order and cohesion to our inner man. Jesus is the embodiment of these truths. His teachings are the revelation of these truths and through his death and resurrection these truths have become accessible to all. Jesus promised, Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth… –John 16:13.

Men of faith are men who have eyes to see these spiritual realities. Their vision is not limited to the natural world. They understand that there are spiritual realities that have “cause and effect” in our lives that are every bit as powerful as the “cause and effect” that we see about us in the natural world every day.

These realities are only visible to men of faith. Paul wrote, But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned –1 Corinthians 2:14. Men of faith, are men whose lives are governed by spiritual realities that are incomprehensible to the natural man. If you will be a man of faith, expect to be misunderstood. You are embarking on a journey that will run counter to the world view of many.

As Peter began to sink into the waves he cried out, “Lord, save me”. His plaintive cry revealed an absolute trust in his Lord. Jesus reached out His hand and rescued him. Jesus next words continue to challenge us. He said to Peter, …O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? Matthew 14:31. Peter had just walked on water—a feat no man had accomplished before or since, yet Jesus called it “little faith” and asked, “why did you doubt?”.

Jesus said at another time, …If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you –Matthew 17:20.

If Peter’s “little faith” empowered him to walk on water, and if faith as tiny as a grain of mustard seed can remove mountains what does that say of your and my faith?

Perhaps it is evidence that our faith is littler than Peter’s “little faith” and tinier than the tiny grain of mustard seed?! It is also evidence that God honors little faith. What he does not honor is no faith. According to your faith be it unto you. Little faith…walk on water! No faith…sink beneath the waves!

Since Jesus is the “Logos”, He is the master of the natural world and the spirit world. He proved himself to be the Master of the wind and the waves—and when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased –Matthew 14:32. And He proved Himself to be the Master of the spirit world—then they that were in the ship came and worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God –Matthew 14:33.

We, in our western world, have become so satiated with materialism that we can easily be led to believe that natural realities are the most powerful realities. This materialism assaults us, not just with the abundance of material things, but also with a bombardment of humanistic philosophy. Humanistic philosophy is thinking that is devoid of spiritual reality… that is devoid of faith.

If you, as a man, find yourself sinking in waves of despair… be it financial struggles… be it relational difficulties… moral failure or maybe you find yourself being your own worst critic…may I challenge you to lift your eyes to the one who is Logos. Jesus is the one who is master of your circumstances and the one who would be Lord of your soul. To allow Jesus to be Lord of your soul is to live in faith obedience to the radical teachings of Jesus.

To live in harmony with the natural world we honor the laws of nature. When we are replacing a roof, we respect the law of gravity. When driving a vehicle, we slow down for turns out of respect for the law of inertia. Defy the natural laws and someone gets hurt.

To live in harmony with the spiritual world, we honor the law of Christ. We love our neighbor. We forgive our brother. We keep our marriage vows. We bear …one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ –Galatians 6:2.

Men of faith are men who are attune to these spiritual realities and order their lives accordingly.

En Petrus antwoordde en zeide tot Hem: Heere, indien Gij het zijt, laat mij dan op het water tot U komen. En Hij zeide: Kom. En als Petrus uit het schip nederstegen was, liep hij op het water, om tot Jezus te gaan – Matteüs 14:28-29.

Mannen die Jezus volgen zijn mannen van geloof. Volgeling zijn is niet voor lafaards of zwakke van hart, noch voor hen die een rationele uitleg eisen voor daden van gehoorzaamheid. De discipelen hadden de dag met Jezus doorgebracht. Na het voeden van de vijfduizend schrijft Matteüs dat …reeds terstond Jezus zijn discipelen aandrong het schip in te gaan, en vooruit te varen naar de overzijde, totdat Hij de menigten weggestuurd had – Matteüs 14:22.

Als er iets was waarmee de discipelen vertrouwd en vaardig waren, dan was het wel varen op het meer van Galilea. Dit was hun terrein. Petrus en Johannes hadden vanaf hun vroegste herinnering met hun vader op deze wateren gevist. Maar vannacht boekten ze weinig vooruitgang… de wind stak tegen.

En in de vierde wacht der nacht ging Jezus tot hen toe, wandelende op de zee. En als de discipelen Hem zagen wandelen op de zee, werden zij ontzet, en zeiden: Het is een verschijning; en zij schreeuwden uit van vreze. Maar terstond sprak Jezus tot hen en zeide: Weest gerust, Ik ben het; vrees niet – Matteüs 14:25-27.

Petrus deed toen deze moedige bede: …Heere, indien Gij het zijt, beveel dat ik op het water tot U kome – Matteüs 14:28. Wat zat Petrus te denken? Hij had nog nooit op water gelopen. Jezus vroeg hem niet expliciet om op water te lopen. Het was niet logisch. Het tartte de natuurwetten… toch, toen Jezus zei “kom”, stapte Petrus uit de boot en liep op het water om naar Jezus te gaan. Dat klopt! Hij liep op water.

Petrus reageerde op een duidelijke oproep van Jezus. Jezus zei “kom”. Het is belangrijk dat we begrijpen dat geloof onze reactie is op de duidelijke roeping van God over ons leven. Te vaak in onze ambitie om nuttig te zijn kiezen we ons pad en noemen onze ambitie “geloof” terwijl God daar misschien helemaal niet in betrokken is.

Als je een man van geloof wilt zijn, open je Bijbel en bid. Vraag God Zijn plan voor je leven te openbaren. De Bijbel bevat vele geboden die praktische richting kunnen geven voor ons leven. Neem God bij Zijn Woord. Stap uit in geloof en gehoorzaamheid en dan zul je het wonder van Gods kracht in je leven ervaren.

Petrus’ boot was zijn veiligheid. Hij en zijn boot hadden een lange relatie. Ze had hem vele jaren goed gediend. Petrus voelde zich thuis in zijn oude schuit, hoewel zij vanavond niet goed leek te reageren op zijn bekwame stuurmanskunst. Hij had vele scheppen vis over haar relingen gehaald. Nu, terwijl hij op dek staat en Jezus ziet naderen, “lopende op het water”, werd hij overvallen door een verlangen naar Jezus toe te gaan. In roekeloze overgave stapte hij van het dek af …en er gebeurde een wonder.

Een weg van geloof roept ons vaak weg van dat wat vertrouwd en veilig is. Als we veiligheid en zekerheid onze prioriteit maken—als we onze handelingen beperken tot zorgvuldig berekende risico’s (binnen datgene wat we kunnen beheersen)—beperken we de macht van God die in en door ons werkt.

Onze voorvaderen in Europa wisten dat als zij de weg van onvoorwaardelijke discipelschap zouden inslaan, het kostbaar kon zijn. Zij riskeren de inbeslagneming van hun eigendom; velen van hen verloren alles wat zij bezaten. Omdat zij bereid waren gevangenisstraf en de dood te aanvaarden, noemen wij hen helden des geloofs. Dit waren mannen die bereid waren alles op te geven ter wille van het evangelie. Door hun geloof ontvangen wij de zegen van een godvruchtige erfenis.

Ik prijs onze jongere generatie Anabaptistische jeugd voor hun bereidheid om Jezus volgen een prioriteit te maken. In het verleden was onze prioriteit om onze zekerheidsbasis op te bouwen, hetzij onze boerderij of zaak, en dan zendingswerk als een mogelijkheid te overwegen. Dat was nooit Jezus’ model van dienst. Toen Jezus zijn discipelen uitzond zei Hij: En Hij zeide tot hen: Neemt niets mede op de reis, geen staf, geen tas, geen brood, geen geld; ook geen twee mantels elk – Lucas 9:3.

Later, als zij teruggekomen waren, vroeg Jezus hun: En Hij zeide tot hen: Als Ik u uitzond zonder beurs, zonder tas en zonder schoenen, hebt gij iets tekort gehad? En zij zeiden: Niets – Lucas 22:35.

Je hoeft niet naar vreemde zending te gaan om de kracht van God in je leven te ervaren. Elke daad van radicale gehoorzaamheid is een daad van geloof. Er zijn mannen in onze Anabaptistische gemeenschappen die morele nederlaag ervaren. Als wij ten onder gaan aan een slachtoffermentaliteit (“ik kan er niets aan doen”), en morele mislukking definiëren als een verslaving, bereiden we ons voor op voortdurende nederlaag. Mannen van geloof zijn mannen van actie die meetbare stappen van gehoorzaamheid nemen die hen naar uiteindelijke overwinning zullen leiden. Morele val begint met kleine compromissen die eindigen in verpletterende nederlaag.

Petrus’ handelen was niet logisch. Als Petrus zijn besluit met de wetenschappelijke methode had geanalyseerd, zou hij niet zo’n risico hebben genomen. Vele van de eenvoudige geboden van Christus hebben geen ogenschijnlijke wetenschappelijke verklaring. Van doop, tot Avondmaal, tot voetwassing, tot zalving met olie, het zijn allemaal daden van geloof. De betekenis en de kracht van elk liggen in het doen ervan met een hart van gehoorzaam geloof, niet in het voorwerp zelf.

Zo is het met vele aspecten van de christelijke ervaring. We kunnen een zaak eindeloos analyseren, wat uiteindelijk leidt tot haar ondergang. Dit gebeurt in vele kerken. We redeneren ons weg van de vrouwenhoofdbedekking. We redeneren ons weg van de niet-conforme levensstijl. We redeneren ons weg van de blijvende aard van het huwelijk. We redeneren ons weg van broederlijke verantwoording. Wat overblijft heeft geen gelijkenis meer met de eenvoudige leer van Jezus. Discipelschap roept ons op tot trouw gehoorzaamheid. Jezus en de apostelen leerden het, dus doen wij het. De zegen en de kracht liggen in het doen ervan.

Dat is wat Petrus ontdekte. Hij liep op het water! Hij dompelde niet eerst een teen om het water te beproeven. Ik denk graag dat hij van de boot sprong en met beide voeten op het water landde. Dat zou geloof zijn en Petrus had geloof.

Maar als hij de sterke wind zag, werd hij bevreesd; en als hij begon te zinken, schreeuwde hij, zeggende: Heere, red mij. En terstond strekte Jezus Zijn hand uit, en greep hem, en zeide tot hem: O gij kleingelovige, waarom hebt gij getwijfeld? En als zij in het schip gekomen waren, hield de wind op – Matteüs 14:30-32.

Petrus had geloof om op het water te lopen totdat hij om zich heen begon te kijken en zijn situatie begon te analyseren met de wetenschappelijke methode. Dit is niet om de wetenschappelijke methode ongeldig te verklaren. De wetenschappelijke methode bewijst de orde van de schepping en het bewijs van een Schepper.

In Hebreeën 11 lezen we dat …geloof is de zekerheid der dingen, die men hoopt, en een bewijs der dingen, die men niet ziet – Hebreeën 11:1.

Het is ons geloof dat de zekerheid is en ons geloof dat het bewijs is van geestelijke realiteiten. Net zoals de wetenschappelijke methode de realiteiten van de geschapene wereld bewijst, zo bewijst ons geloof geestelijke realiteiten.

Gierende wind en klotsende golven veroorzaakten een bevreesde, zinkende Petrus. Soms bekritiseren we Petrus omdat hij zijn ogen van Jezus afwendde en in de golven zonk; toch, Petrus liep op het water, ik ken niemand anders die op het water liep. Als wij overgaan van gehoorzaam geloof naar wereldse rationalisatie, verliezen wij kracht bij God.

Zegenen wij daarmee dat geloof irrationeel is? Nee, helemaal niet. Integendeel, de eerste handeling van geloof is te geloven dat Jezus de Logos is. Johannes schreef, In het begin was het Woord [Logos], en het Woord [Logos] was bij God, en het Woord [Logos] was God – Johannes 1:1. Het is uit het Griekse woord Logos dat wij ons woord logica krijgen.

Net zoals er wetten in de natuur zijn die de wetenschappelijke methode duurzaam en reproduceerbaar maken, zo zijn er geestelijke wetten die orde en samenhang geven aan ons innerlijk leven. Jezus is de belichaming van deze waarheden. Zijn leer is de openbaring van deze waarheden en door Zijn dood en opstanding zijn deze waarheden voor allen toegankelijk geworden. Jezus beloofde: Maar als die gekomen is, de Geest der waarheid, zal Hij u leiden in alle waarheid… – Johannes 16:13.

Mannen van geloof zijn mannen die ogen hebben om deze geestelijke realiteiten te zien. Hun gezichtsveld is niet beperkt tot de natuurlijke wereld. Zij begrijpen dat er geestelijke realiteiten zijn die “oorzaak en gevolg” hebben in ons leven die even krachtig zijn als de “oorzaak en gevolg” die wij dagelijks om ons heen in de natuurlijke wereld zien.

Deze realiteiten zijn alleen zichtbaar voor mannen van geloof. Paulus schreef, Maar de natuurlijke mens ontvangt de dingen des Geestes Gods niet; want zij zijn hem dwaasheid, en hij kan ze niet kennen, omdat zij geestelijk onderscheiden worden – 1 Korintiërs 2:14. Mannen van geloof zijn mannen wier leven wordt bestuurd door geestelijke realiteiten die voor de natuurlijke mens onbegrijpelijk zijn. Als je een man van geloof wilt zijn, verwacht dan miskend te worden. Je begint aan een weg die tegen de wereldbeschouwing van velen ingaat.

Toen Petrus begon te zinken in de golven riep hij uit: “Heere, red mij”. Zijn klaaglijke roep toonde een absolute vertrouwen in zijn Heer. Jezus reikte Zijn hand uit en redde hem. Jezus’ volgende woorden blijven ons uitdagen. Hij zei tegen Petrus: …O gij kleingelovige, waarom hebt gij getwijfeld? – Matteüs 14:31. Petrus had zo-even op het water gelopen—een prestatie die geen mens vóór of na hem had verricht, toch noemde Jezus het “kleingeloof” en vroeg: “waarom hebt gij getwijfeld?”.

Jezus zei op een ander moment: …Indien gij geloof hebt als een mosterdzaad, zult gij tot deze berg zeggen: Verwijder u hiertoe yonder, en zij zal zich verwijderen; en niets zal u onmogelijk zijn – Matteüs 17:20.

Als Petrus’ “kleingeloof” hem in staat stelde op het water te lopen, en als geloof zo klein als een mosterdzaad bergen kan verzetten, wat zegt dat dan over jouw en mijn geloof?

Misschien is het bewijs dat ons geloof nog kleiner is dan Petrus’ “kleingeloof” en fijnzinniger dan het kleine mosterdzaad?! Het is ook bewijs dat God klein geloof eert. Wat Hij niet eert is geen geloof. Na uw geloof geschiede u. Klein geloof… loop op het water! Geen geloof… zink onder de golven!

Aangezien Jezus de “Logos” is, is Hij de meester van de natuurlijke wereld en de geestelijke wereld. Hij bewees Zich de Meester van de wind en de golven—en als zij in het schip gekomen waren, hield de wind op – Matteüs 14:32. En Hij bewees Zich de Meester van de geestelijke wereld—en zij, die in het schip waren, kwamen en verneden Hem, zeggende: Voorwaar, Gij zijt de Zoon van God – Matteüs 14:33.

Wij, in onze westerse wereld, zijn zo verzadigd geraakt met materialisme dat wij makkelijk kunnen gaan geloven dat natuurlijke realiteiten de machtigste realiteiten zijn. Dit materialisme valt ons aan, niet alleen met de overvloed van materiële zaken, maar ook met een bombardement van humanistische filosofie. Humanistische filosofie is denken dat ontdaan is van geestelijke realiteit… dat ontdaan is van geloof.

Als jij, als man, merkt dat je zinkt in golven van wanhoop… hetzij financiële worstelingen… hetzij relationele moeilijkheden… morele mislukking of misschien ben je je eigen ergste criticus… mag ik je uitdagen je ogen op te heffen naar Degene die Logos is. Jezus is Degene die meester is van je omstandigheden en Degene die Heer van je ziel wil zijn. Jezus Heer van je ziel laten zijn is leven in geloofsgehoorzaamheid aan de radicale leer van Jezus.

Om in harmonie met de natuurlijke wereld te leven, eren wij de wetten der natuur. Als we een dak vervangen, respecteren we de wet van de zwaartekracht. Als we een voertuig besturen, minderen we voor bochten uit respect voor de wet van traagheid. Trotseer de natuurlijke wetten en iemand raakt gewond.

Om in harmonie met de geestelijke wereld te leven, eren wij de wet van Christus. Wij hebben onze naaste lief. Wij vergeven onze broeder. Wij houden onze huwelijksgeloften. Wij dragen …elkanders lasten, en zo vervult gij de wet van Christus – Galaten 6:2.

Mannen van geloof zijn mannen die afgestemd zijn op deze geestelijke realiteiten en hun leven dienovereenkomstig ordenen.

In the last couple of years, something that God has been working on in my heart is the area of submission. I don’t want to look back in a wrong way, but I see where I have failed my husband in the role that God has given for me to function as his helper, one that is meet for him. As I have been thinking about my own life, I have come to realize how important our role is as Christian women, in our homes and in the lives of our children.

I realize that our children are going to need to make their own decision when it comes to being a disciple of Christ, but my desire is that I am not the reason that our children rebel against the Word of God. When we honor our husbands the way that God has taught in His Word, the example of our lives will draw the unbelieving to Christ. In the flesh, we will not be able to honor our husbands in a way that will bring glory to God, but with Christ we can do all things according to His will.

I have a burden about this because in the last couple of months I have noticed how much our homes are under constant attack from the enemy of our souls, as he tries to use our flesh and the world. As I write on this, I don’t feel that I will do justice to it, so I will just write some of my thoughts and pray that all who read this article will be encouraged in their marriages to honor, respect, and love their husbands.

  • Nevertheless let … the wife see that she reverence her husband –Ephesians 5:33.
  • Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands… –1 Peter 3:1.
  • Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are… –1 Peter 3:6.
  • Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord –Ephesians 5:22.
  • But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God –1 Corinthians 11:3.
  • Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection. But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence. For Adam was first formed, then Eve. And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression –1 Timothy 2:11-14.
  • Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be [subject] to their own husbands in every thing –Ephesians 5:24.
  • Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law –1 Corinthians 14:34.

These Scriptures are not my own, but God’s. He gives us His Word to read and to live by because that is the only way we will be able to have peace and harmony in our homes. Even more importantly, the ONLY way that we can have a clear conscience before God is when we are in the center of His will.

When we think of submission, what comes to mind? Do we think that if we submit, we will be taken advantage of? Do we think that we are wiser than our husbands? I know to the flesh this sounds kind of hard, but if we could only realize that if we don’t allow our husbands to lead out and make decisions, we are only crippling them. The reality is that if our husbands make mistakes, it is okay because we ourselves make mistakes as well. Also, if we are born again, and we are walking with God, but our husbands are not, God will still take care of us. The Scriptures teach that if our husband is not in his place, then through the wife walking according to the clear teaching that God has given her in His Word, the husband can be won through her conversation (or by the way she conducts her life).

We need to trust God with our whole lives, even in the area of our marriage. God is a God of order. Think of how God desires the children to honor the parents and the parents to not provoke their children to anger; it’s no different in the husband-and-wife relationship. The husband is to love his wife as Christ loves the church, and the wife is to reverence her husband.

In the beginning, God created male and female. He created Adam and said that it was not good for man to be alone; then He created woman from the rib of Adam’s side. God’s heart in the beginning was that man and woman would be one, and together they would walk with God and glorify Him. Then through Adam and Eve yielding to temptation, sin was brought into the world. Whenever we are struggling in our marriage, I am reminded how it was Eve that first yielded to the serpent’s temptation. Let us as wives be quick to examine our own hearts to be sure that we are in our place. When situations arise, how often are we as women tempted to think that we know better and could handle the situation better than our husbands.

God has designed our husbands to be our protector if we stay under them. I realize that we are imperfect, and that makes it more challenging to submit to our husbands. However, I believe that when we are born again by the Spirit of God, His love in us enables us to submit to our husbands. I also realize that there are a lot of broken homes. My encouragement to anyone who is in a less than ideal situation is to sincerely pray…first for yourself that you can walk in a blameless way and also for your husband that he would be what God has designed him to be—not what you think he should be. Many times, we get confused about this and it causes us to have bad thoughts about our husbands.

Titus gives us sisters clear direction from God. The aged women likewise, that they be … teachers of good things; That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed –Titus 2:3-5.

Another temptation that we women face is to compare our husbands with other men. Perhaps we tell our husbands that this other man wouldn’t do such and such the way you do, or the way he does something is better than the way you do. Maybe we don’t even say these words, but our actions can tell our husbands a lot. God’s Word teaches us to be obedient to our own husbands, and not another. Each husband is gifted in a different way, and that is why each wife is especially suited for their husband. And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help [helper, aid, supporter] meet [suitable, appropriate, complementary] for him –Genesis 2:18.

That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children –Titus 2:4. The word “love,” in to love their husbands means “to be affectionately fond of their man” as compared to the word “love” in to love their children which means “to have a maternal fondness for one’s children”. What kind of love are we showing our husbands? Can our husbands trust us that we only have their good in mind, or do we pretend to love in order to get something in return? True love will forgive in spite of failures, even when we think the pain is too great to bear. True love will cause us to pray for ourselves and our husbands when we feel differently about something than they do. True love will not cause us to despair, rather it will cause us to seek God even more.

When we are tempted to speak about our husbands’ faults to others, let us not yield to that temptation but let’s pray for them. Would we appreciate our husbands talking about our faults to other people? Also, pray for discernment to know if, and when, to speak to someone about a sin that your husband may be involved in. Let us not rail on or nag our husbands when difficulties arise. Instead, let us ask God to work in our lives and give the problem to Him and let it there. Our husbands are only too human, just as we are. If we fail at times, then we must not be surprised that they too might fail at times as well. I think what makes our marriages perfect is that we learn to forgive one another and press on to be one together.

Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation [conduct] of the wives; While they behold your chaste [modest, innocent, perfect, pure] conversation coupled with fear. Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement [terror]. Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered –1 Peter 3:1-2 & 3:6-7.

One of the first times that this verse became real to us was when our first child was around five months old. We were quite a ways from home and he started crying with a lot of pain. We prayed for him, but he still cried. We could not figure out what was wrong, so we took him into the ER. They told us that he had an ear infection and gave us medication. However, he still cried. We had a ten-hour journey home, and he cried the whole way. After we had gotten home, my husband and I discovered that there were some unresolved things between us. After we confessed our wrongs to each other and to God, we prayed again for our son. Immediately after we prayed, our son quit crying. I know not every situation turns out like this one did, but God taught us that we need to be open with each other with no hidden sin, that our prayers be not hindered.

Some questions that could be asked are: What are our children seeing in our homes? Do they see Mom reverencing their dad with joy or with fear? Do they see Mom being appropriately affectionate with her husband, such as through kind words, seeking to love the things that he loves, holding hands, etc. (I have come to realize that it is difficult to hold hands with my husband if there is something between us.) Does Mom question, challenge, or criticize what Dad does?

As our own children are growing older and into their youth years, I see how important it is that these principles are lived out in our homes. If we openly question our husband’s authority, I believe we are sowing a seed in our children that they too will question their dad’s authority. Ultimately, in the time that we live, we are seeing a generation that is questioning everything about God’s created order—there is gender confusion, evolution, and rebellion against authority in general. I have often wondered if perhaps the reason that we see so much rebellion in our plain churches is because of God’s order not being lived out in our homes.

There was a friend of ours who told us that if there would be one Christian principle that he thought would have the most impact on the home, it would be the principle of the headship order. We have a dear friend who had become a Christian before her husband. She went through a lot of difficult times, but she continued to love and reverence her husband. She fasted and prayed for many years for her husband. Today her husband will testify that it was because of his wife’s godly conduct that drew him to repentance and faith in Christ.

Another example with a different outcome… I know of a couple that didn’t have a solid marriage. The husband was not in his place and the wife became bitter, so bitter in fact, that she said that when she is buried in the grave, she doesn’t want to be buried beside her husband. This much bitterness has had a terrible effect on their children. I wondered if she had not become bitter, if she could have at least spared her children from the many heartaches that they have suffered.

I also know of another couple where both of them were badly mistreated by close family, but they chose not to become bitter. They drew closer to God and to each other through those valleys and they are reaping the benefits of the fruit of their choices to this day.

Even closer to home… I grew up in a home that was not a Christian home. Neither of my parents were born again. When they began to allow God to work in their hearts, I could see it. I would come home from gatherings and see my dad weeping as he was reading his Bible. Also, on one particular evening I came home and saw my parents sitting at the table and they were singing together. I will testify that this had a tremendous effect on my life. I could also see my own mother desiring to be in her place as God had designed her to be. When we pass from this life, what will our family say about us? Will they testify that the love of God reigned in our mortal bodies?

On a practical note, I thought I would write a few ways that we can show that we love our husbands in deed and not just in word.

  • Asking them for advice (not just going on what we think)
  • Fixing their favorite foods
  • Keeping the house orderly and neat
  • Being ready and willing to drop our plans to help our husbands with whatever they need
  • Meeting them at the door with a smile (no matter how bad of day we may have had)
  • Keeping the house quiet, even with little children, when he’s trying to rest or study
  • Teaching our children proper manners in relating to each other in the home
  • Teaching our children to love and respect their father, even if he isn’t always perfect

Another challenge I wish to give to each married sister is to think of something that you can tell your husband that you are blessed about with him, Try doing this every day for two weeks. It’s amazing what effect kindness can have on a marriage. Maybe to some this would seem like drudgery, but it’s not. I am amazed that as we get older, how much we think alike, even sometimes finishing each other’s sentences. I realize there is so much more that could have been written. I trust that God will continue to open His Word to us as we seek Him.

Editor’s Note:

I was one who struggled majorly and for years with not knowing how to submit and yet wanting to. Following is my attempt to share what God has been teaching me.

One of the main reasons that many people struggle with “submission” is that they don’t really understand what God means with the subject—they don’t understand the reality of biblical submission. Usually, a person knows what they believe on a certain subject, so in their mind when they are being asked to “submit” on that point, they think they are being asked to compromise their personal belief—or sin against their conscience.

The answer is two-fold.

First, if two people agree on an issue, then there is no need for anyone to submit. Thus, to submit does not mean that the person submitting is necessarily changing their mind, rather they are choosing to support the other person’s decision based on the fact that God says that that person is the one He is holding responsible for the decisions of that party—whether it be a couple, the home, a school, a church, etc.

Second, God knew that whenever there would be more than one person discussing a decision that needs to be made, that it would always mean that the one would end up submitting to the other. Therefore, to provide clarity in responsibility, He gives clear direction regarding whom He considers the responsible person (the spiritual authority) in each type of situation—the husband in a marriage, the father in the family, the man (the head) in the home, the ordained leaders in the church, the schoolteachers/principal in the school setting, etc. That way everyone can know who God sees as responsible for any mistakes that are made.

Consider that even though Eve took the fruit and ate it first, and then gave it to her husband to eat, God provides us with clarity regarding who He holds responsible for that failure (sin). Wherefore, as by one man [not one woman] sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned … Nevertheless death reigned from Adam [not from Eve] to Moses, even over them [Adam’s descendants—all of the human race] that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam’s transgression… –Romans 5:12-14.

So, we see that God provides protection and security to all those who are under authority if they stay under that authority. The one who God clearly states as being the authority figure in each relationship will always be the one that God holds responsible for decisions made by that group of people. Just like in the fall in the Garden of Eden, sins of omission and of commission within each family will be primarily held to dad’s account. Whether dad was giving wrong direction to the family or if he was not giving direction at all, it doesn’t matter, he will still be held to account since God sees the man as being the head of his home. (see 1 Corinthians 11:3 and Romans 13:12)

In die afgelope paar jaar is daar iets waaraan God in my hart werk en dit is die gebied van onderwerping. Ek wil nie op ’n verkeerde wyse terugkyk nie, maar ek sien waar ek my man in die rol wat God vir my gegee het as sy hulp, een wat by hom pas, gefaal het. Terwyl ek oor my eie lewe nadink, het ek besef hoe belangrik ons rol is as Christenvroue, in ons huise en in die lewens van ons kinders.

Ek besef dat ons kinders self hul eie besluit sal moet neem wanneer dit by die volgskap van Christus kom, maar my begeerte is dat ek nie die rede wees dat ons kinders by die Woord van God rebelleer nie. Wanneer ons ons mans eer op die manier wat God in Sy Woord geleer het, sal die voorbeeld van ons lewens die ongelowiges na Christus toe trek. In die vlees sal ons nie in staat wees om ons mans so te eer dat dit God verheerlik nie, maar met Christus kan ons alle dinge doen volgens Sy wil.

Ek dra ’n las oor dit omdat ek die afgelope paar maande gesien het hoe ons huise konstant aangeval word deur die vyand van ons siele, soos hy probeer om ons vlees en die wêreld te gebruik. Terwyl ek hieroor skryf, voel ek nie dat ek geregtigheid daaraan sal doen nie, so ek sal net ’n paar van my gedagtes neerskryf en bid dat almal wat hierdie artikel lees, in hul huwelike bemoedig sal word om hul mans te eer, te respekteer en lief te hê.

  • Desnieteenstaande, laat … die vrou sien dat sy respek vir haar man het – Efesiërs 5:33.
  • Eveneens, julle vroue, wees onderdanig aan julle eie mans… – 1 Petrus 3:1.
  • Soos Sara gehoorsaam was aan Abraham en hom Here noem: aan wie julle dogters is… – 1 Petrus 3:6.
  • Vroue, onderwerp julle aan julle eie mans, soos aan die Here – Efesiërs 5:22.
  • Maar ek wil julle laat weet, dat die hoof van elke man Christus is; en die hoof van die vrou is die man; en die hoof van Christus is God – 1 Korintiërs 11:3.
  • Laat die vrou in stilte met alle onderdanigheid leer. Ek laat nie toe dat ’n vrou leer, of oor die man heers nie, maar sy moet in stilte wees. Want Adam is eers gevorm, daarna Eva. En Adam is nie bedrieglik geword nie, maar die vrou is deur die verleier mislei en het oortree – 1 Timoteus 2:11-14.
  • Soos die kerk aan Christus onderwerp is, so moet ook die vroue aan hul eie mans in alles onderdanig wees – Efesiërs 5:24.
  • Laat julle vroue stil wees in die kerk: want dit is hulle nie toegestaan om te praat nie; maar hulle word beveel om onderdanig te wees, soos ook die wet sê – 1 Korintiërs 14:34.

Hierdie Skrifte is nie my eie nie, maar God se. Hy gee ons Sy Woord om te lees en daarna te leef, want dit is die enigste manier waarop ons vrede en harmonie in ons huise sal hê. Nog belangriker, die ENIGE manier waarop ons ’n skoon gewete voor God kan hê, is wanneer ons in die sentrum van Sy wil is.

Wanneer ons aan onderwerping dink, wat kom by ons op? Dink ons dat as ons onderwerp, ons uitgebuit sal word? Dink ons dat ons wyser as ons mans is? Ek weet dat dit in die vlees nogal hard klink, maar as ons net sou besef dat as ons nie ons mans toelaat om leiding te neem en besluite te neem nie, ons net hulle verkrag. Die realiteit is dat as ons mans foute maak, dit reg is omdat ons self ook foute maak. Ook, as ons wedergebore is en met God wandel, maar ons mans nie, sal God steeds vir ons sorg. Die Skrifte leer dat as ons man nie in sy plek is nie, deur die vrou wat wandel volgens die duidelike onderrig wat God haar in Sy Woord gee, die man deur haar gesprek (of deur die manier waarop sy haar lewe voer) gewen kan word.

Ons moet God vertrou met ons hele lewe, selfs in die gebied van ons huwelik. God is ’n God van orde. Dink daaraan hoe God verlang dat kinders hul ouers eer en ouers hul kinders nie tot toorn moet aanhits nie; dit is nie anders in die man-en-vrou verhouding nie. Die man moet sy vrou liefhê soos Christus die kerk liefhet, en die vrou moet haar man eerbiedig.

In die begin het God manlik en vroulik geskep. Hy het Adam geskep en gesê dat dit nie goed was dat die mens alleen moet wees nie; toe het Hy die vrou gemaak uit die rib van Adam se sy. God se hart in die begin was dat man en vrou een sou wees, en saam met God sou wandel en Hom verheerlik. Toe, deurdat Adam en Eva aan die versoeking toegegee het, is sonde in die wêreld gebring. Wanneer ons in ons huwelike worstel, word ek herinner dat dit Eva was wat eerste aan die slang se versoeking toegegee het. Laat ons as vroue vinnig ons eie harte ondersoek om seker te maak dat ons in ons plek is. Wanneer situasies ontstaan, hoe gereeld word ons as vroue in versoeking gebring om te dink dat ons beter weet en die situasie beter as ons mans kan hanteer.

God het ons mans ontwerp om ons beskermers te wees as ons onder hulle bly. Ek besef dat ons onvolmaak is, en dit maak dit meer uitdagend om aan ons mans gehoorsaam te wees. Tog glo ek dat wanneer ons deur die Gees van God wedergebore is, Sy liefde in ons ons in staat stel om aan ons mans te onderwerp. Ek besef ook dat daar baie gebroke huise is. My aanmoediging aan enigiemand wat in ’n minder as ideale situasie is, is om opreg te bid… eerstens vir jouself sodat jy onbeskuldig kan wandel en ook vir jou man dat hy sal wees wat God hom bedoel het om te wees—nie wat jy dink hy behoort te wees nie. Baie keer raak ons deurmekaar oor dit en dit veroorsaak dat ons slegte gedagtes oor ons mans kry.

Titus gee vir ons susters duidelike rigting van God. En die ouer vroue ook, moet wees … leraars van goeie dinge; sodat hulle die jong vroue leer om ernstig te wees, om hul mans lief te hê, om hul kinders lief te hê, om verstandig te wees, kuis, huisbewaarsters, goeie, onderdanig aan hul eie mans, sodat die woord van God nie gelaster word nie – Titus 2:3-5.

’n Ander versoeking wat ons vroue in die gesig staar, is om ons mans met ander mans te vergelyk. Miskien sê ons vir ons mans dat daardie ander man nie sulks en sulks sou doen soos jy doen nie, of die manier waarop hy iets doen is beter as jou manier. Miskien sê ons hierdie woorde nie eens nie, maar ons dade kan baie aan ons mans sê. God se Woord leer ons om aan ons eie mans gehoorsaam te wees, en nie ’n ander man nie. Elke man is op ’n ander manier begaaf, en daarom is elke vrou spesiaal geskik vir haar man. En die HERE God het gesê: Dit is nie goed dat die mens alleen is; Ek sal vir hom ’n hulp geskik maak – Genesis 2:18.

Dat hulle die jong vroue leer om ernstig te wees, om hul mans lief te hê, om hul kinders lief te hê – Titus 2:4. Die woord “lief” in om hul mans lief te hê beteken “om innig aan hul man geheg te wees” in vergelyking met die woord “lief” in om hul kinders lief te hê wat beteken “om ’n moederlike liefde vir een se kinders te hê”. Watter soort liefde toon ons vir ons mans? Kan ons mans ons vertrou dat ons net hul beste in gedagte het, of doen ons voor om lief te hê om iets in ruil te kry? Ware liefde sal vergewe ondanks mislukkings, selfs wanneer ons dink die pyn is te groot om te dra. Ware liefde sal ons laat bid vir onsself en vir ons mans wanneer ons anders oor iets voel as hulle. Ware liefde sal ons nie tot moedeloosheid dryf nie, maar sal ons eerder aanspoor om nog meer na God te soek.

Wanneer ons in versoeking kom om oor ons mans se foute aan ander te praat, laat ons nie daardie versoeking toegee nie, maar laat ons eerder vir hulle bid. Sou ons dit waardeer as ons mans ons foute aan ander mense vertel? Bid ook vir onderskeiding om te weet of, en wanneer, om met iemand te praat oor ’n sonde waarin jou man betrokke mag wees. Laat ons nie ons mans beledig of aanraak wanneer moeilikhede ontstaan nie. In plaas daarvan, laat ons God vra om in ons lewens te werk en die probleem aan Hom oor te laat en dit daar te laat lê. Ons mans is net so menslik soos ons. As ons soms faal, dan moet ons nie verbaas wees dat hulle ook soms mag faal nie. Ek dink wat ons huwelike volmaak maak, is dat ons leer om mekaar te vergewe en aan te hou om een saam te wees.

Eveneens, julle vroue, wees onderdanig aan julle eie mans; sodat, as iemand die woord nie gehoorsaam nie, hulle ook sonder die woord deur die gesprek [gedrag] van die vroue gewen mag word; terwyl hulle julle kuise [reserwe, onskuldige, volmaakte, suiwer] gesprek saam met vrees aanskou. Soos Sara gehoorsaam was aan Abraham en hom Here noem: aan wie julle dogters is, solank julle wel doen en nie met enige ontsteltenis [terreur] vrees nie. Net so, julle mans, woon by hulle volgens kennis, gee eer aan die vrou as aan die swakere vat, en as mede-erwe van die genade van die lewe; sodat julle gebede nie verhinder word nie – 1 Petrus 3:1-2 & 3:6-7.

Een van die eerste kere toe hierdie vers vir ons werklikheid geword het, was toe ons eerste kind ongeveer vyf maande oud was. Ons was nogal ver van huis en hy het begin huil van baie pyn. Ons het vir hom gebid, maar hy het steeds gehuil. Ons kon nie uitvind wat verkeerd was nie, so ons het hom na die noodkamer geneem. Hulle het vir ons gesê dat hy ’n oorinfeksie het en het medikasie gegee. Hy het egter steeds gehuil. Ons het ’n tien uur se reis huis toe gehad, en hy het die hele pad gehuil. Nadat ons tuis gekom het, het my man en ek ontdek dat daar onopgeloste dinge tussen ons was. Nadat ons ons verkeerdes aan mekaar en aan God bely het, het ons weer vir ons seun gebid. Onmiddellik nadat ons gebid het, het ons seun opgehou huil. Ek weet nie elke situasie verloop soos hierdie een nie, maar God het ons geleer dat ons oop met mekaar moet wees sonder verborge sonde, sodat ons gebede nie verhinder word nie.

’n Paar vrae wat gevra kan word is: Wat sien ons kinders in ons huise? Sien hulle Mamma haar pa met blydskap of met vrees eerbiedig? Sien hulle Mamma gepaste toewyding aan haar man, soos deur vriendelike woorde, om die dinge wat hy liefhet te wil liefhê, hande vashou, ens. (Ek het besef dit is moeilik om hande met my man te hou as daar iets tussen ons is.) Vra Mamma, bevraagteken, daag of kritiseer wat Pa doen?

Soos ons eie kinders ouer word en hul jeugjare betree, sien ek hoe belangrik dit is dat hierdie beginsels in ons huise geleef word. As ons openlik ons man se gesag bevraagteken, glo ek ons saai ’n saad in ons kinders dat hulle ook hul pa se gesag sal bevraagteken. Uiteindelik, in die tyd waarin ons leef, sien ons ’n generasie wat alles oor God se geskape orde bevraagteken—daar is geslagsverwarring, evolusie, en rebellie teen gesag in die algemeen. Ek het dikwels gewonder of miskien die rede dat ons soveel rebellie in ons eenvoudige kerke sien, is omdat God se orde nie in ons huise beoefen word nie.

Daar was ’n vriend van ons wat vir ons gesê het dat as daar een Christelike beginsel sou wees wat volgens hom die grootste impak op die huis sou hê, sou dit die beginsel van hoofskapsorde wees. Ons het ’n dierbare vriendin wat voor haar man ’n Christen geword het. Sy het baie moeilike tye deurgegaan, maar sy het aanhou om haar man lief te hê en hom te eerbiedig. Sy het baie jare gevast en gebid vir haar man. Vandag sal haar man getuig dat dit was vanweë sy vrou se goddelike gedrag dat hy tot bekeering en geloof in Christus getrek is.

Nog ’n voorbeeld met ’n ander uitkoms… Ek ken ’n paar wat nie ’n stewige huwelik gehad het nie. Die man was nie in sy plek nie en die vrou het bitter geword, so bitter dat sy gesê het dat wanneer sy in die graf begrawe word, sy nie langs haar man begrawe wil word nie. So ’n mate van bitterheid het ’n verskriklike uitwerking op hul kinders gehad. Ek het gewonder of sy nie bitter geword het nie, of sy ten minste haar kinders sou kon spaar van die baie hartseer wat hulle ervaar het.

Ek ken ook ’n ander paar waar albei sleg behandel is deur naaste familie, maar hulle het besluit om nie bitter te word nie. Hulle het deur daardie dale nader aan God en aan mekaar getrek en hulle pluk tot op hede die voordele van die vrugte van hul keuses.

Nog nader aan huis… Ek het in ’n huis grootgeword wat nie ’n Christelike huis was nie. Geen van my ouers was wedergebore nie. Toe hulle begin toelaat dat God in hul harte werk, kon ek dit sien. Ek sou van byeenkomste kom en my pa sien huil terwyl hy sy Bybel lees. Ook, op een bepaalde aand het ek tuis gekom en my ouers by die tafel sien sit en hulle het saam gesing. Ek sal getuig dat dit ’n geweldige uitwerking op my lewe gehad het. Ek kon ook sien dat my eie ma begeer het om in haar plek te wees soos God haar ontwerp het om te wees. Wanneer ons van hierdie lewe oorgaan, wat sal ons familie oor ons sê? Sal hulle getuig dat die liefde van God in ons sterflike liggame geheers het?

Op ’n praktiese noot, het ek gedink ek sal ’n paar maniere neerpen waarop ons kan wys dat ons ons mans in daad liefhet en nie net met woorde nie.

  • Om hulle om raad te vra (nie net te doen wat ons dink nie)
  • Om hul gunstelingkosse te maak
  • Om die huis ordelik en netjies te hou
  • Om gereed en gewillig te wees om ons planne te laat vaar om ons mans te help met wat hulle ook al nodig het
  • Om hulle by die deur te ontvang met ’n glimlag (maak nie saak hoe sleg ons dag was nie)
  • Om die huis rustig te hou, selfs met klein kinders, wanneer hy probeer rus of studeer
  • Om ons kinders behoorlike maniere by te bring in hoe om aan mekaar in die huis te verwys
  • Om ons kinders te leer om hul vader lief te hê en te respekteer, selfs al is hy nie altyd perfek nie

Nog ’n uitdaging wat ek aan elke getroude suster wil gee is om iets te dink wat jy elke dag vir jou man kan sê dat jy oor hom geseënd is. Probeer dit elke dag vir twee weke doen. Dit is ongelooflik watter effek vriendelikheid op ’n huwelik kan hê. Vir sommige mag dit as vervelig voorkom, maar dit is dit nie. Ek is verbaas oor hoe, soos ons ouer word, ons soveel dink dieselfde, soms mekaar se sinne afmaak. Ek besef daar is soveel meer wat geskryf kon gewees het. Ek vertrou dat God Sy Woord aan ons sal bly oopmaak soos ons Hom soek.

Redakteur se Nota:

Ek was een wat jare lank grootliks gesukkel het met nie te weet hoe om te onderwerp en tog te wil. Wat volg is my poging om te deel wat God my geleer het.

Een van die hoofredes waarom baie mense met “onderwerping” sukkel, is omdat hulle nie regtig verstaan wat God met die onderwerp bedoel nie—hulle verstaan nie die realiteit van Bybelse onderwerping nie. Gewoonlik weet ’n persoon wat hulle oor ’n bepaalde onderwerp glo, so in hul gedagte wanneer hulle gevra word om op daardie punt te “onderwerp”, dink hulle dat hulle gevra word om hul persoonlike oortuiging in te gee—of teen hul gewete te sondig.

Die antwoord het twee aspekte.

Eerstens, as twee mense oor ’n saak saamstem, is daar geen behoefte vir iemand om te onderwerp nie. Dus beteken onderwerp nie noodwendig dat die persoon wat onderwerp, hul gemoed verander nie, eerder kies hulle om die besluit van die ander persoon te ondersteun gebaseer op die feit dat God sê dat daardie persoon die een is wat Hy verantwoordelik hou vir die besluite van daardie party—wees dit ’n egpaar, die huis, ’n skool, ’n kerk, ens.

Tweedens, God het geweet dat wanneer daar meer as een persoon sou wees wat ’n besluit bespreek wat geneem moet word, dit altyd sal beteken dat die een uiteindelik aan die ander sou onderwerp. Daarom, om duidelikheid in verantwoordelikheid te voorsien, gee Hy duidelike rigting oor wie Hy as die verantwoordelike persoon (die geestelike gesag) in elke tipe situasie beskou—die man in ’n huwelik, die vader in die familie, die man (die hoof) in die huis, die aangestelde leiers in die kerk, die skoolonderwysers/hoof in die skoolomgewing, ens. Sodanig kan almal weet wie God as verantwoordelik vir enige foute wat gemaak word, sien.

Oorweeg dat al het Eva die vrug geneem en eerste geëet, en toe dit aan haar man gegee het om te eet, God ons duidelikheid voorsien oor wie Hy aanspreeklik hou vir daardie mislukking (sonde). Daarom, soos deur een man [nie een vrou nie] die sonde in die wêreld ingekom het, en die dood deur die sonde; en so het die dood op alle mense oorgegaan, omdat almal gesondig het … Nietemin het die dood van Adam af geregeer [nie van Eva af nie] tot Moses, selfs oor die wat nie gesondig het na die gelykenis van Adam se oortreding nie… – Romeine 5:12-14.

So, ons sien dat God beskerming en sekuriteit verskaf aan almal wat onder gesag is as hulle onder daardie gesag bly. Die een wat God duidelik verklaar as die gesagsfiguur in elke verhouding, sal altyd die persoon wees wat God aanspreeklik hou vir besluite wat deur daardie groep mense gemaak word. Net soos in die val in die Tuin van Eden, sal sondes van versuim en van kommissie binne elke familie hoofsaaklik aan pa se rekening toegeskryf word. Of pa nou verkeerde rigting aan die gesin gegee het of geen rigting gegee het nie, dit maak nie saak nie; hy sal steeds aanspreeklik gehou word aangesien God die man as die hoof van sy huis sien. (sien 1 Korintiërs 11:3 en Romeine 13:12)

This hymn is generally considered to be one of the greatest hymns ever written and is found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. It was written by a man who was frail in body, but strong in spirit. It was he who coined the phrase, “It is better to wear out than to rust out.” Let us now take a glimpse into the life of this servant of God.

Henry Francis Lyte, the author of this great and noteworthy hymn, was born June 1, 1793, in Ednam, near Kelso, Scotland. At a young age, he was left an orphan and was in comparative poverty. He was educated at Trinity College in Dublin, Ireland. It was there that his gift of poetry began to appear, winning him three prizes. His primary goal with his studies was to become a physician, instead, by the providence of God, he became a minister of the gospel of Jesus Christ.

One day in Cornwall, a fellow clergyman who was on his deathbed, requested that Lyte would come and give him some spiritual comfort. “To their mutual grief, they found themselves [both] groping for the light, veritable blind guides”. As they searched for truth and assurance of salvation, they fixed their faith on Christ, and Lyte came away from that sickroom a changed man, never to be the same again. It is said that it was his encounter with God at the bedside of that dying man that prompted Lyte’s noble hymn, “Jesus, I My Cross Have Taken.” In the year 1823, Henry F. Lyte took charge of a seashore parish, Lower Brixham, in Devonshire, England. It was at that place where he spent the last 23 years of his life toiling as a pastor for the spiritual good of the poor fishing people and the rough seafaring men of that region until his death in the fall of 1847. For all of Henry’s dedication and labor, he received a reward: having a Sunday school of several hundred scholars, as well as “a splendid company of seventy or eighty teachers, personally trained by him.”

Throughout his lifetime, his health was continually threatened by asthma and tuberculosis. Notwithstanding his physical frailties, he worked tirelessly with an established reputation as a poet, musician, and minister. Wherever he went, he was greatly loved and admired by his people. Toward the end of these later years, his health became gradually worse. So it was that during the winter months, he felt compelled to seek a warmer climate in Italy, which is a part of southern Europe.

Though he was greatly weakened by his sickness, on September 4, 1847, as Lyte was about to leave to head southward, he was arrested by an “irresistible desire” to preach once more to his congregation. He dearly loved these people and he had labored among them for so many years. “Against the protest of his amazed friends, he accomplished this purpose, and it is recorded that Lyte nearly had to crawl to the pulpit and his message came as from a dying man.” “O brethren,” he said, as he entered the familiar pulpit for the last time, “I stand here among you today, as alive from the dead, if I may hope to impress it upon you, and induce you to prepare for that solemn hour which must come to all, by a timely appreciation and dependance on the death of Christ.” These final words made a deep impact upon his congregation, after which he closed the service by administering the Lord’s Supper to his weeping people. Later that evening, after the service, he was inspired to “poetical composition” and wrote the eight stanzas of his last and greatest hymn:

Abide with me: fast falls the eventide;
The darkness deepens; Lord, with me abide:
when other helpers fail, and comforts flee,
Help of the helpless, O abide with me.

Swift to its close ebbs out life’s little day;
Earth’s joys grow dim, its glories pass away;
Change and decay in all around I see;
O Thou who changest not, abide with me.

Not a brief glance I beg, a passing word;
But, as Thou dwell’st with Thy disciples, Lord,
Familiar, condescending, patient, free,
Come, not to sojourn, but abide, with me.

Come not in terrors, as the King of kings;
But kind and good, with healing in Thy wings;
Tears for all woes, a heart for every plea;
Come, Friend of sinners, and thus ‘bide with me.

Thou on my head in early youth didst smile;
And, though rebellious and perverse meanwhile,
thou hast not left me, oft as I left thee:
On to the close, O Lord, abide with me.

I need Thy presence every passing hour;
What but Thy grace can foil the tempter’s power?
Who like Thyself my guide and stay can be?
Through cloud and sunshine, O abide with me.

I fear no foe, with Thee at hand to bless:
Ills have no weight, and tears no bitterness.
Where is death’s sting? Where, grave, thy victory?
I triumph still, if Thou abide with me.

Hold Thou Thy cross before my closing eyes;
Shine through the gloom, and point me to the skies;
Heaven’s morning breaks, and earth’s vain shadows flee:
In life, in death, O Lord, abide with me.

This hymn he gave to one of the family members that very night. Leaving the following day, he began his trek to Rome, Italy, hoping to gain some relief from his sickness. Lyte make it as far as Nice, France where his sickness prevented his further travel. He passed away soon after the age of 55, on November 20, 1847. His last words were “Joy! Peace!”

The scene behind this hymn is that of the resurrected Christ Jesus walking on the road to Emmaus with two of His somewhat sad and discouraged disciples. As they neared the end of their seven-mile walk and approached the village where they were going, Jesus …made as though he would have gone further. But they constrained him, saying, Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them –Luke 24:28-29.

We can draw a parallel between that scene and Henry F. Lyte’s own experience of drawing toward the close of his earthly journey. Thus, as the disciples besought the risen Lord to abide with them in the close of that ancient day, so was the meaning of this song written in the “shadows of death” to the hymn writer.

Lyte himself composed a tune for this hymn on the same evening that he wrote it, but it never became widely used. However, the tune universally used was written fourteen years later by William Henry Monk, a noted London musician, and editor of the well-known Anglican hymnal, Hymns Ancient and Modern. He included this song in his first edition, which was published in 1861.

In all, William H. Monk composed 50 tunes for the hymnal. It is said that Monk, being “inspired by the beauty of a glorious sunset while yet experiencing a deep personal sorrow,” composed (in only 10 minutes) the tune, Eventide, for the song, “Abide With Me, Fast Falls The Eventide”. William Monk also wrote the music for other familiar hymns such as “Look, Ye Saints! The Sight Is Glorious”, and “The Strife Is O’er”.

To summarize, Henry Lyte experienced many sorrows during his lifetime. Both of his parents died at an early age leaving him an orphan. And his own sickness and frailty caused him to be in ongoing danger of asthma and tuberculosis. Yet, in spite of all his trials, we find in him a resilient spirit to reach out to others; to touch and minister the Gospel to those poor people among whom he lived. “In no other writer,” says Dr. Breed (in the Treasury of Hymn Stories), “are poetry and religion more exquisitely united.”

Αυτός ο ύμνος θεωρείται γενικά ως ένας από τους σπουδαιότερους ύμνους που έχουν γραφτεί ποτέ και βρίσκεται σχεδόν σε κάθε ύμνο ή βιβλίο ύμνων που εκδίδεται σήμερα. Γράφτηκε από έναν άνθρωπο που ήταν ευάλωτος στο σώμα, αλλά δυνατός στο πνεύμα. Αυτός που επινόησε τη φράση «Καλύτερα να φθαρείς παρά να σκουριάσεις.» Ας ρίξουμε τώρα μια ματιά στη ζωή αυτού του δούλου του Θεού.

Ο Henry Francis Lyte, ο συγγραφέας αυτού του μεγάλου και αξιοσημείωτου ύμνου, γεννήθηκε την 1η Ιουνίου 1793 στο Ednam, κοντά στο Kelso της Σκωτίας. Σε μικρή ηλικία έμεινε ορφανός και βρισκόταν σε σχετική φτώχεια. Σπούδασε στο Trinity College στο Δουβλίνο της Ιρλανδίας. Εκεί άρχισε να φαίνεται το ποιητικό του χάρισμα, κερδίζοντας τρία βραβεία. Ο πρωταρχικός του στόχος με τις σπουδές του ήταν να γίνει ιατρός· αντ’ αυτού, με τη διακυβέρνηση του Θεού, έγινε κήρυκας του ευαγγελίου του Ιησού Χριστού.

Μια μέρα στην Κορνουάλη, ένας συνάδελφος κληρικός που βρισκόταν σε κοιτώνα θανάτου, ζήτησε από τον Lyte να έρθει και να του δώσει πνευματική παρηγοριά. «Προς της αμοιβαίας τους λύπης, βρέθηκαν [και οι δύο] να ψάχνουν το φως, αληθινοί τυφλοί οδηγοί». Καθώς έψαχναν την αλήθεια και τη βεβαιότητα της σωτηρίας, στερέωσαν την πίστη τους στον Χριστό, και ο Lyte βγήκε από εκείνο το δωμάτιο ασθενή αλλαγμένος άνθρωπος, για να μην είναι ποτέ πια ο ίδιος. Λέγεται ότι η συνάντησή του με τον Θεό στο προσκέφαλο εκείνου του πεθαίνοντος ανθρώπου προκάλεσε τον ευγενή ύμνο του Lyte, «Jesus, I My Cross Have Taken.» Το 1823, ο Henry F. Lyte ανέλαβε την ευθύνη μιας παραθαλάσσιας ενορίας, της Lower Brixham, στο Devonshire της Αγγλίας. Ήταν εκεί όπου πέρασε τα τελευταία 23 χρόνια της ζωής του εργαζόμενος ως ποιμένας για το πνευματικό καλό των φτωχών ψαράδων και των σκληροτράχηλων ναυτικών της περιοχής μέχρι τον θάνατό του το φθινόπωρο του 1847. Για όλη την αφοσίωση και τον κόπο του Henry, έλαβε μια ανταμοιβή: είχε μια Κυριακάτικη σχολή με αρκετές εκατοντάδες μαθητές, καθώς και «μια εξαίρετη ομάδα εβδομήντα ή ογδόντα διδασκόντων, προσωπικά εκπαιδευμένων από αυτόν.»

Καθ’ όλη τη διάρκεια της ζωής του, η υγεία του απειλούνταν συνεχώς από άσθμα και φυματίωση. Παρά τις σωματικές αδυναμίες του, εργάστηκε ακούραστα με καθιερωμένη φήμη ως ποιητής, μουσικός και κήρυκας. Όπου και αν πήγαινε, αγαπιόταν και θαυμαζόταν πολύ από τον λαό του. Προς το τέλος αυτών των τελευταίων χρόνων, η υγεία του χειροτέρευε βαθμιαία. Έτσι, κατά τη διάρκεια των χειμερινών μηνών ένιωσε την ανάγκη να αναζητήσει πιο θερμό κλίμα στην Ιταλία, που είναι μέρος της νότιας Ευρώπης.

Παρά το ότι ήταν πολύ εξασθενημένος από την αρρώστια του, στις 4 Σεπτεμβρίου 1847, καθώς ο Lyte ετοιμαζόταν να αναχωρήσει προς νότο, τον προσέλκυσε μια «ακαταμάχητη επιθυμία» να κηρύξει ακόμη μία φορά στο ποίμνιό του. Αγαπούσε βαθιά αυτούς τους ανθρώπους και είχε εργαστεί ανάμεσά τους για τόσα χρόνια. «Ενάντια στην αντίρρηση των εμβρόντητων φίλων του, εκπλήρωσε αυτόν τον σκοπό, και καταγράφεται ότι ο Lyte σχεδόν έπρεπε να σέρνεται προς το άμβωνά του και το μήνυμά του ακουγόταν σαν από έναν πεθαίνοντα άνθρωπο.» «Ω αδελφοί,» είπε, καθώς ανέβηκε στο γνώριμο άμβωνα για τελευταία φορά, «βρίσκομαι εδώ ανάμεσά σας σήμερα, σαν ζωντανός εκ των νεκρών, αν μπορώ να ελπίζω να σας το επιβάλω, και να σας ωθήσω να προετοιμαστείτε για εκείνη την επισημην ώρα που πρέπει να έρθει σε όλους, με έναν έγκαιρο εκτίμηση και εξάρτηση στον θάνατο του Χριστού.» Αυτά τα τελευταία λόγια έκαναν βαθιά εντύπωση στο ποιμνιό του, μετά από τα οποία έκλεισε τη λατρεία χορηγώντας τη Θεία Κοινωνία στο κλαίον λαό του. Αργότερα εκείνο το βράδυ, μετά τη λατρεία, αισθάνθηκε έμπνευση για «ποιητική σύνθεση» και έγραψε τις οκτώ στροφές του τελευταίου και σπουδαιότερου ύμνου του:

Μείνε μαζί μου: γρήγορα πέφτει η δύση·
Το σκοτάδι βαθαίνει· Κύριε, μείνε μαζί μου·
όταν άλλοι βοηθοί αποτυγχάνουν, και παρηγοριές φεύγουν,
Βοήθεια των αβοήθητων, ω μείνε μαζί μου.

Γρήγορα εκπνέει η μικρή ημέρα της ζωής·
Οι χαρές της γης θαμπώνουν, οι δόξες της παρέρχονται·
Αλλαγή και φθορά βλέπω παντού γύρω μου·
Ω Εσύ που δεν αλλάζεις, μείνε μαζί μου.

Δεν ζητώ μια σύντομη ματιά, έναν εφήμερο λόγο·
Αλλά, όπως συ διαμένεις με τους μαθητές Σου, Κύριε,
Οικείος, ταπεινός, υπομονετικός, ελεύθερος,
Έλα, όχι για λίγες μέρες, αλλά μείνε μαζί μου.

Μη έρθεις σε τρόμους, ως Βασιλιάς των βασιλιάδων·
Αλλά καλός και αγαθός, με θεραπεία στα φτερά Σου·
Δάκρυα για κάθε κακό, καρδιά για κάθε παράκληση·
Έλα, Φίλε των αμαρτωλών, και έτσι μείνε μαζί μου.

Σε νεανική μου ηλικία χαμογέλασες στο κεφάλι μου·
Και, αν και επαναστατικός και διεφθαρμένος ενδιάμεσα,
δεν με εγκατέλειψες, όσο εγώ σε εγκατέλειψα·
Έως το τέλος, ω Κύριε, μείνε μαζί μου.

Χρειάζομαι την παρουσία Σου κάθε περαστική ώρα·
Τι άλλο εκτός από τη χάρη Σου μπορεί να ανακόψει τη δύναμη του πειραστή;
Ποιος σαν Εσένα μπορεί να είναι οδηγός και στηρίγμα μου;
Μέσα από σύννεφο και ήλιο, ω μείνε μαζί μου.

Δεν φοβάμαι εχθρό, με Σένα κοντά να ευλογείς·
Τα κακά δεν έχουν βάρος, και τα δάκρυα δεν έχουν πικρία·
Πού είναι το κεντρί του θανάτου; Πού, τάφε, η νίκη σου;
Εξακολουθώ να θριαμβεύω, αν Εσύ μείνεις μαζί μου.

Κράτα Σταυρό Σου μπροστά στα κλείνοντα μάτια μου·
Λάμψε μέσα στο σκότος, και δείξε με προς τους ουρανούς·
Το πρωινό του ουρανού ανατέλλει, και οι μάταιες σκιές της γης φεύγουν·
Εν ζωή, εν θανάτω, ω Κύριε, μείνε μαζί μου.

Αυτόν τον ύμνο τον έδωσε σε ένα από τα μέλη της οικογένειας εκείνο το βράδυ. Φεύγοντας την επόμενη μέρα, άρχισε το ταξίδι του προς τη Ρώμη της Ιταλίας, ελπίζοντας να ανακουφιστεί από την αρρώστια του. Ο Lyte έφτασε ως το Νις της Γαλλίας όπου η αρρώστια του εμπόδισε την περαιτέρω πορεία. Πέθανε λίγο μετά τα 55 του χρόνια, στις 20 Νοεμβρίου 1847. Τα τελευταία του λόγια ήταν «Χαρά! Ειρήνη!»

Η σκηνή πίσω από αυτόν τον ύμνο είναι εκείνη του αναστημένου Χριστού Ιησού που περπατά στον δρόμο προς την Εμμαούς με δύο από τους κάπως θλιμμένους και απογοητευμένους μαθητές Του. Καθώς πλησίαζαν το τέλος του επταμίλιου περπατήματός τους και την προσέγγιση του χωριού όπου πορεύονταν, ο Ιησούς …έδειχνε ότι θα προχωρούσε περαιτέρω. Αλλά εκείνοι τον παρεκάλεσαν λέγοντας, Μείνε μαζί μας· γιατί προς το εσπέραν κλίνει η ημέρα και έχει παρέλθει. Και αυτός μπήκε να μείνει μαζί τους –Λουκ. 24:28-29.

Μπορούμε να αντλήσουμε ένα παράλληλο ανάμεσα σε εκείνη τη σκηνή και την ίδια την εμπειρία του Henry F. Lyte που πλησίαζε το τέλος του γήινου ταξιδιού του. Έτσι, όπως οι μαθητές παρακάλεσαν τον ανασταμένο Κύριο να μείνει μαζί τους στο τέλος εκείνης της αρχαίας ημέρας, έτσι γράφτηκε το νόημα αυτού του τραγουδιού στα «σκιές του θανάτου» για τον συγγραφέα του ύμνου.

Ο ίδιος ο Lyte συνέθεσε μια μελωδία για αυτόν τον ύμνο το ίδιο βράδυ που τον έγραψε, αλλά δεν έγινε ευρύτατα χρησιμοποιημένη. Ωστόσο, η μελωδία που χρησιμοποιείται καθολικά γράφτηκε δεκατέσσερα χρόνια αργότερα από τον William Henry Monk, έναν εξέχοντα Λονδρέζο μουσικό και επιμελητή του γνωστού αγγλικανικού ύμνολογίου, Hymns Ancient and Modern. Την συμπεριέλαβε στην πρώτη του έκδοση, η οποία δημοσιεύθηκε το 1861.

Συνολικά, ο William H. Monk συνέθεσε 50 μελωδίες για το ύμνολογιο. Λέγεται ότι ο Monk, «εμπνευσμένος από την ομορφιά μιας ένδοξης δύσης ενώ ακόμη βίωνε βαθιά προσωπική λύπη», συνέθεσε (σε μόλις 10 λεπτά) τη μελωδία Eventide για το τραγούδι «Μείνε Μαζί Μου, Γρήγορα Πέφτει Η Δύση». Ο William Monk επίσης έγραψε τη μουσική για άλλους γνωστούς ύμνους όπως «Look, Ye Saints! The Sight Is Glorious», και «The Strife Is O’er».

Για να συνοψίσουμε, ο Henry Lyte βίωσε πολλές λύπες κατά τη διάρκεια της ζωής του. Και οι δύο γονείς του πέθαναν σε νεαρή ηλικία αφήνοντάς τον ορφανό. Και η ίδια η αρρώστια και η αδυναμία του τον έθεταν σε συνεχή κίνδυνο άσθματος και φυματίωσης. Όμως, παρ’ όλες τις δοκιμασίες του, βρίσκουμε σε αυτόν ένα ανθεκτικό πνεύμα που έφτανε προς τους άλλους· να αγγίζει και να διακονεί το Ευαγγέλιο σε εκείνους τους φτωχούς ανθρώπους ανάμεσα στους οποίους ζούσε. «Σε κανένα άλλο συγγραφέα,» λέει ο Δρ. Breed (στο Treasury of Hymn Stories), «η ποίηση και η θρησκεία δεν ενώνονται πιο εξαίσια.»
