La humanidad se define por su búsqueda de la verdad. Algunas personas buscan esta verdad mediante el poder personal, intentando dominar a sus semejantes. Otras la buscan en el placer, viendo la auto-gratificación como el mayor logro en la vida. Otras buscan la iluminación mediante sus propios pensamientos y razonamientos, siempre aprendiendo, y nunca capaces de llegar al conocimiento de la verdad –2 Timoteo 3:7. Otros más creen que una vida de servicio será recompensa en sí misma, y por ello intentan hacerse un nombre a través de la publicidad de sus actos de servicio y caridad.

Una y otra vez, a lo largo de la historia, el pensamiento colectivo del hombre se ha vuelto hacia algo mayor que él mismo. Surgen religiones y caen religiones, se fundan imperios y se desmoronan, se desarrollan filosofías y se deshacen.

Sobre este trasfondo de ondulación intelectual, arraigó un movimiento que la mayoría de mis lectores reconocerá. Zúrich, Suiza, en el año 1525 d. C., fue la ciudad y la fecha dadas como su nacimiento, pero sus raíces se habían establecido ciento cincuenta0 años antes, en Galilea, donde Alguien enseñó y vivió las respuestas finales a todas las preguntas del hombre.

Los inicios de este movimiento más reciente están bien documentados. En breve, fue fundado por un pequeño grupo de estudiantes, clérigos y gente común que buscaba la verdad en su forma más pura. Las historias de Conrad Grebel, Félix Manz y George Blaurock son conocidas por muchos de nosotros. Ellos se esforzaron por separarse de la corrupción espiritual que los rodeaba, al establecer los comienzos de lo que llegaría a conocerse como el movimiento anabaptista.

Estos tres pronto afrontaron el escrutinio de las autoridades civiles y espirituales de su tiempo, soportando penurias y sufrimientos por su fe. Dos de ellos eventualmente dieron sus vidas por la verdad que tanto estimaban. Félix Manz fue el primer anabaptista martirizado. El 5 de enero de 1527, a menos de dos años de su valiente re-bautismo, fue ahogado en el río Limmat que atraviesa Zúrich. Sus últimas palabras fueron: “En tus manos, oh Dios, encomiendo mi espíritu.”

El movimiento anabaptista vivió más allá de estos tres hombres.

Se extendió y creció por Moravia, los Países Bajos, Suiza y la región del Palatinado en Alemania. Casi cien años después hubo otro líder destacado en las colinas de Zúrich; este era un anciano agricultor. Estaba bien curtido en guiar a su rebaño a través del vaivén de los desafíos que enfrentaban los creyentes de aquella época. Su nombre es Hans Landis.

El año era 1613, el 26 de enero para ser exactos. Confluyeron al pequeño castillo de Wadenswil, en la orilla del lago de Zúrich, el anciano Hans Landis junto con catorce miembros de su iglesia. Entre los más notables se encontraba Galli Fuchs, un maestro de escuela y converso reciente, así como Bachman, un herrero y conocido alborotador, que también se había convertido recientemente. Allí para reunirse con ellos había nueve funcionarios de iglesia y del estado, incluido el alcalde de Zúrich, Rudolf Rhan; su jefe de policía, Conrad Grebel (aparentemente homónimo del rebautizador original de casi un siglo antes); y numerosos ministros locales de la iglesia protestante de Zúrich. La razón de esta reunión era que la obra espiritual de Hans había sido bendecida, y su pequeña congregación estaba creciendo rápidamente, provocando repercusiones en la asistencia de las parroquias rurales pertenecientes a la iglesia protestante. La caída de asistencia presentaba varias dificultades a este gobierno combinado de iglesia y estado.

Primero, la Iglesia Protestante recaudaba vastos fondos de sus feligreses. Por tanto, otra iglesia que atraía y convertía a sus miembros se veía no solo como una amenaza espiritual, sino también financiera. Los cantones de la zona a menudo se veían inmersos en hostilidades alimentadas por la religión, que iban desde debates airados hasta campañas militares a gran escala. Segundo, las doctrinas espirituales desviadas que discrepaban con las religiones oficiales del gobierno solían introducirse en tiempos de agitación civil, y las revueltas campesinas de cantones cercanos aún estaban frescas en la memoria de la nobleza y el clero local. Eventos como los de los menonitas de Münster y sus interpretaciones violentas de las Escrituras seguían siendo una clara advertencia sobre el fervor religioso descontrolado. Estas revueltas habían tenido lugar cuando la iglesia católica colapsó en la zona, lo que presentó oportunidades para que nuevas y a veces extremas creencias echaran raíces. Ahora, las actividades de Hans y su iglesia parecían a estos funcionarios un asunto que bordeaba la rebelión y la traición.

Esta reunión no fue el primer encuentro que Hans Landis y su rebaño tuvieron con las autoridades locales. Se había realizado una investigación anterior, casi cuatro años antes. Ese informe daba sus lugares de reunión como los bosques, graneros e incluso la casa de Hans Landis. Sin embargo, no se incluyó una lista de miembros, ya que incluso los vecinos protestantes de la iglesia se negaron a nombrar a ninguno de los anabaptistas. No solo la población local se negó a cooperar en identificar a los miembros de la congregación de Hans, sino que además se rumoraba que los Taufer mantenían un fondo general, a cargo del diácono Jacob Isler, del cual proveían para las necesidades de su comunidad. Para los funcionarios, esto parecía no ser más que otro truco para persuadir a los pobres de la comunidad de abandonar su iglesia y unirse a Hans y su grupo.

El alcalde Rhan abrió la reunión, dirigiéndose a los asistentes como “Reverendos, altos y muy doctos, piadosos, nobles, inteligentes, sabios, (y) queridos señores.” Luego habló a Hans y a los hermanos con él, dándoles un saludo cordial de “Honorables, queridos y buenos amigos” antes de recordarles sus posiciones refiriéndose a ellos como “súbditos”. Tras estas maniobras nada sutiles, les interrogó, pidiendo una explicación sobre “las razones [por las que] os separasteis de nuestra iglesia y … empezasteis una secta separada.” Tras esta pregunta, les aseguró que el consejo deseaba ser tolerante pero que los separatistas “no debían abusar de la paciencia y la bondad de los señores.”

Ante esta introducción, Hans pidió permiso para que él y sus hermanos se pusieran de pie y dirigieran la palabra a sus “Señores Graciosos”. Concedido el permiso, se puso en pie, agradeciendo al alcalde por sus amables palabras de saludo antes de preguntar por su interés en las creencias anabaptistas, afirmando que ya las habían oído con frecuencia. Añadió que toda su doctrina era “nada más que lo que Cristo enseñó y lo que escribieron los apóstoles.” Como antes, los anabaptistas pidieron simplemente que se les permitiera mantener esto, apoyando a su gobierno en asuntos no relacionados con la conciencia. También continuarían orando por el gobierno y sus líderes.

Al alcalde Rhan no le gustó esta respuesta, tomándola como una implicación de que él y la iglesia protestante no obedecían los mandamientos de Cristo. Hans, al oír esa réplica, pidió permiso para sacar a su grupo fuera de la sala por un momento. Al regresar, se presentó a Galli Fuchs, quien dio un testimonio a los señores, describiendo su trayecto espiritual tanto por la iglesia protestante como por la católica, observando que aunque ambos predicaban bien desde el púlpito, ambos también negaban esa enseñanza con su vida impía. Tras estudiar la fe y la práctica anabaptista, Galli se convirtió.

Los funcionarios se mostraron escépticos, argumentando que los puntos de Galli “todavía no mostraban razón para vuestra separación.” Tras esta réplica, se presentó otro converso, un herrero llamado Bachman. Bachman fue inmediatamente reconocido por Conrad Grebel (no el fundador anabaptista), el jefe de policía de Zúrich, como conocido por ser uno de los pendencieros locales—“Es verdad, eras impío [y] no hay nadie en toda la zona con quien yo hubiera tenido más problemas que contigo.”

El testimonio de Bachman resonó con muchos de los puntos de Galli, especialmente sobre la pureza y separatividad de la verdadera iglesia, terminando con esta cita del Sirácida: “El que se revuelve en pez negra se mancha.”

Los debates continuaron, con disputas que ardían en torno a la comunión, los ejemplos de los líderes de la iglesia y el conocimiento de la salvación. Al terminar la reunión, Galli Fuchs no pudo resistir un último comentario: “Si nos dierais la iglesia en Hirzel, … veríais … ¡quién tendría la multitud más grande!” Esto provocó una risa en la sala, y Hans aprovechó una última oportunidad para hablar, suplicando: “Oh, queridos señores, mantengámonos en lo que creemos.”

Tras esta súplica, el alcalde deliberó, decidiendo finalmente que a los hermanos se les permitiría marcharse sin ser arrestados, quienes, al salir, fueron escuchados decir con acuerdo: “También daríamos la vida, el cuerpo, la propiedad y la sangre.” Pronto tendrían la oportunidad de vivir este compromiso.

Pasaron quince meses. Hans fue encarcelado en la torre Wellenberg en Zúrich, junto con Galli Fuchs, el diácono Jacob Isler, Hans Meili, Stephen Zehnder y Paul Degia (natural de Milán, Italia). Allí estuvieron detenidos catorce semanas, y fueron repetidamente halagados, interrogados y amenazados. Finalmente se dictó una orden de que debían abandonar el cantón de Zúrich, pero Hans se negó, a lo que el consejo respondió con una amenaza a menudo considerada peor que la muerte. El consejo sostuvo que debido a la desobediencia civil de estos hombres, no por sus creencias, debían ser sentenciados como galeotes para remar a bordo de los navíos de Francia en el Mediterráneo.

Jacob Isler suplicó a los señores, preguntándoles cómo podían hacer tal cosa, sabiendo que los Taufer (anabaptistas) no podían soportar dejar a sus familias. Stephen Zhender añadió: “No tendríamos miedo de ir por mar y por agua puesto que ellos [también] son creación de Dios.” A pesar de estas súplicas, el consejo cumplió sus amenazas, sentenciando a los seis a las galeras.

La sentencia causó un estremecimiento en la comunidad. La esperanza de vida para un joven y sano galeote no superaba los tres años, y esos tres años estarían llenos de hambre, exposición, palizas y agotamiento. Incluso en los cantones católicos más duros, esta sentencia era severa. En la comunidad protestante más indulgente, provocó indignación pública.

A todos los prisioneros se les dio una última oportunidad para abandonar el cantón, tras lo cual tres de ellos claudicaron. Pero Galli Fuchs, Stephen Zehnder y Hans Landis se negaron firmemente a cambiar de parecer. Fueron conducidos bajo custodia hacia el oeste hasta un embajador francés en Solothurn, una ciudad del cantón de Berna. Berna reaccionó de forma muy parecida a Zúrich, ofreciendo un rescate por la liberación de los prisioneros. Cuando eso fracasó, se deslizó en secreto una lima en su celda en Solothurn. Las cadenas de los prisioneros fueron cortadas rápidamente y escaparon de la ciudad, huyendo a sus hogares. Una vez allí, la población, todavía indignada por su trato, se negó a denunciarlos a las autoridades.

La noticia de la fuga se difundió y creció, y Hans pronto se puso en marcha, bautizando a los nuevos convertidos e incluso oficiando varios matrimonios. Los anabaptistas prosperaron, ayudando a los pobres de la comunidad mediante alimentos y préstamos sin interés desde su fondo de limosnas. Esta actividad renovada enfureció y asustó a las autoridades, que finalmente decidieron que los esfuerzos de su anciano líder debían ser neutralizados.

Hans fue arrestado de inmediato tras esa decisión y nuevamente recluido en el Wellenberg. Allí se intensificaron las amenazas y advertencias de las autoridades. Si no se retractaba o al menos abandonaba el cantón, tendrían que matarlo.

Amenazas como esas no hicieron flaquear a Hans. En cambio, amonestó a los gobernantes para que no cometieran pecado en su trato hacia él, afirmando su resolución de que se había “entregado a Dios” y “estaba dispuesto a esperar lo que Dios quisiera hacerle.”

Esta valiente postura de Hans provocó una realización similar en las autoridades: tendrían que cumplir sus amenazas. Considerándolo un rebelde, sostuvieron que él “quería ser su propio señor y amo sin considerar a las honorables autoridades,” y que mostraba la “resistencia obstinada y sediciosa de gente malvada.” A pesar de estas alegaciones junto con sus amenazas, los magistrados se dieron cuenta de que una ejecución sería una empresa impopular. Hans era muy respetado por la población local e incluso tenía conexiones en Ámsterdam, donde vivía su hija, casada con un menonita holandés.

El oficial Grebel, el clero protestante y varios otros pasaron mucho tiempo discutiendo con Hans en su celda, pero sin resultado. Para el jueves 29 de septiembre de 1614, se dieron cuenta de que él era completamente inmovible en su fe, rehusando retractarse o abandonar el cantón. Este informe, presentado a los señores, los sumió en profunda deliberación. Algunos abogaron por cortar públicamente la oreja de Hans y exiliarlo, mientras que otros consideraron el encarcelamiento de por vida una sentencia más apropiada. La cuestión se sometió a votación al mediodía, y rápidamente se alcanzó una decisión por mayoría. Hans Landis sería decapitado públicamente de inmediato.

Hans, al oír la decisión, pensó que no era más que otra artimaña para persuadirlo de retractarse. Sin embargo, al acercarse al conocido lugar público de ejecuciones en Zúrich, su rostro palideció y sus manos se llevaron a la cabeza. No obstante, se recompondría con prontitud, sonriendo y amonestando a la multitud para que no llorara, pues confiaba en su buena esperanza. Al notar a su esposa y a sus hijos presentes, les pidió que se marcharan para que su resolución no se debilitará.

Se leyó la sentencia; Hans permaneció en silencio. No se había alzado palabra alguna criticando su moral personal. En cambio, la cuestión era su negativa a disolver su iglesia. Permaneció firme, y así el verdugo, Paul Vollmar, condujo a Hans al lugar de la ejecución. Algunos observadores afirmaron que Vollmar soltó a Hans, aparentemente dándole una vía de escape. Cuando Hans no lo hizo, Vollmar alzó las manos hacia Dios, pidiendo perdón por lo que la ley le requería ejecutar. Hans, sonriendo, perdonó al hombre, mientras varios ministros de la iglesia lo amonestaban a retractarse, pero Hans respondió que no había visto arrepentimiento en ellos.

Vollmar, al haber llegado al sitio de la ejecución, dio a Hans la oportunidad de hablar sin impedimentos, y Hans habló brevemente: “No sé qué más debería decir salvo que desearía que todos llegaran al conocimiento de sus pecados y se arrepintieran, para que pudieran ser salvos; esto lo desearía para todos.”

Luego, a la vista del lugar donde Félix Manz dio su vida casi un siglo antes, se arrodilló e inclinó la cabeza. La espada brilló hacia abajo, entonces Paul Vollmar hizo la pregunta ritual: “¿He ejecutado a este hombre correctamente?”

“Sí,” vino la respuesta, “has ejecutado a este pobre hombre.”

El impacto inmediato del sacrificio del anciano Hans fue una oleada de apoyo e indignación en la comunidad no anabaptista. Rhudlof Rhan y Conrad Grebel continuaron presionando a los anabaptistas restantes, confinando a Margaretha Landis, la viuda de Hans, en aislamiento en el hospital de la ciudad tras su negativa a cumplir sus demandas. Los hijos de Hans también se mantendrían firmes, negándose a retractarse, pero varios de sus nietos comenzaron a asistir a la iglesia de la ciudad poco después de la ejecución de su abuelo.

La congregación anabaptista local también permaneció fuerte. Sus descendientes espirituales llevarían la palabra de Cristo consigo cuando, un siglo más tarde, una gran emigración los llevó a las salvajes costas del Nuevo Mundo. Aquí, en la libertad religiosa de Pensilvania, establecerían nuevas comunidades donde la fe que le costó la vida a Hans Landis florecería a través de las generaciones futuras. Hoy, hay creyentes en toda América que se esfuerzan por vivir su fe conforme a su conciencia, que están donde están como resultado de la vida vivida por Hans hace unos 400 años. Algunos son sus descendientes y otros son amigos de sus descendientes. Que seamos inspirados a andar como anduvo Jesús, tal como Hans.

As a child, you might think you can’t make a difference in the lives of people around you, but that is not true! Your little acts of kindness will not soon be forgotten. Being a true friend to someone who is hurting can change that person’s life forever.

This is the true story of “Hadassah” (not her real name) a young girl who was very much looking forward to starting school. Once she started first grade, what a disappointment it was to find that the second-grade girls were ready for someone to be mean to, or so it seemed. Maybe it would have been better if Hadassah had stood up to them, but she didn’t. Instead, she chose to act as if it didn’t hurt and tried to ignore them. Some days were better than others, but sadly this went on for three or four years.

Sure, there were good times too, but many evenings she walked home from school, crying most of the way and wishing that she wouldn’t need to go back to school the next day!

One day, one of the girls lost her pen. She was sure that Hadassah had stolen it. This was very disturbing to a very conscientious Hadassah. At the next recess she was blamed for cheating on her flash cards. Many other made-up stories were also passed around among the girls.

However, there was one little girl in that second-grade group of girls whose name we’ll say was “Esther”. She was Hadassah’s best friend and supported her all through those difficult years.

Esther was a very gentle, sweet girl, which is mostly what Hadassah remembered her for. Esther had cystic fibrosis and in the 1970s they didn’t have as many treatment options available for that disease as they do now, so those patients usually died very young. As Esther’s sickness became worse, the days that she felt well enough to be in school were rare. Since Esther was well-liked, the days when she was in school were special to everyone. Perhaps Esther realized she would be in heaven before the other girls—we don’t know for sure. But she taught the girls a song, “How Far Is Heaven”, which Hadassah still likes to sing today!

Hadassah still remembers seeing the emergency squad go past her house when they took Esther to the hospital for the last time. It was a very sad group of schoolgirls when Esther died at the age of 13. Esther had touched the hearts of many people in her short life, including the nurses who had cared for her during her stay in the hospital. Hadassah still remembers seeing some of the nurses crying at Esther’s funeral. Do you think Hadassah will ever forget Esther? Never!

Besides being her best friend, another bright spot for Hadassah was that when Esther was in school the other girls weren’t as mean to her (Hadassah). It so happened that in about the fourth grade, Esther was in school more often. One day she went home and told her parents what she was witnessing in school—how the other girls were against Hadassah and were being so mean to her. Esther’s father brought this problem up in the next parent/teacher meeting. What a night and day change started the very next day! One of the girls even came to Hadassah and apologized. Finally, they could all be friends and today those girls are Hadassah’s “old school friends”.

It’s worth it to stand beside someone who is being treated unkindly. Your support may be what God uses to help your friend to go through their hard times in a good way! And share it with your parents, they can help find a way to change the problem.

Quando criança, você pode pensar que não consegue fazer diferença na vida das pessoas ao seu redor, mas isso não é verdade! Seus pequenos atos de bondade não serão esquecidos tão cedo. Ser um verdadeiro amigo de alguém que está sofrendo pode transformar a vida dessa pessoa para sempre.

Esta é a história verdadeira de “Hadassah” (não é o nome real dela), uma menina que estava muito animada para começar a escola. Quando ela começou a primeira série, que decepção foi descobrir que as meninas da segunda série estavam prontas para maltratar alguém, ou pelo menos parecia assim. Talvez teria sido melhor se Hadassah tivesse enfrentado-as, mas ela não o fez. Em vez disso, escolheu agir como se não doesse e tentou ignorá-las. Alguns dias foram melhores que outros, mas infelizmente isso continuou por três ou quatro anos.

Claro, também houve bons momentos, mas muitas noites ela voltava para casa da escola chorando na maior parte do caminho e desejando não ter que voltar para a escola no dia seguinte!

Um dia, uma das meninas perdeu sua caneta. Ela tinha certeza de que Hadassah a havia roubado. Isso foi muito perturbador para a conscienciosa Hadassah. No recreio seguinte ela foi acusada de colar nos flash cards. Muitas outras histórias inventadas também foram espalhadas entre as meninas.

No entanto, havia uma menininha naquele grupo de segunda série cujo nome diremos ser “Esther”. Ela era a melhor amiga de Hadassah e a apoiou durante todos aqueles anos difíceis.

Esther era uma menina muito meiga e doce, que é principalmente como Hadassah se lembrava dela. Esther tinha fibrose cística e, na década de 1970, não havia tantas opções de tratamento para essa doença como há hoje, de modo que esses pacientes geralmente morriam muito jovens. Conforme a doença de Esther piorava, os dias em que ela se sentia bem o bastante para ir à escola tornavam-se raros. Como Esther era querida, os dias em que ela estava na escola eram especiais para todos. Talvez Esther percebera que estaria no céu antes das outras meninas—não sabemos ao certo. Mas ela ensinou às meninas uma canção, “How Far Is Heaven”, que Hadassah ainda gosta de cantar hoje!

Hadassah ainda lembra de ver a equipe de emergência passar em frente à sua casa quando levaram Esther ao hospital pela última vez. Foi um grupo de colegiais muito triste quando Esther morreu aos 13 anos. Esther tocou o coração de muitas pessoas em sua curta vida, incluindo as enfermeiras que a cuidaram durante sua internação. Hadassah ainda se lembra de ver algumas das enfermeiras chorando no funeral de Esther. Você acha que Hadassah algum dia esquecerá Esther? Nunca!

Além de ser sua melhor amiga, outro ponto luminoso para Hadassah era que quando Esther estava na escola as outras meninas não eram tão más com ela (Hadassah). Aconteceu que, por volta da quarta série, Esther estava mais frequentemente na escola. Um dia ela foi para casa e contou aos pais o que testemunhara na escola—como as outras meninas se voltavam contra Hadassah e eram tão cruéis com ela. O pai de Esther levou esse problema à próxima reunião de pais e professores. Que mudança de dia para noite começou já no dia seguinte! Uma das meninas até foi até Hadassah e pediu desculpas. Finalmente, todas puderam ser amigas e hoje essas meninas são as “velhas colegas de escola” de Hadassah.

Vale a pena ficar ao lado de alguém que está sendo tratado com crueldade. Seu apoio pode ser o que Deus usa para ajudar sua amiga a passar pelos tempos difíceis de uma boa maneira! E conte isso aos seus pais; eles podem ajudar a encontrar uma forma de mudar o problema.

This hymn is generally considered to be one of the greatest hymns ever written and is found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. It was written by a man who was frail in body, but strong in spirit. It was he who coined the phrase, “It is better to wear out than to rust out.” Let us now take a glimpse into the life of this servant of God.

Henry Francis Lyte, the author of this great and noteworthy hymn, was born June 1, 1793, in Ednam, near Kelso, Scotland. At a young age, he was left an orphan and was in comparative poverty. He was educated at Trinity College in Dublin, Ireland. It was there that his gift of poetry began to appear, winning him three prizes. His primary goal with his studies was to become a physician, instead, by the providence of God, he became a minister of the gospel of Jesus Christ.

One day in Cornwall, a fellow clergyman who was on his deathbed, requested that Lyte would come and give him some spiritual comfort. “To their mutual grief, they found themselves [both] groping for the light, veritable blind guides”. As they searched for truth and assurance of salvation, they fixed their faith on Christ, and Lyte came away from that sickroom a changed man, never to be the same again. It is said that it was his encounter with God at the bedside of that dying man that prompted Lyte’s noble hymn, “Jesus, I My Cross Have Taken.” In the year 1823, Henry F. Lyte took charge of a seashore parish, Lower Brixham, in Devonshire, England. It was at that place where he spent the last 23 years of his life toiling as a pastor for the spiritual good of the poor fishing people and the rough seafaring men of that region until his death in the fall of 1847. For all of Henry’s dedication and labor, he received a reward: having a Sunday school of several hundred scholars, as well as “a splendid company of seventy or eighty teachers, personally trained by him.”

Throughout his lifetime, his health was continually threatened by asthma and tuberculosis. Notwithstanding his physical frailties, he worked tirelessly with an established reputation as a poet, musician, and minister. Wherever he went, he was greatly loved and admired by his people. Toward the end of these later years, his health became gradually worse. So it was that during the winter months, he felt compelled to seek a warmer climate in Italy, which is a part of southern Europe.

Though he was greatly weakened by his sickness, on September 4, 1847, as Lyte was about to leave to head southward, he was arrested by an “irresistible desire” to preach once more to his congregation. He dearly loved these people and he had labored among them for so many years. “Against the protest of his amazed friends, he accomplished this purpose, and it is recorded that Lyte nearly had to crawl to the pulpit and his message came as from a dying man.” “O brethren,” he said, as he entered the familiar pulpit for the last time, “I stand here among you today, as alive from the dead, if I may hope to impress it upon you, and induce you to prepare for that solemn hour which must come to all, by a timely appreciation and dependance on the death of Christ.” These final words made a deep impact upon his congregation, after which he closed the service by administering the Lord’s Supper to his weeping people. Later that evening, after the service, he was inspired to “poetical composition” and wrote the eight stanzas of his last and greatest hymn:

Abide with me: fast falls the eventide;
The darkness deepens; Lord, with me abide:
when other helpers fail, and comforts flee,
Help of the helpless, O abide with me.

Swift to its close ebbs out life’s little day;
Earth’s joys grow dim, its glories pass away;
Change and decay in all around I see;
O Thou who changest not, abide with me.

Not a brief glance I beg, a passing word;
But, as Thou dwell’st with Thy disciples, Lord,
Familiar, condescending, patient, free,
Come, not to sojourn, but abide, with me.

Come not in terrors, as the King of kings;
But kind and good, with healing in Thy wings;
Tears for all woes, a heart for every plea;
Come, Friend of sinners, and thus ‘bide with me.

Thou on my head in early youth didst smile;
And, though rebellious and perverse meanwhile,
thou hast not left me, oft as I left thee:
On to the close, O Lord, abide with me.

I need Thy presence every passing hour;
What but Thy grace can foil the tempter’s power?
Who like Thyself my guide and stay can be?
Through cloud and sunshine, O abide with me.

I fear no foe, with Thee at hand to bless:
Ills have no weight, and tears no bitterness.
Where is death’s sting? Where, grave, thy victory?
I triumph still, if Thou abide with me.

Hold Thou Thy cross before my closing eyes;
Shine through the gloom, and point me to the skies;
Heaven’s morning breaks, and earth’s vain shadows flee:
In life, in death, O Lord, abide with me.

This hymn he gave to one of the family members that very night. Leaving the following day, he began his trek to Rome, Italy, hoping to gain some relief from his sickness. Lyte make it as far as Nice, France where his sickness prevented his further travel. He passed away soon after the age of 55, on November 20, 1847. His last words were “Joy! Peace!”

The scene behind this hymn is that of the resurrected Christ Jesus walking on the road to Emmaus with two of His somewhat sad and discouraged disciples. As they neared the end of their seven-mile walk and approached the village where they were going, Jesus …made as though he would have gone further. But they constrained him, saying, Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them –Luke 24:28-29.

We can draw a parallel between that scene and Henry F. Lyte’s own experience of drawing toward the close of his earthly journey. Thus, as the disciples besought the risen Lord to abide with them in the close of that ancient day, so was the meaning of this song written in the “shadows of death” to the hymn writer.

Lyte himself composed a tune for this hymn on the same evening that he wrote it, but it never became widely used. However, the tune universally used was written fourteen years later by William Henry Monk, a noted London musician, and editor of the well-known Anglican hymnal, Hymns Ancient and Modern. He included this song in his first edition, which was published in 1861.

In all, William H. Monk composed 50 tunes for the hymnal. It is said that Monk, being “inspired by the beauty of a glorious sunset while yet experiencing a deep personal sorrow,” composed (in only 10 minutes) the tune, Eventide, for the song, “Abide With Me, Fast Falls The Eventide”. William Monk also wrote the music for other familiar hymns such as “Look, Ye Saints! The Sight Is Glorious”, and “The Strife Is O’er”.

To summarize, Henry Lyte experienced many sorrows during his lifetime. Both of his parents died at an early age leaving him an orphan. And his own sickness and frailty caused him to be in ongoing danger of asthma and tuberculosis. Yet, in spite of all his trials, we find in him a resilient spirit to reach out to others; to touch and minister the Gospel to those poor people among whom he lived. “In no other writer,” says Dr. Breed (in the Treasury of Hymn Stories), “are poetry and religion more exquisitely united.”

Himne ini umumnya dianggap sebagai salah satu himne terbesar yang pernah ditulis dan ditemukan di hampir setiap himne atau buku himne yang diterbitkan saat ini. Itu ditulis oleh seorang pria yang lemah badan, tetapi kuat dalam semangat. Dialah yang mencetuskan ungkapan, “Lebih baik aus daripada berkarat.” Marilah kita sekarang mengintip kehidupan hamba Tuhan ini.

Henry Francis Lyte, pengarang himne agung dan terkenal ini, lahir 1 Juni 1793, di Ednam, dekat Kelso, Skotlandia. Pada usia muda, ia menjadi yatim piatu dan hidup dalam kemiskinan relatif. Ia berpendidikan di Trinity College di Dublin, Irlandia. Di sanalah bakat puisinya mulai tampak, memenangkan tiga hadiah. Tujuan utamanya dengan studinya adalah menjadi seorang dokter, namun, oleh penyelenggaraan Tuhan, ia menjadi seorang pelayan Injil Yesus Kristus.

Pada suatu hari di Cornwall, seorang rekan imam yang sedang sekarat meminta Lyte datang dan memberinya penghiburan rohani. “Untuk kesedihan bersama mereka, mereka mendapati diri mereka [keduanya] meraba-raba menuju terang, benar-benar pemimpin yang buta”. Saat mereka mencari kebenaran dan kepastian keselamatan, mereka menempatkan iman mereka pada Kristus, dan Lyte keluar dari kamar sakit itu sebagai orang yang berubah, tak lagi sama. Dikatakan bahwa pertemuannya dengan Tuhan di sisi ranjang orang yang sekarat itu mendorong lahirnya himne mulia Lyte, “Jesus, I My Cross Have Taken.” Pada tahun 1823, Henry F. Lyte memimpin sebuah paroki pesisir, Lower Brixham, di Devonshire, Inggris. Di tempat itulah ia menghabiskan 23 tahun terakhir hidupnya bekerja sebagai gembala demi kebaikan rohani orang-orang nelayan miskin dan para pelaut kasar di daerah itu sampai kematiannya pada musim gugur 1847. Untuk semua pengabdian dan jerih payah Henry, ia menerima ganjaran: memiliki sekolah Minggu berisi beberapa ratus murid, serta “sebuah kumpulan yang mulia dari tujuh puluh atau delapan puluh guru, yang dilatih olehnya secara pribadi.”

Sepanjang hidupnya, kesehatannya terus-menerus terancam oleh asma dan tuberkulosis. Terlepas dari kelemahan fisiknya, ia bekerja tanpa lelah dengan reputasi mapan sebagai penyair, musisi, dan pelayan. Ke mana pun ia pergi, ia sangat dicintai dan dikagumi oleh umatnya. Menjelang akhir tahun-tahun itu, kesehatannya perlahan menjadi lebih buruk. Maka saat musim dingin, ia merasa terdorong untuk mencari iklim yang lebih hangat di Italia, yang merupakan bagian dari Eropa selatan.

Walaupun sangat melemah oleh penyakitnya, pada 4 September 1847, ketika Lyte akan berangkat ke selatan, ia dihentikan oleh “keinginan yang tak tertahankan” untuk berkhotbah sekali lagi kepada jemaatnya. Ia sangat mengasihi orang-orang ini dan ia telah melayani di antara mereka selama begitu banyak tahun. “Bertentangan dengan protes teman-temannya yang tercengang, ia melaksanakan tujuan ini, dan tercatat bahwa Lyte nyaris merangkak ke mimbar dan pesannya keluar seperti dari orang yang sekarat.” “Hai saudara-saudara,” katanya, saat ia memasuki mimbar yang telah dikenalnya untuk terakhir kali, “aku berdiri di sini di antara kamu hari ini, seperti hidup dari antara orang mati, jika aku boleh berharap untuk menekankannya padamu, dan mendorong kamu untuk mempersiapkan diri untuk saat yang khidmat itu yang harus datang kepada semua, dengan menghargai dan bergantung tepat waktu pada kematian Kristus.” Kata-kata terakhir ini memberikan dampak mendalam kepada jemaatnya, setelah itu ia menutup kebaktian dengan membagikan Perjamuan Tuhan kepada umatnya yang menangis. Kemudian malam itu, setelah kebaktian, ia terinspirasi untuk “komposisi puitis” dan menulis delapan bait himne terakhir dan agungnya:

Abide with me: fast falls the eventide;
The darkness deepens; Lord, with me abide:
when other helpers fail, and comforts flee,
Help of the helpless, O abide with me.

Swift to its close ebbs out life’s little day;
Earth’s joys grow dim, its glories pass away;
Change and decay in all around I see;
O Thou who changest not, abide with me.

Not a brief glance I beg, a passing word;
But, as Thou dwell’st with Thy disciples, Lord,
Familiar, condescending, patient, free,
Come, not to sojourn, but abide, with me.

Come not in terrors, as the King of kings;
But kind and good, with healing in Thy wings;
Tears for all woes, a heart for every plea;
Come, Friend of sinners, and thus ‘bide with me.

Thou on my head in early youth didst smile;
And, though rebellious and perverse meanwhile,
thou hast not left me, oft as I left thee:
On to the close, O Lord, abide with me.

I need Thy presence every passing hour;
What but Thy grace can foil the tempter’s power?
Who like Thyself my guide and stay can be?
Through cloud and sunshine, O abide with me.

I fear no foe, with Thee at hand to bless:
Ills have no weight, and tears no bitterness.
Where is death’s sting? Where, grave, thy victory?
I triumph still, if Thou abide with me.

Hold Thou Thy cross before my closing eyes;
Shine through the gloom, and point me to the skies;
Heaven’s morning breaks, and earth’s vain shadows flee:
In life, in death, O Lord, abide with me.

Himne ini ia berikan kepada salah satu anggota keluarga malam itu juga. Berangkat keesokan harinya, ia memulai perjalanan menuju Roma, Italia, dengan harapan mendapatkan sedikit kelegaan dari penyakitnya. Lyte sempat sampai di Nice, Prancis di mana penyakitnya menghentikan perjalanannya lebih lanjut. Ia meninggal tak lama setelah usia 55 tahun, pada 20 November 1847. Kata-kata terakhirnya adalah “Joy! Peace!”

Latar di balik himne ini adalah Kristus yang bangkit berjalan di jalan menuju Emaus bersama dua murid-Nya yang agak sedih dan kecewa. Ketika mereka mendekati akhir jalan tujuh mil mereka dan mendekati desa tujuan mereka, Yesus …seolah-olah Ia hendak berjalan lebih jauh. Tetapi mereka menahannya, katanya: Tinggallah bersama kami, sebab hari sudah hampir malam dan hari hampir habis. Lalu Ia masuk untuk tinggal bersama mereka – Lukas 24:28-29.

Kita dapat menarik paralel antara adegan itu dan pengalaman Henry F. Lyte yang semakin mendekati akhir perjalanan duniawinya. Dengan demikian, sebagaimana para murid memohon kepada Tuhan yang bangkit agar tinggal bersama mereka pada akhir hari kuno itu, demikian pula makna lagu ini ditulis dalam “bayang-bayang maut” bagi sang penulis himne.

Lyte sendiri mengarang sebuah melodi untuk himne ini pada malam yang sama ketika ia menulisnya, tetapi melodi itu tidak pernah luas dipakai. Namun, melodi yang dipakai secara universal ditulis empat belas tahun kemudian oleh William Henry Monk, seorang musisi terkenal London, dan penyunting himne Anglikan yang terkenal, Hymns Ancient and Modern. Ia memasukkan lagu ini dalam edisi pertamanya, yang diterbitkan pada 1861.

Secara keseluruhan, William H. Monk mengarang 50 melodi untuk himne tersebut. Dikatakan bahwa Monk, yang “terinspirasi oleh keindahan matahari terbenam yang agung sementara ia sedang mengalami kesedihan pribadi yang mendalam,” mengarang (dalam hanya 10 menit) melodi Eventide untuk lagu “Abide With Me, Fast Falls The Eventide”. William Monk juga menulis musik untuk himne-himne yang lebih akrab seperti “Look, Ye Saints! The Sight Is Glorious”, dan “The Strife Is O’er”.

Untuk meringkas, Henry Lyte mengalami banyak kesedihan selama hidupnya. Kedua orang tuanya meninggal pada usia dini sehingga membuatnya menjadi yatim piatu. Dan penyakit serta kelemahannya membuatnya terus-menerus dalam bahaya asma dan tuberkulosis. Namun, terlepas dari segala ujiannya, kita menemukan dalam dirinya semangat tangguh untuk meraih orang lain; untuk menyentuh dan melayani Injil kepada orang-orang miskin tempat ia tinggal. “Dalam tidak ada penulis lain,” kata Dr. Breed (dalam Treasury of Hymn Stories), “puisi dan agama lebih indah bersatu.”

Greetings to one and all in our dear Saviour’s name, Jesus Christ. Another year has passed from the present into the annals of history. Nothing that we have said or done can be recalled and re-lived. Another year is before us. Many are waiting with bated breath, anticipating what this new year will bring forth.

I read somewhere in the news that those on the frontier of technology believe that this year will be a big year for artificial intelligence. One example given was: they are anticipating that this technology will be able to be a part of events such as board meetings with the ability to hear and understand all that is shared by each one present. Then at the end of the meeting, with the push of a button, the artificial intelligence will produce detailed minutes of that meeting with a fair degree of accuracy. Over the last number of years, many of the things that used to be considered science fiction have recently become reality, so, likely, this will become a new reality as well.

What is this world coming to? To the Bible-literate Christian, the end of time certainly seems to be fast approaching. According to the United Nations, the world’s population surpassed 8 billion on November 15, 2022. Many in the world are desperately trying to figure out how to sustain that many people for the long term. Just like the Bible has prophesied, there is an uptick in the number of famines, drought, floods, earthquakes, wars, and rumors of wars, etc. One thing that I find interesting is that even though the world does not want to retain God in their knowledge, insurance companies still refer to certain specific events as “acts of God”.

As Bible-believing Christians how shall we then live? And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet –Matthew 24:6. Let us remember that we should not be troubled. Rather, we should remember that …he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:13. If we, like Peter, take our eyes off of our Lord and start focusing on the stormy conditions around us we will start to sink as well. Remember, it is …the fearful, and unbelieving … [who] shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone… –Revelation 21:8. But, He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son –Revelation 21:7.

In this issue of the magazine, we again have an interesting group of articles for your consideration. Join us as we learn of a somewhat obscure, yet influential leader of the early Anabaptist movement in Switzerland. Let’s honestly evaluate our own hearts as we follow the expository teaching from Habakkuk regarding what it means to have a real faith that is first personal, then corporate. Together we can consider what it really means to enter into the rest of God that is detailed in Hebrews chapter four. The youth can take a look into their emotions as they consider those times when they feel like giving up. The author for our sisters’ article has tackled a very difficult subject—when and how to be submissive as a godly wife. We have another thought-provoking article in the discipleship series. And the doctor has chosen to venture into some uncharted territory with the first of a two-part series on cancer.

A final thought I wish to share, a story in fact… Recently, I heard a first-hand account of a man who was lost before God, how he came to spiritual awakening, and how this started affecting his life. This story caused me to stop and consider where I am as a Christian. Is my relationship with my Lord vibrant? How strong is my commitment towards God and His Word? Is my love for my Lord and Saviour still as real and as strong as it was when I first had my awakening and was converted? I’m sure there are more questions that we could ask ourselves in light of this real-life story. I’ll let you as a reader start compiling your own list. Now for the story…

This man is living somewhere within the United States of America. He is a married man with a young family. He is part of a certain religious group within the plain people—those of Anabaptist heritage. Throughout his lifetime he had endeavored to live his life according to the mandates set forth by the leaders of his local church. Yet, for some reason, he had not been finding answers to his personal need, whatever that was—perhaps even he didn’t know.

This man and some of his family were traveling and ended up lodging overnight in a motel. There, in the nightstand drawer he discovered a book titled “The Holy Bible”. Sure, in his church the Bible was read or quoted each week during their normal worship services. Although this man understood English quite well, his church had a policy that they did not want to be too worldly or too modern by reading from an English Bible so they continued their efforts of teaching God’s Word using the original language of their people.

The problem was that this man, somehow, never developed an understanding of that language, thus he never heard the truth of God’s Word. All that he heard was what 1 Corinthians chapter 14 refers to as tongues (languages) and since he didn’t understand the language and since there was no interpretation given, he was not able to be edified. The purpose of this story is not to find fault or to place blame, but rather to bring light to an obvious problem among some of the plain people. A problem for which God would surely desire to see changes made for the betterment of those seeking Him in such settings.

With this in mind, we now come back to this man—a man zealous in his religious life—yet having NEVER heard the message of the Gospel of Jesus Christ. As he hesitantly picked up this English Bible he cautiously started to read the message contained within those book covers. As he read, he became more and more excited. Here were things that he had never heard before—teachings that brought sense to his many questions and the emptiness that he felt within his soul. He was so engrossed that he almost couldn’t pull himself away to allow time for sleep. After a short night, they went on with their travels.

Completing their business they returned home, but life would never be the same for that man. Something had been awakened deep within his soul. Questions had been answered. Longings had been met. Peace had begun to settle over his troubled heart. At long last, he had found the answer, but his time of reading had been so short. Surely there was more to learn, much more. So, before too much time had elapsed, he once more scheduled a trip to get away from his local area and to once more provide a reason to spend another night in a motel with a Bible in the nightstand drawer. He eagerly anticipated another night alone with God and His Word. After a second sleepless night spent devouring the teachings of the Scriptures, he started seeking others who understood and practiced what the Bible said. He was desiring to fellowship and learn all that he could from those who understood God’s Word and who practiced what they preached.

As this man has endeavored to find his way through this confusing maze of religious idiosyncrasies he finally purchased a German/English Bible. He felt driven in his continued pursuit of the Truth, yet he was afraid to be found out by his local church leaders. He wanted to stay within his local church, yet his conscience demanded that he must continue his search. For some reason he believed that his local church leaders would not be understanding in his quest for truth and that maybe he would be placed under church discipline for his actions.

His local church is a part of the descendants of the Anabaptists who were persecuted for their faith, including their desire to understand, and read the Scriptures in their native tongue—Swiss or German, instead of Latin as was required by the church leaders of their day. Yet here he is, some 500 years later, in America, possibly facing persecution from his own church which claims to be a part of the “right” church of God. Herein, his church leaders are finding themselves on the opposite side of the issue of freedom of religious worship that their forefathers suffered for, since they are insisting that the only way to learn of God’s will is through the official language of Scripture—German. This is NO different than the struggle of the original Anabaptists who were persecuted for not studying the Scriptures in the official language of their day—Latin.

Let’s remember, IF church members do not understand the teachings of God’s Word due to their church leaders’ stubborn insistence that the church members are NOT allowed to read or hear the Scriptures in the language that they understand, then the ignorance of the common man WILL be laid at the feet of those leaders come judgment day. Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account… –Hebrews 13:17. Obey here is only in the context of God’s Word, not just according to church leaders’ personal ideas or whims. For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad –2 Corinthians 5:10. Every person will receive personal judgment based on what the Bible teaches NOT according to a church’s detailed dogma.

When I think of the zealous efforts of this man I think of the verse of Scripture… When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel –Matthew 8:10. I also observe the current trends of some of our plain publishing houses—they have borrowed from the world’s idea (in a spiritual way, of course) that to sell books and reading material they need to print exhilarating stories, ones that keep people on the edge of their seats—all this because today’s Christian has become bored with that which seems old-fashioned.

What a difference between this story and many of today’s Anabaptist descendants. Many of today’s conservative Anabaptist people have a difficult time getting excited about the Bible. They are too over-stimulated by the lack of rest and quiet in their normal daily lives.

Usually, we hear of stories like this from the jungles of Central America, the deserts of Africa, or the slums of India. What I am amazed about is that this story takes place right in the midst of one of our plain groups of conservative Anabaptists. Let’s seek God for opportunities to share the truth of the Gospel message with those within the sphere of our influence. We might be surprised how many people we rub shoulders with during our daily lives who would be just as hungry for the Truth as the man in our story.

Groeten aan eenieder in de naam van onze dierbare Zaligmaker, Jezus Christus. Weer een jaar is van het heden in de annalen van de geschiedenis overgegaan. Niets van wat we gezegd of gedaan hebben kan worden teruggehaald en opnieuw geleefd. Er ligt weer een jaar voor ons. Velen wachten met ingehouden adem en zijn benieuwd wat dit nieuwe jaar zal voortbrengen.

Ik las ergens in het nieuws dat degenen aan het front van de technologie geloven dat dit jaar een groot jaar zal worden voor kunstmatige intelligentie. Een gegeven voorbeeld was: men verwacht dat deze technologie deel kan uitmaken van gebeurtenissen zoals bestuursvergaderingen, met het vermogen alles te horen en te begrijpen wat door ieder aanwezig wordt gedeeld. Aan het eind van de vergadering zal, met het indrukken van een knop, de kunstmatige intelligentie gedetailleerde notulen van die vergadering produceren met een behoorlijke mate van nauwkeurigheid. In de afgelopen jaren zijn veel dingen die vroeger als sciencefiction werden beschouwd onlangs realiteit geworden, dus waarschijnlijk zal ook dit een nieuwe realiteit worden.

Waar gaat deze wereld naar toe? Voor de Bijbel-begrijpende christen lijkt het einde der tijden zeker nabij te komen. Volgens de Verenigde Naties overschreed de wereldbevolking op 15 november 2022 de 8 miljard. Velen in de wereld proberen wanhopig uit te vinden hoe zovele mensen op lange termijn in leven gehouden kunnen worden. Zoals de Bijbel heeft geprofeteerd is er een toename van hongersnoden, droogtes, overstromingen, aardbevingen, oorlogen en geruchten van oorlogen, enzovoort. Eén ding dat ik opmerkelijk vind is dat hoewel de wereld God niet in hun kennis wil houden, verzekeringsmaatschappijen toch bepaalde specifieke gebeurtenissen nog steeds aanduiden als “gevallen van God” (acts of God).

Als bijbelgelovende christenen, hoe zouden we dan leven? En u zult horen van oorlogen en geruchten van oorlogen; zie toe, wordt niet verontrust; want dat alles moet gebeuren, maar het einde is nog niet –Mattheüs 24:6. Laten we ons herinneren dat we niet verontrust moeten worden. Integendeel, laten we onthouden dat …wie volhardt tot het eind, die zal behouden worden –Mattheüs 24:13. Als wij, zoals Petrus, onze ogen van onze Heere afwenden en ons op de stormachtige omstandigheden om ons heen gaan richten, zullen ook wij beginnen te zinken. Gedenk, het is …de vrezenden, en de ongelovigen … [die] hun deel zullen hebben in de poel die brandt met vuur en zwavel… –Openbaring 21:8. Maar, Wie overwint zal dit alles erven; en Ik zal zijn God zijn, en hij zal mijn zoon zijn –Openbaring 21:7.

In dit nummer van het tijdschrift hebben we opnieuw een interessante verzameling artikelen voor uw overweging. Ga met ons mee terwijl we leren over een enigszins obscure, maar invloedrijke leider van de vroege wederdopersbeweging in Zwitserland. Laten we eerlijk ons eigen hart evalueren terwijl we de expositieleer uit Habakuk volgen over wat het betekent om een echt geloof te hebben dat eerst persoonlijk is en daarna collectief. Samen kunnen we overwegen wat het werkelijk betekent om in de rust van God binnen te gaan die wordt beschreven in Hebreeën hoofdstuk vier. De jeugd kan een blik werpen op hun emoties wanneer ze aan die tijden denken dat ze het op willen geven. De schrijfster van ons zusterartikel heeft een zeer moeilijk onderwerp aangepakt — wanneer en hoe onderdanig te zijn als een godvruchtige vrouw. We hebben weer een prikkelend artikel in de discipelschapserie. En de dokter heeft gekozen om onontgonnen terrein te betreden met het eerste deel van een tweedelige serie over kanker.

Een laatste gedachte die ik wil delen, een verhaal in feite… Onlangs hoorde ik uit de eerste hand over een man die verloren was voor God, hoe hij tot geestelijke ontwaking kwam, en hoe dit zijn leven begon te beïnvloeden. Dit verhaal deed me stilstaan en overwegen waar ik als christen sta. Is mijn relatie met mijn Heere levendig? Hoe sterk is mijn toewijding aan God en Zijn Woord? Is mijn liefde voor mijn Heere en Zaligmaker nog steeds even echt en sterk als toen ik voor het eerst mijn ontwaking had en bekeerd werd? Ik ben er zeker van dat er meer vragen zijn die we onszelf zouden kunnen stellen naar aanleiding van dit waargebeurde verhaal. Ik laat u als lezer uw eigen lijst samenstellen. Nu het verhaal…

Deze man woont ergens in de Verenigde Staten van Amerika. Hij is een getrouwde man met een jong gezin. Hij behoort tot een bepaalde religieuze groep binnen de plattelandsmensen — die van wederdoper-afkomst. Gedurende zijn leven had hij getracht zijn leven te leiden in overeenstemming met de voorschriften die door de leiders van zijn lokale kerk waren gesteld. Toch had hij om de een of andere reden geen antwoorden gevonden op zijn persoonlijke behoefte, wat die ook was — misschien wist hij het zelf niet eens.

Deze man en enkele familieleden reisden en logeerden één nacht in een motel. Daar ontdekte hij in het nachtkastlade een boek met de titel “De Heilige Bijbel”. Zeker, in zijn kerk werd de Bijbel elke week tijdens hun normale erediensten gelezen of geciteerd. Hoewel deze man Engels behoorlijk goed begreep, had zijn kerk als beleid dat men niet te werelds of te modern wilde zijn door uit een Engelse Bijbel te lezen, dus zij bleven hun inspanningen voortzetten om Gods Woord in de oorspronkelijke taal van hun volk te onderwijzen.

Het probleem was dat deze man, op de een of andere manier, nooit een begrip van die taal had ontwikkeld, zodat hij nooit de waarheid van Gods Woord had gehoord. Alles wat hij hoorde was wat 1 Korinthiërs hoofdstuk 14 noemt tongen (talen) en omdat hij de taal niet begreep en er geen uitleg werd gegeven, kon hij niet opgebouwd worden. Het doel van dit verhaal is niet om schuld te zoeken of de schuld te leggen, maar om licht te werpen op een duidelijk probleem onder sommige van de eenvoudige mensen. Een probleem waarvoor God zeker veranderingen zou willen zien ten bate van hen die Hem in zulke kringen zoeken.

Met dit in gedachten keren we nu terug naar deze man — een man ijverig in zijn religieuze leven — maar die NOOIT de boodschap van het Evangelie van Jezus Christus had gehoord. Terwijl hij aarzelend deze Engelse Bijbel oppakte, begon hij voorzichtig de boodschap binnen die boekomslagen te lezen. Terwijl hij las, raakte hij meer en meer opgewonden. Hier stonden dingen die hij nog nooit had gehoord — leringen die betekenis gaven aan zijn vele vragen en de leegte die hij in zijn ziel voelde. Hij raakte zo verdiept dat hij zich bijna niet los kon rukken om tijd voor slaap toe te staan. Na een korte nacht gingen ze verder met hun reis.

Hun zaken afgehandeld keerden zij huiswaarts, maar het leven zou voor die man nooit meer hetzelfde zijn. Er was iets diep in zijn ziel ontwaakt. Vragen waren beantwoord. Verlangens waren vervuld. Vrede begon neer te dalen op zijn onrustige hart. Eindelijk had hij het antwoord gevonden, maar zijn leestijd was zo kort geweest. Zeker was er meer te leren, veel meer. Dus, voordat er te veel tijd verstreek, plande hij opnieuw een reis om weg te zijn uit zijn lokale omgeving en opnieuw een reden te hebben om een nacht in een motel te doorbrengen met een Bijbel in het nachtkastlade. Hij keek reikhalzend uit naar nog een nacht alleen met God en Zijn Woord. Na een tweede slapeloze nacht waarin hij de leringen van de Schriften verslond, begon hij anderen te zoeken die begrepen en praktiseerden wat de Bijbel zei. Hij verlangde te gemeenschap te hebben en te leren van hen die Gods Woord begrepen en naar hun prediking leefden.

Terwijl deze man ernaar heeft gestreefd zijn weg te vinden door dit verwarrende doolhof van religieuze eigenaardigheden, kocht hij uiteindelijk een Duits/Engelse Bijbel. Hij voelde zich gedreven in zijn voortgezette zoektocht naar de Waarheid, maar hij was bang dat zijn lokale kerkleiders hem zouden ontdekken. Hij wilde in zijn lokale kerk blijven, maar zijn geweten eiste dat hij zijn zoektocht moest voortzetten. Om de een of andere reden geloofde hij dat zijn plaatselijke kerkleiders niet begripvol zouden zijn in zijn zoektocht naar de waarheid en dat hij misschien kerkelijke tucht over zich heen zou krijgen vanwege zijn daden.

Zijn lokale kerk behoort tot de afstammelingen van de wederdopers die vanwege hun geloof werden vervolgd, inclusief hun verlangen om de Schriften in hun moedertaal — Zwitsers of Duits — te begrijpen en te lezen, in plaats van in het Latijn zoals destijds door de kerkelijke leiders werd vereist. En toch is hij hier, zo’n 500 jaar later, in Amerika, mogelijk geconfronteerd met vervolging door zijn eigen kerk die beweert deel uit te maken van de “juiste” kerk van God. Hierin bevinden zijn kerkleiders zich aan de andere kant van de kwestie van vrijheid van godsdienstige eredienst waar hun voorouders voor leden, aangezien zij erop aandringen dat de enige manier om Gods wil te leren is via de officiële taal van de Schrift — Duits. Dit verschilt NIETS van de strijd van de oorspronkelijke wederdopers die werden vervolgd omdat ze de Schriften niet in de officiële taal van hun tijd — Latijn — bestudeerden.

Laten we ons herinneren, ALS kerkleden de leringen van Gods Woord niet begrijpen doordat hun kerkleiders koppig vasthouden aan het feit dat de kerkleden NIET mogen lezen of horen in de taal die zij begrijpen, dan zal de onwetendheid van de gewone man op de dag van het oordeel bij die leiders gelegd worden. Gehoorzaamt hen die over u de leiding hebben, en onderwerpt uzelf; want zij waken over uw zielen, als zij die rekenschap moeten geven… –Hebreeën 13:17. Gehoorzamen hier is alleen in de context van Gods Woord, niet louter volgens de persoonlijke ideeën of grillen van kerkleiders. Want wij allen moeten geopenbaard worden voor de rechterstoel van Christus; opdat ieder ontvange hetgeen in het lichaam gedaan is, naardat hij het gedaan heeft, hetzij goed of kwaad –2 Corintiërs 5:10. Ieder mens zal persoonlijke rekenschap geven naar hetgeen de Bijbel leert, NIET volgens het gedetailleerde dogma van een kerk.

Als ik denk aan de ijverige inspanningen van deze man denk ik aan het Schriftwoord… Toen Jezus het hoorde, verwonderde Hij zich en zei tot hen die Hem volgden: Voorwaar, Ik zeg u: Ik heb zulk groot geloof niet gevonden, neen, niet in Israël –Mattheüs 8:10. Ik merk ook de huidige trends van sommige van onze eenvoudige uitgeverijen op — zij hebben (op geestelijke wijze, natuurlijk) de wereldse gedachte overgenomen dat om boeken en leesmateriaal te verkopen ze opwindende verhalen moeten drukken, verhalen die mensen op het puntje van hun stoel houden — dit alles omdat de christen van vandaag verveeld is geraakt van dat wat oudmodisch lijkt.

Wat een verschil tussen dit verhaal en veel van de hedendaagse wederdoper-afstammelingen. Velen van de hedendaagse conservatieve wederdopers hebben moeite om enthousiast te raken over de Bijbel. Zij zijn te overgestimuleerd door het gebrek aan rust en stilte in hun normale dagelijks leven.

Meestal horen we zulke verhalen uit de jungles van Midden-Amerika, de woestijnen van Afrika of de sloppenwijken van India. Wat mij verbaast is dat dit verhaal zich afspeelt midden onder één van onze eenvoudige groepen conservatieve wederdopers. Laten we God zoeken voor kansen om de waarheid van het Evangelie te delen met degenen binnen onze invloedssfeer. We zouden verrast kunnen zijn hoeveel mensen we dagelijks tegenkomen die even hongerig naar de Waarheid zouden zijn als de man in ons verhaal.

Greetings to one and all in our dear Saviour’s name, Jesus Christ. Another year has passed from the present into the annals of history. Nothing that we have said or done can be recalled and re-lived. Another year is before us. Many are waiting with bated breath, anticipating what this new year will bring forth.

I read somewhere in the news that those on the frontier of technology believe that this year will be a big year for artificial intelligence. One example given was: they are anticipating that this technology will be able to be a part of events such as board meetings with the ability to hear and understand all that is shared by each one present. Then at the end of the meeting, with the push of a button, the artificial intelligence will produce detailed minutes of that meeting with a fair degree of accuracy. Over the last number of years, many of the things that used to be considered science fiction have recently become reality, so, likely, this will become a new reality as well.

What is this world coming to? To the Bible-literate Christian, the end of time certainly seems to be fast approaching. According to the United Nations, the world’s population surpassed 8 billion on November 15, 2022. Many in the world are desperately trying to figure out how to sustain that many people for the long term. Just like the Bible has prophesied, there is an uptick in the number of famines, drought, floods, earthquakes, wars, and rumors of wars, etc. One thing that I find interesting is that even though the world does not want to retain God in their knowledge, insurance companies still refer to certain specific events as “acts of God”.

As Bible-believing Christians how shall we then live? And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet –Matthew 24:6. Let us remember that we should not be troubled. Rather, we should remember that …he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:13. If we, like Peter, take our eyes off of our Lord and start focusing on the stormy conditions around us we will start to sink as well. Remember, it is …the fearful, and unbelieving … [who] shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone… –Revelation 21:8. But, He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son –Revelation 21:7.

In this issue of the magazine, we again have an interesting group of articles for your consideration. Join us as we learn of a somewhat obscure, yet influential leader of the early Anabaptist movement in Switzerland. Let’s honestly evaluate our own hearts as we follow the expository teaching from Habakkuk regarding what it means to have a real faith that is first personal, then corporate. Together we can consider what it really means to enter into the rest of God that is detailed in Hebrews chapter four. The youth can take a look into their emotions as they consider those times when they feel like giving up. The author for our sisters’ article has tackled a very difficult subject—when and how to be submissive as a godly wife. We have another thought-provoking article in the discipleship series. And the doctor has chosen to venture into some uncharted territory with the first of a two-part series on cancer.

A final thought I wish to share, a story in fact… Recently, I heard a first-hand account of a man who was lost before God, how he came to spiritual awakening, and how this started affecting his life. This story caused me to stop and consider where I am as a Christian. Is my relationship with my Lord vibrant? How strong is my commitment towards God and His Word? Is my love for my Lord and Saviour still as real and as strong as it was when I first had my awakening and was converted? I’m sure there are more questions that we could ask ourselves in light of this real-life story. I’ll let you as a reader start compiling your own list. Now for the story…

This man is living somewhere within the United States of America. He is a married man with a young family. He is part of a certain religious group within the plain people—those of Anabaptist heritage. Throughout his lifetime he had endeavored to live his life according to the mandates set forth by the leaders of his local church. Yet, for some reason, he had not been finding answers to his personal need, whatever that was—perhaps even he didn’t know.

This man and some of his family were traveling and ended up lodging overnight in a motel. There, in the nightstand drawer he discovered a book titled “The Holy Bible”. Sure, in his church the Bible was read or quoted each week during their normal worship services. Although this man understood English quite well, his church had a policy that they did not want to be too worldly or too modern by reading from an English Bible so they continued their efforts of teaching God’s Word using the original language of their people.

The problem was that this man, somehow, never developed an understanding of that language, thus he never heard the truth of God’s Word. All that he heard was what 1 Corinthians chapter 14 refers to as tongues (languages) and since he didn’t understand the language and since there was no interpretation given, he was not able to be edified. The purpose of this story is not to find fault or to place blame, but rather to bring light to an obvious problem among some of the plain people. A problem for which God would surely desire to see changes made for the betterment of those seeking Him in such settings.

With this in mind, we now come back to this man—a man zealous in his religious life—yet having NEVER heard the message of the Gospel of Jesus Christ. As he hesitantly picked up this English Bible he cautiously started to read the message contained within those book covers. As he read, he became more and more excited. Here were things that he had never heard before—teachings that brought sense to his many questions and the emptiness that he felt within his soul. He was so engrossed that he almost couldn’t pull himself away to allow time for sleep. After a short night, they went on with their travels.

Completing their business they returned home, but life would never be the same for that man. Something had been awakened deep within his soul. Questions had been answered. Longings had been met. Peace had begun to settle over his troubled heart. At long last, he had found the answer, but his time of reading had been so short. Surely there was more to learn, much more. So, before too much time had elapsed, he once more scheduled a trip to get away from his local area and to once more provide a reason to spend another night in a motel with a Bible in the nightstand drawer. He eagerly anticipated another night alone with God and His Word. His local church is a part of the descendants of the Anabaptists who were persecuted for their faith, including their desire to understand, and read the Scriptures in their native tongue—Swiss or German, instead of Latin as was required by the church leaders of their day. Yet here he is, some 500 years later, in America, possibly facing persecution from his own church which claims to be a part of the “right” church of God. Herein, his church leaders are finding themselves on the opposite side of the issue of freedom of religious worship that their forefathers suffered for, since they are insisting that the only way to learn of God’s will is through the official language of Scripture—German. This is NO different than the struggle of the original Anabaptists who were persecuted for not studying the Scriptures in the official language of their day—Latin.

Let’s remember, IF church members do not understand the teachings of God’s Word due to their church leaders’ stubborn insistence that the church members are NOT allowed to read or hear the Scriptures in the language that they understand, then the ignorance of the common man WILL be laid at the feet of those leaders come judgment day. Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account… –Hebrews 13:17. Obey here is only in the context of God’s Word, not just according to church leaders’ personal ideas or whims. For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad –2 Corinthians 5:10. Every person will receive personal judgment based on what the Bible teaches NOT according to a church’s detailed dogma.

When I think of the zealous efforts of this man I think of the verse of Scripture… When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel –Matthew 8:10. I also observe the current trends of some of our plain publishing houses—they have borrowed from the world’s idea (in a spiritual way, of course) that to sell books and reading material they need to print exhilarating stories, ones that keep people on the edge of their seats—all this because today’s Christian has become bored with that which seems old-fashioned.

What a difference between this story and many of today’s Anabaptist descendants. Many of today’s conservative Anabaptist people have a difficult time getting excited about the Bible. They are too over-stimulated by the lack of rest and quiet in their normal daily lives.

Usually, we hear of stories like this from the jungles of Central America, the deserts of Africa, or the slums of India. What I am amazed about is that this story takes place right in the midst of one of our plain groups of conservative Anabaptists. Let’s seek God for opportunities to share the truth of the Gospel message with those within the sphere of our influence. We might be surprised how many people we rub shoulders with during our daily lives who would be just as hungry for the Truth as the man in our story.
